name: A Bengal Currie
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one tablespoonful (or two if required very hot) of currie powder
steps: Wash and cut up into pieces, about an inch square, two pounds or rather less of good mutton
Put the pieces of meat into a stewpan
Add an onion previously fried in butter, and a clove of garlic, chopped fine
Sprinkle over the meat one tablespoonful (or two if the currie is required to be very hot) of currie powder
Brown two ounces of butter in a frying-pan, and pour it over the meat
Add sufficient good gravy to cover it
Let it stew gently for two hours
Add some tamarind juice, or lemon to give the required acid
Thicken the gravy and serve

name: A Madras Currie
author: Source author unknown
steps: Skin a fowl and cut it up into small joints
Fry it in butter a light brown
Put it into a saucepan with two tablespoonfuls of currie powder, the juice of a lemon, half a cocoa nut finely grated, a teaspoonful of salt, a little fried onion, and a clove of garlic
Let it simmer slowly for three hours, adding a thickening of butter and flour, just before it is sufficiently cooked

name: A Nice Way to Serve Crabs
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Boil the crabs five minutes
Pick and chop them, adding all the ingredients
Shape in forms of mutton chops, and roll in the beaten egg
Stick in a claw
Put in a frying pan three tablespoons of lard
When boiling, put in the crabs to brown, which they will do in three minutes
Serve in a round dish with claws in the center

name: A Portugal Cake
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Take half-a-pound of the best flour, put it before the fire to dry for half an hour.
Sift it through a sieve, put it aside.
Melt 1/2 lb. of butter to oil.
Put 3/4 lb. of castor sugar in a skillet or pan that is round at the bottom.
Break over the sugar 9 fresh eggs.
Stir the eggs and sugar till it froths.
Put in the butter by degrees while another person stirs the eggs and sugar.
When the butter is well worked in, then put the flour in the same way by spoonfuls.
When it is well worked in, grease your tin and sift a little fine sugar in the tin.
Put it in a slow oven.
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: A Relish
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take of cayenne, ground ginger, black pepper, cinnamon and mace each one quarter of an ounce
of white pepper and grated nutmegs one ounce, and half a teaspoonful of ground cloves
mix well and put into a bottle
it will be found a great addition to soups and gravies, and mixed with a little vinegar to form a paste will make a delicious sauce for cold meat, steaks, &c.

name: Aadi Khyghana
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: about two ounces of fresh butter
steps: Break four or five eggs in a basin
Add a little salt and pepper
Beat them well up with a fork
Put into a very clean frying-pan about two ounces of fresh butter
Put it on the fire
When hot, pour in the eggs
Keep stirring till all is nicely set
Let it slip to the edge of the pan, laying hold by the handle and raising it slantwise, which will give an elongated shape to the omelette
Turn in the edges and let it set a moment
Turn it over on to a dish
Serve

name: Aadi Pilaw
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound of the best rice, well washed
half a pound of fresh butter
steps: Pour two pints of water in a saucepan, and put it on the fire
When boiling, throw in a pound of the best rice, well washed, and sufficient salt, and boil it until the whole of the liquid is absorbed
Put in a saucepan half a pound of fresh butter, and set it on the fire until it boils
Pour it all at once over the rice, put the cover over the pan, wrap a wet cloth round it, to prevent the steam from escaping, and keep it on the hob for half an hour
Take the lid off and stir it once round with a fork
Dish up in the shape of a dome, and serve hot

name: Aadi Shier ub
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Put three pounds of loaf sugar in a clean stewpan, with two pints of cold water
Whip up the white of an egg, and add it to the sugar
Stir well with a wooden spoon, and set it to boil until it becomes a little thickish
Skim it well
Just before you take it off, add a few drops of the essence of orange-flower, or any other essence you choose
Pass it through a clean cloth
When cold, bottle and cork it up until wanted

name: Abgeruehrter Kugelhopf
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: one-half ounce of yeast or one cake compressed yeast
a scant cup of powdered sugar
one-half cup of cleaned and seeded dark raisins
steps: Soak one-half ounce of yeast or one cake compressed yeast in a very little lukewarm milk; add a pinch of salt and one tablespoon of sugar, stir it up smooth and set back of the stove to rise
In the meantime rub a scant cup of butter and a scant cup of powdered sugar to a cream, add gradually the yolks of four eggs, one at a time and add also the grated peel of a lemon
Sift two cups of flour into a bowl, make a depression in the centre, pour in the yeast, one cup of lukewarm milk, and make a light batter of this
Add the creamed butter and eggs and stir until it forms blisters and leaves the bowl clean

Take one-half cup of cleaned and seeded dark raisins and cut up some citron very fine. Dredge flour over them before adding, and if necessary, add more flour to the dough, which should be of the consistency of cup cake batter
Last add the stiffly-beaten whites of the eggs
Place in a well-greased long or round pan with tube in centre; let rise until double in bulk, and bake in moderate oven until browned and thoroughly done

name: Achar of Amlaki
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
steps: Make a few deep cuts on each of some ripe and fresh amlaki fruits and remove the seeds if you can
Boil them in plenty of water till soft
Drain out the water and wash with fresh cold water
Drop them in a boiling syrup of sugar and boil for 20 or 25 minutes
Make a paste of powders of chillies, pepper, aniseed, cardamom seeds, pasted or powdered ginger in adequate quantities with little mustard oil
Smear the boiled fruits with it and preserve in an airtight jar

name: Alcachofas Fritas (Fried Artichokes)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Choose tender artichokes and use only the hearts, cutting them in four pieces
Fry diced bacon and finely sliced bacon, and there add the artichokes
They are also fried in oil, coating them first in a batter made of egg yolks with a bit of sugar

name: Aletria Caseira (Homemade Aletria)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Make a dough with wheat flour, five eggs and a little salt
Beat well until it shows air bubbles when cut
Unroll the dough on a cloth and when well extended and thin, roll it up on itself
Cut the roll into very fine strips

name: Alfajor de Miel Virgen (Sweet Pastry with Virgin Honey)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Make a syrup with sugar and virgin honey
Cook until it reaches the soft candy stage, which is when threads form when stretched between the fingers
Add ground cinnamon, clove, pepper and crushed biscuit that can absorb the syrup
Make the alfajores between wafers or in paper cones, decorating as appropriate
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Alones de Guajolote á las Yerbas (Turkey Wings with Herbs)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Remove the bones from the wings
After plucking and cleaning, blanch lightly in boiling water
Cover with small pieces of bacon, passed through completely
Cook like pipila in adobo, covering with paper well soaked in butter
Once well cooked, place in a sauce or stew of herbs

name: Amati Tamana (Sweet and Sour Cabbage)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Cut a small, hard cabbage very fine.
Place in frying pan one tablespoonful of goma oil, and when it is boiling hot throw in the shredded cabbage.
Sprinkle with salt, and fry, stirring constantly to keep it from burning.
Add one tablespoonful of sugar, the same quantity of vinegar, and a little piece of lemon or orange peel, shaved very fine.
Cover tight, and let all simmer for twenty minutes.
Finally add half a teaspoon of goma seeds.
Serve hot.

name: An Apricot Anlauf
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Mash 12 or 14 ripe apricots through a sieve
Pound the kernels quite fine
Make a thick paste with 1/2 pint of milk and as much flour as it will take up
When cold put it in a basin
Dissolve in the milk 2 oz. of butter
Stir the apricots up with this paste
Mix with yolks of 6 eggs and 1 lb. of powdered sugar
Work this in with the paste and apricots
Beat the whites to a snow and stir in lightly
Grease the shape and put it in
Place in a middling oven
When it rises and is a good colour it is done
About 1/2 of an hour before you send it up sprinkle sugar over it
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Another Way
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one pound and a quarter of treacle
three-quarters of a pound of butter (melted)
a small quantity of cayenne pepper
steps: Mix all together and roll out to about the thickness of half an inch, or not quite so much
Cut into cakes, and bake in a moderate oven

name: Anta Estufada (Stewed Tapir)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put a tapir loin in a pan lined with slices of pork fat, with one cup of wine, one glass of vinegar, two tablespoons of sugar, two cut onions, one clove of garlic, salt, pepper and two cloves
Leave the meat in these seasonings for six hours, turning from time to time
Seal the lid, put the pan on the fire and boil for two to three hours; serve with the strained sauce without fat

name: Ante de Coco (Coconut Paste Cake)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Remove the brown skin from coconut
Grate or grind it
Add to syrup at medium point
Preserve it
Add raisins, almonds and aromatics
Layer this mixture and sponge cake
Top with pastille and sesame seeds

name: Ante de Mamey (Mamey Paste Dessert)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Grind the mamey and add it to the syrup at medium point for six boilings
Add white wine, spices, raisins, almonds, and sesame seeds
Pour over sponge cake

name: Apple Float
author: Source author unknown
steps: Beat the whites of eggs until very light
Add powdered sugar and beat until fine and dry
Into this grate two apples, beating carefully until the meringue will hold no more apples
Spread this over a soft custard or whipped cream
Serve at once

name: Apple Pie, No. 2
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: five large apples or six small ones
steps: Put in saucepan sugar and water and let it boil a few minutes
Lay in apples which have previously been peeled and quartered
Cover with a lid and steam until tender but not broken
Line pie-plate with rich milchig pastry
Lay on the apples
Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon and bits of butter
Drop a few drops of syrup over all
Bake

name: Apple Tarts
author: Source author unknown
steps: Prepare the Pie Paste (see recipe), and line six tart molds with it.
Peel and core the apples and cut into quarters, and put into a saucepan with a pint of cold water.
Let them cook on a hot stove for ten minutes.
Then remove and drain, and let cool for half an hour.

Then cut the quarters into three slices each; line the bottom of the molds with the marmalade divided evenly; arrange the sliced apples nicely over the marmalade, and dredge nicely with two ounces of powdered sugar.
Set in a baking dish and bake for twenty minutes, or a half hour if necessary.

name: Arara, Papagaio, etc., Assados no Forno (Macaw, Parrot, etc. Roasted in the Oven)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Stuff the bird with its giblets, four cooked and chopped eggs, salt, pepper, and one chopped onion.
Sew the opening and sauté the bird in three spoonfuls of fat, turning it to brown on all sides.
Cover the pan and let it finish roasting either in the oven or over coals.
When cooked, serve with some spicy sauce or salad.

name: Arroz con Leche (Rice with Milk)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one quarter pound of refined sugar
sugar and cinnamon powder for serving
steps: Heat the milk in a new pot with a small piece of cinnamon and lemon or orange peels tied with strong thread for removal
When the milk begins to boil, add the rice that has been half-cooked with water and salt and drained
Stir constantly with one hand without stopping to prevent the milk from curdling
Serve with sugar and ground cinnamon

name: Aspic Jelly
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: bacon bone or slice or two of ham or bacon
steps: Put into a stew-pan an ox-foot cleaned and cut up with a bacon bone or a slice or two of ham or bacon
Add any scraps of raw meat such as cutlet trimmings or a young fowl cut up as for fricassee with a few mixed vegetables as for soup
Add a cup of cold water and cover the pan
Set it on the fire, shaking it occasionally
When the pieces of meat begin to take colour, add a little more water
In about half an hour, pour in enough water to cover the contents of the pan completely
Put in a tea-spoonful of caramel and let the vessel simmer for three hours very gently
When ready, strain the liquor off into a bowl and let it get cool
Skim it carefully and add a tea-spoonful of sugar and table-spoonful of tarragon vinegar
Clarify it and strain it finally through a clean cloth
This produces a clear, amber-coloured liquid which will set of its own accord without isinglass if put in the ice-box

name: Assude Helwdssi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound of the best white honey
half a pound of fresh butter
steps: Put in a clean stewpan a pound of wheat-starch, a pint of water, a pound of the best white honey, and half a pound of fresh butter, melted
Put it on the fire and commence stirring until the butter begins to appear on the surface of the mixture
Keep stirring from the bottom of the pan and pressing it with the back of the spoon for a few minutes longer
Dish up like a dome and serve

name: Aunt Lizzie's Spice Cake
author: Source author unknown
steps: Combine ingredients
Bake

name: Azas de Peru Fritas (Fried Turkey Wings)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take the turkey wings and neck and cook in water with salt, parsley, and onion leaves
When cooked, remove the bones and cut the meat into small pieces
Beat with six eggs
Fry in lard
When fried, serve

name: Bacalao en Ajo Blanco sin Chile (Cod in White Garlic Sauce without Chile)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Toast a piece of bread in the fire until half burnt, and grind it with garlic browned in lard and a little pepper.
Burn oil in a pan and brown there some chopped garlic cloves, add the ground bread with everything else, and the already-cooked cod, cut into slices.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Bachelor's Loaf
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
ingredientsText: 1 pint of boiling hot new milk
steps: Pour boiling hot new milk on the sifted cornmeal
Stir well together
Beat the whites and yolks of eggs separately
Reserve the whites for the last ingredient added
Add salt and lard
Beat the whole quite light
Grease the pan and pour in the mixture
Bake 1 hour

name: Badinjan Dolmássi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: one or two pounds of raw mutton
juice of one or two lemons
steps: Procure six or seven egg-plants and remove the stalks
Cut off the tops as large as a two-shilling piece
Take out the insides without making a hole at the other end and throw them in salt water for ten or fifteen minutes
Mince fine one or two pounds of raw mutton
Add a handful of well-washed rice, two onions chopped very fine, sufficient salt and pepper, and mix them together with your hands
Stuff the egg-plants with these ingredients and cover them with the tops contrariwise
Beat up five or six eggs in a basin and dip the egg-plants in them
Fry them in hot fresh butter
Prick them here and there with a fork and place them in a stewpan, the bottom of which you have previously covered with rib-bones of mutton
Cover them either with broth or water and add the juice of one or two lemons
Set it on a charcoal fire and let it simmer till the liquor is nearly absorbed or until it forms a nice thick gravy at the bottom

Dish them up carefully and serve hot, or beat up two or three eggs with the gravy and the juice of half a lemon in a saucepan, place it on a very slow fire and keep stirring, and when it begins to thicken, pour over the egg-plants and serve

name: Bagre con Pan Rallado (Catfish with Breadcrumbs)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: After washing the catfish well and cutting it into portions, roll it in breadcrumbs.
Grind pepper, clove, thyme and marjoram; chop onion and parsley very finely, and place a casserole greased with lard with paper on the bottom.

Form a layer of catfish portions, sprinkle with chopped onion and parsley, another of fish rolled in breadcrumbs with spices on top, and thus continue multiplying the layers, the last one being onion and parsley.
Place at two fires, and when it is cooked, sprinkle it with vinegar, adding plenty of oil and decorating it with olives and pickled chili peppers.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Bagre en Xitomate con Chile Verde (Catfish in Tomato with Green Chile)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: After frying the catfish portions, chop onion, green chile, garlic, and very ripe tomato very fine
Fry it and add water, a splash of vinegar, a lump of sugar, a little clove, cinnamon, and pepper powder
Cook until the sauce is very thick
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Bak Toy Gun (Chinese Soup of White Vegetables)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one half pound of white mushrooms
one quarter pound of bean sprouts
three pints of boiling, salted water
steps: Have ready three pints of boiling, salted water, with the two tablespoonfuls of syou in it
Add all vegetables (which have been previously washed in cold water, and cut in small pieces) except the mushrooms and celery
Boil for fifteen minutes, then add the mushrooms and celery
Whip up the three eggs in a little cold water, and drop slowly into the boiling soup, stirring the soup as it drops
Remove at once, and serve

name: Baked Apple Dumpling
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Pare and core apples carefully without making holes through
Enclose each in the usual pie paste
Place in a pan and fill apples with nutmeg, butter and sugar
Leave the tops of apples open
Flute with the fingers the top of crust
Bake until golden
Eat with hard sauce

name: Baked Apple Dumplings
author: Lafcadio Hearn
ingredientsText: wine or sugar and butter sauce
steps: Make a nice pie crust, raised with yeast, or not, as you desire
Divide it into six parts, and roll each part thin
Have ready six good-sized tart apples, pared and cored
Fill up the cores with sugar and butter
Close the dough neatly around the apples, and turn that side down in a deep dish
If they are made with raised dough they should stand one hour
If with unleavened paste, sprinkle some sugar over them, also a little grounded cinnamon or other spice
Spread a little batter over each of the dumplings as they go to the oven
Put plenty of spices, nutmegs, cinnamon and mace
Throw a little water in the dish, and bake three-quarters of an hour

name: Baked Bananas
author: Source author unknown
steps: Peel and cut bananas into halves lengthwise
Place slices in a shallow granite pan
Melt the butter and stir in sugar and lime or lemon juice
Pour one-half of this mixture over the bananas
Place the pan in a slow oven and bake twenty minutes
While baking, baste the bananas occasionally with the remainder of the syrup mixture

name: Baked Rice
author: Source author unknown
steps: Mix well rice, cheese in small bits, milk, eggs, butter and salt.
Place in baking dish with cheese and a little butter on top.
Bake half an hour.

name: Baked Squash
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut open the squash; take out the seeds and without paring cut into large pieces.
Place in a moderately hot oven and bake about an hour.
When done, serve the pieces hot, to be eaten with butter like sweet potatoes.

name: Bakers' Bread
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: Flour Sufficient to Make a Smooth Dough
steps: Allow one ounce of Compressed Yeast to one quart of lukewarm water, and mix well in a wooden bread trough.
Then add flour enough to make a nice smooth dough of medium degree, not too stiff, nor yet too soft.
Work it well, and then let it stand for about five hours in a warm place so as to rise well.

When it drops, or begins to fall (you can tell this by watching the sides of the dough), add the same amount of water that was used in making the dough, putting two teaspoonfuls of salt into the water before adding it.

Work this well, and then throw down on the table, cut and mold the dough into loaves of whatever length is desired, and take a smooth stick and press lightly down across the loaf about two inches from the edge.
Put the loaves into the oven without setting in a pan.
Watch carefully, and see that the oven is of the proper temperature.
By following these directions, you will have nice, fresh, sweet New Orleans Bakers' Bread.

name: Banana Pudding
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut cake in thin slices and line a dish with slices
Cover the cake with bananas sliced very thin
Over this pour a cupful of thin, boiled custard
Make another layer of cake, banana and custard
Set away to cool

name: Barbacoa Mexicana (Mexican Barbacoa)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: Chile-garlic sauce or adobo or other sauce
steps: Form a hole three-quarters deep and of competent size for the piece to be cooked
Put stones at the bottom
With dry firewood form a fire in the center so that after two or three hours the hole is well heated
Remove all the fire, leaving the stones
Moisten a new palm petate and place it over the stones
Place the prepared meat on top, either with chile-garlic, or adobo, or another sauce well spread and loaded with salt
Place another petate over the meat, sticks or maguey leaves to cover it and some hot stones so earth does not fall
Cover with another wet petate, a little earth on top, and enough fire over it
After eight or ten hours, remove the meat well cooked
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Bean Cake Omelet Fo Yung Dow Fo
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Beat the eggs with a little salt and oil.
Fry the bean cakes in an oiled pan. Add water and boil for 10 minutes.
Put plenty of oil in the pan, greasing it well all over. Put in the egg. Keep on turning until nearly done. Add the bean cake and cook until done.
Use Chinese ham dice and parsley for garnish.

name: Beef a la Mode
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: four pounds of lard or fat bacon
half a tablespoonful of cinnamon powdered
half a seer or one pound of finely-powdered pepper
four tablespoonfuls of chutnee strained through muslin
claret-glassful of mixed sauces such as Harvey, walnut, Worcestershire, tap, tomato
steps: Corn a round of beef in every particular as directed in recipe No. 123
Twenty-four hours previously to its being cooked lard it as follows with the undermentioned ingredients
Mix the ground pepper, ground hot spices, and strained chutnee with a claret-glassful of mixed sauces
Cut up into long narrow slips the lard or bacon to correspond in thickness with the larding-pin
Lay the slips into the mixture of spices, sauces, etc., for an hour or two before larding the beef
Lard the beef through and through, and as closely as possible
Cook it the next day, either in plain water with half a pint of vinegar and with bay-leaves and peppercorns, or in a preparation of claret or champagne with vinegar, bay-leaves, etc.

name: Beef Kidney with Chinese Mushrooms
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one quarter pound of dried mushrooms
one and one half teaspoonfuls of salt
two tablespoonfuls of chopped fat pork
steps: Soak the kidney for half an hour in cold water with a handful of salt; then cut in small pieces and fry in pork fat.
Wash a quarter of a pound of dried mushrooms in lukewarm water, pull off the stalks, and soak for ten minutes.
Add this to the kidney, with one small chopped onion, one and one quarter teaspoonfuls of salt, and three tablespoonfuls of syou.
Cover tight, and boil very slowly for one hour, adding boiling water if it dries.
Serve with rice.

name: Beef or Mutton Baked with Potatoes
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil some potatoes.
Peel and pound them in a mortar with one or two small onions.
Moisten them with milk and an egg beaten up.
Add a little salt and pepper.
Season slices of beef or mutton chops with salt and pepper, and more onion, if the flavour is approved.

Rub the bottom of a pudding-dish with butter, and put in a layer of the mashed potatoes, which should be as thick as a batter, and then a layer of meat, and so on alternately, till the dish is filled, ending with potatoes.
Bake in an oven for one hour.

name: Beef with Celery, White Beans and Peas
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
ingredientsText: one pint of dried white peas
half a pint of dried white beans
a nice piece of brisket of about eight pounds weight
steps: Soak the peas and beans for twelve hours, or longer if very dry
Put the brisket in a stew-pan with the peas and beans, and three heads of celery cut in small pieces
Add water enough to cover
Season with pepper and salt only
Let it all stew slowly till the meat is extremely tender and the peas and beans quite soft
Add four large lumps of sugar and nearly a tea-cup of vinegar

name: Beefsteak with Oysters
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put oysters with very little of the juice into stew-pan.
When they come to a boil, remove the scum.
Stir in butter mixed with flour.
Let boil one minute until it thickens.
Pour over the steak.
Serve hot.

name: Beignets a la Pignatelli
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: one and a half ounces of butter
four and a half ounces of flour
one ounce of lean cooked ham
steps: Put one pint of water in a stew-pan with one and a half ounces of butter, season with salt and pepper
Boil, and add four and a half ounces of flour and one ounce of grated Parmesan
Stir over the fire for three minutes
Add sufficient eggs to turn the mixture to a smooth paste
Add to the paste one ounce of lean cooked ham finely chopped
When mixed, form the paste into fritters
Fry in plenty of hot fat

name: Beshmi
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
steps: Mix 1 powa of ghee thoroughly with 1 seer of besam of grams and heat
Stir constantly
Add 1 seer of ghee more in 2 or 3 instalments
Add 1 powa of sugar when the besam is fried red
Take down when it is thoroughly mixed up
Mix with 1 tola of powdered pepper
Powdered garam-masalla may also be added if desired
Make balls while the mass is yet warm

name: Bird's Nest Pudding
author: Lafcadio Hearn
steps: Peel and core six mellow apples.
Line a pudding dish with pastry.
Lay the apples in the bottom of the dish, and stick long narrow strips of citron around them.
Stir to a cream a pint of powdered sugar, and half a pint of butter.
Beat separately the yolks and whites of eight eggs.
Mix them with the butter and sugar, season with nutmeg.
Place it on the fire, and stir until it is hot.
Pour it over the apples, and bake immediately.
It can be eaten warm or cold.
It should be covered with a pan when first put into the oven, to prevent the top from browning too soon.

name: Black Angel Cake
author: Source author unknown
steps: While this is warm, stir in first mixture

name: Black Cake
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
ingredientsText: 1 lb. of citron cut into thin slices
steps: Beat the butter and sugar to a cream
Stir in the whipped eggs
Sift in the flour
Add the raisins, currants, nutmegs, cinnamon, cloves, and citron
Mix all well together
Bake in a buttered pan in rather a moderate oven

name: Blackberry Roll
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: A Plain Paste, Not Too Flaky
steps: Make a Plain Paste, which should be rather firm, to prevent the berries from escaping.
Roll this out to about one and a half feet in length, or one foot, according to the size of the family, and the number of guests.
Spread the blackberries, which you will have carefully picked, over this paste.
Carefully roll over and over until the entire paste is taken up.
Sew in a clean piece of white muslin and put into a kettle of boiling water.
Let it boil continuously for at least two hours and a half.
Take out, let it cool slightly, rip the cloth which binds it, and serve immediately with a Hard Sauce or Cream or Brandy Sauce.

name: Boiled and Deviled Cucumbers
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Peel the cucumbers, and place in salted boiling water.
Boil slowly until the cucumbers become transparent.
Drain off all water and serve with a sauce made of one tablespoonful of olive oil and one teaspoonful of vinegar, beaten well with a dash of cayenne and the yolks of two hard-boiled eggs.

name: Boiled Leg of Mutton, Caper Sauce
author: Source author unknown
steps: Rub the leg of mutton well with salt and pepper
Have ready a pot of boiling water, into which you have thrown the herbs, bay leaf, salt and pepper, allowing a teaspoonful each of the two latter ingredients
Put the leg of mutton into the water, being very careful to have it well covered with water, else the meat will blacken
Let it boil gently but steadily, allowing fifteen minutes to every pound of meat
When done, place on a dish and serve with a Caper Sauce
In serving slice nicely and put a few drops of lemon on each slice, and pour over the Caper sauce

name: Boiled Potatoes
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Put potatoes in just water enough to cover them, with the skins on
Boil them constantly till done
Squeeze them in a dry cloth
Send them to the table very hot

name: Boiled Turbot
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: An hour before dinner, put the turbot into boiling water and salt
Rub the juice of a lemon over it
Let it boil fast at first, then draw the fish-kettle to the side
Slit the skin at the back a little to prevent it breaking
If done before wanted, lift the steamer out of the water and put it across the kettle with a cloth to keep it warm
Dish it on a fish napkin garnished with fried smelts, horseradish, and parsley
Serve with caper, anchovy sauce, or sauce No. 33
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Bolinhos de Manteiga (Butter Balls)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: bread the size of two closed hands
steps: Soak bread the size of two closed hands in hot milk
When softened, remove it and knead with three tablespoons of wheat flour, four egg yolks and two egg whites, little salt, half a tablespoon of sugar and one tablespoon of butter
Form small balls with this mixture, boil them in water that is already boiling
Serve with meat broth or egg sauce

name: Boston Brown Bread
author: Source author unknown
steps: Stir all together and steam in fireless three hours and a half, or bake in oven forty minutes.

name: Bouillon
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut vegetables in small pieces and let lie in cold water
Cut meat in cubes with no fat, wash and put on stove
Add to three quarts of cold water with vegetables
Season to taste
Cook ten hours
Strain

name: Braised Loin with Forcemeat
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: gravy made from the loin's own bones and trimmings
scraps of vegetables of all kinds
steps: Bone the loin and introduce a number of slices of bacon under the flap

Fill the inside with a forcemeat made with the meat of the undercut chopped up small, with the kidney (scalded first), and some of the nicest fat, seasoned with herbs, spiced pepper, chopped bacon, a little onion, and any mushroom or truffle parings
Bind the salpicon with four eggs, and spread it thickly over the inside of the boned loin
Roll the joint up, and tie it firmly into shape, do not skewer it
Braise the loin in a gravy made from its own bones and trimmings, with a glass of Madeira, a clove of garlic, and scraps of vegetables of all kinds arranged round it
When done and nicely browned, lift up the loin and remove the string
Dish it on a layer of boiled maccaroni
Strain off the gravy, throw away the garlic, and pass all the vegetables through the sieve
Thicken the gravy, add the vegetable pulp, and when thoroughly incorporated, pour it round the loin and serve

name: Bread Muffins
author: Source author unknown
steps: Soak the stale bread crumbs in the milk for a half hour.
Beat the yolks of the eggs till very light, and the whites to a stiff froth.
Add a teaspoonful of salt to the bread, and then pour in the melted butter, and mix thoroughly.
Add the flour, into which you will have sifted the baking powder, and beat well.
Lastly, add the whites of the eggs, and put the muffins into the muffin rings or gem pans, and bake for about a half hour in a quick oven.

name: Breast of Mutton with French Beans
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Prepare the breast just as you did for the peas, with the stuffing
Put it in a stewpan with sliced onion, salt, and pepper
Wash and cut the French beans
Put them on top of the mutton with 1/2 pint of water
When done, rub in a basin one spoonful of flour, one of moist sugar, two of vinegar, and browning to colour
Mind that you take off all the fat before you put the sauce in
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Brisket Stewed
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
ingredientsText: about six or seven pounds of brisket of beef
steps: Take about six or seven pounds of brisket of beef
Place it in a stewpan with only enough water to cover it
Season with a little spice tied in a bag
When the meat is tender and the spices sufficiently extracted to make the gravy rich and strong, part of it must be removed to another saucepan
Have ready a variety of vegetables cut into small shapes, such as turnips, carrots, mushrooms, cauliflowers, or whatever may be in season
Stew them gently till tender in the gravy
Glaze the meat and pour the gravy in the dish
Arrange the vegetables round

name: Brittle Pork
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: 3 pounds pork cut into pieces 3/8 inch by 1 3/8 inches by 3/8 inch
A few pieces of Octogon spicery
steps: Boil the pork and spicery in plain water for 10 minutes. Let cool.
Break the egg. Mix with the cornstarch. Then mix with the pork.
Fry in boiling oil until it gets red.
Put the fried pork into cold water and change water several times until no oil floats on the surface.
Dry the pork and place in a bowl.
Add the Fun Wine, and steam for 2 hours.

name: Broiled Woodcock on Toast
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: Parsley Sprigs and Sliced Lemon to Garnish
steps: Prepare the birds by hand picking.
Singe and wipe well.
Rub the bird well with salt and pepper, and then with melted butter.
Tie a strip of very finely-sliced bacon around the body of the bird, joining with a skewer.
Place on a broiler over a slow fire and let it cook for ten, fifteen, twenty, or even thirty minutes, according to the size of the bird.
Turn frequently so that it may cook well without burning.
When done take off the broiler.
Have ready buttered French toasts and place the birds upon them, allowing a slice of toast for each bird.
Trim away the rough edges of the toast.
Pour over the bird a little of the juice that has run from it in broiling, and let it soak down into the toast.
Pour over a little melted butter and chopped parsley, and lemon juice, if you like.
Garnish with sliced lemon and parsley sprigs, and bring to the table hot.

name: Browned Potatoes with Roast
author: Source author unknown
steps: Peel, cook and mash the required amount.
Add while hot, salt, pepper and a very little chopped onion.
Form into small balls.
Dredge with flour.
Place around roast and bake about twenty minutes before serving.

name: Budín Inglés (English Pudding)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: two pounds beef marrow or two pounds beef kidney fat
one and a half pounds raisins
steps: Take two pounds of beef marrow, or if unavailable, two pounds of beef kidney fat.
Remove the skin and tendons, cut into small pieces and place in a large bowl.
Remove the pits from one and a half pounds of raisins and mix with the marrow or fat.

Add three pounds of bread crumbs passed through a sieve; one glass of Málaga wine, two small glasses of Cognac brandy, the zest of half a lemon chopped very fine, a handful of candied citron cut into small pieces, a handful of flour, sufficient salt, and eight whole eggs.
Moisten everything with milk, knead with the hands so it mixes well, and form a somewhat liquid paste.
Place in a capable pot to cook.

name: Buñuelos de Maíz (Corn Fritters - Second Recipe)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Wash niztamal well, grind, strain, and let settle
To one cup of settled corn add one and a half cups of milk, eight egg yolks, sugar to taste and a pinch of cinnamon
Mix well and cook until it reaches the right consistency, then pour into a platter to cool
Clarify two pounds of sugar, beat four eggs as for chiles and cut the dough into quarter portions
Add the egg, a pinch of flour, fry in butter like fried pastries, and place in syrup to boil

name: Buñuelos Trasparentes (Transparent Fritters)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: A piece of leavening the size of an egg
steps: Mix one pound flour with fifteen yolks, three whites, half pound ground aged cheese, a piece of leavening, one cup anise water, salt, and enough melted lard so the dough is not very thick
Beat everything well
With a small spoon, fry spoonfuls in lard until golden
Remove and when cool, boil in syrup until they become transparent
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Cabeça de Porco (Pork Head)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Stuff a pork head with pieces of fresh pork meat after carefully removing all the bones
Season with aromatic herbs, nutmeg, clove, pepper, salt, onions, and chopped chives
Place everything in a vessel and leave for eight to ten days
Remove the head from the vessel and let it drain
Sew up the openings where the bones were removed and tie with string so it maintains its shape during cooking
Wrap it in white cloth tied at both ends
Place it in a frying pan with the head bones, salt pork, carrots, onions, six to eight bay leaves, sprigs of chives, clove, a little salt, and some pieces of pork or other meat
Moisten everything with meat broth
Cook over low heat for ten hours
Remove the head and squeeze it gently to release the liquid it contains, being careful not to lose its shape
Trim any protruding points and serve cold

name: Cajetas de Camote, Leche y Chirimoya (Sweet Potato, Milk and Custard Apple Candy)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: One pound of clean sweet potato
One pound of sugar in powder
One pound of clean, pitted and ground custard apple
steps: Make clarified syrup without lemon with one pound of sugar
When it reaches breaking point, set aside and add one pound of clean sweet potato mixed with one pound of powdered sugar, dissolved in two quartillos of milk, beating everything
Return to the fire and once it has boiled and is near cajeta point, add one pound of clean, pitted and ground custard apple and one pound of sugar, letting it boil until completely cooked
Custard apple may be omitted and the candy will still be good, and grated coconut may also be added when the syrup is put on
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Calves Brains Brown Butter Sauce
author: Source author unknown
steps: Prepare the brains as mentioned above by boiling
Place in a saucepan with a tablespoonful of butter
Cut up a tiny onion and add also a sprig of thyme, bay leaf and parsley, all minced very fine
Add to the butter
Add the brains cut in slices a half inch thick
Season again to taste
Fry for five minutes and serve with a Sauce aux Beurre Noir

name: Capirotada de Nabos (Capirotada with Turnips)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Cook turnips in salted water with garlic.
Make the sauce with broth poured over a mixture of ground garlic with cooked and ground chickpeas.
Layer in this order: bread toasts, turnips, slices of cooked ham, and cooked whole chickpeas.
Do not use cheese.
When sufficiently thickened, cover with breadcrumbs, add salt, pepper and burnt butter on top.
Place a hot griddle on top to brown it.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Capão Recheado com Carapicús (Capon Stuffed with Carapicús)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Make a stuffing of one handful of carapicús, half pound of ham, one quarter of bacon, the capon's giblets, one onion, salt, parsley, pepper and four cooked eggs
Cook everything together with one glass of wine, stirring so it does not stick
When cooked, fill the capon's cavity and crop, lifting the skin between the neck and breast for this purpose
Place it in the oven in a pan over bacon slices, and bring to the table

name: Capón Cocido (Boiled Capon)
author: Source author unknown
steps: After preparing, sprinkle with lemon juice
Cover with bacon slices and cook over low heat with onions, garlic, chopped bacon, and the capon's own neck
Moisten with broth and serve

name: Caramelo Común (Common Caramel)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Make a syrup from very white sugar and clarify it with lemon
Let it boil without stirring or inserting a spoon until it reaches the hard-crack stage when a drop is placed in cold water
Oil a metate with sweet almond oil and pour the syrup carefully with a silver spoon so it does not granulate
Cut the caramels and wrap them in powdered sugar
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Carne de Carneiro Refogada com Palmitos (Braised Mutton with Palm Hearts)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: four pounds of mutton meat, chopped
palm hearts cooked in water and salt
steps: Take four pounds of mutton meat, chop it well, removing nerves and skins that appear
Season with salt, parsley, celery, onion and pepper
Braise in a little melted butter and add a bowl of meat broth or water
Let it boil over coals until the broth almost dries out
Add palm hearts cooked in water and salt over which place the braised mutton with the broth
Cover everything with grated cheese and put in the oven until it takes on a golden color, then serve

name: Carne de Carneiro Refogada em Vinho com Limão (Braised Mutton in Wine with Lemon)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut the meat into pieces and scald them in hot water
Braise them in a little butter and one spoonful of wheat flour until they are browned
Add one glass of white wine, some bay leaves, onions, lemon juice, sugar and cooked raisins

name: Carne de Puerco en Aceite (Pork in Oil)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take pork loin and slice as for beefsteak.
Roll in salt and pepper.
Place in a pot and cover with oil.
Add all spices, apply very low heat.
When cooked, remove and let cool.
Place in glass jars, cover with the same oil in which it cooked, and seal.

name: Carne de Vacca Enrolada (Rolled Beef)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take the beef, cut it into thin and long slices and sprinkle over them salt, a little saltpeter and ground clove.
Cover them with equal slices of fresh bacon with another layer of the same seasonings.
Roll these two slices then, the beef should be on the outside.
Tie these rolls with twine and after two hours boil them in water.
To put this meat on the table, after it cools cut it into transverse slices and serve with a cold sauce also.

name: Carrack
author: Source author unknown
steps: Chop eight pickled walnuts and one head of garlic, put these into a large jar
add walnut vinegar, soy, and mushroom catsup, of each half a tumblerful, a tablespoonful of Harvey sauce, and one quart of vinegar
put the jar in a dry place, and shake it every day for a month
a few spoonfuls of mango pickle is a great improvement

name: Carrot Soup
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
ingredientsText: a good stock, about two quarts
a little lemon juice or vinegar
steps: Take a dozen carrots scraped clean and rasp them, but do not use the core
Take two heads of celery and two onions thinly sliced
Season to taste
Pour over a good stock, say about two quarts
Boil it
Pass it through a sieve
Return it to the saucepan
Boil it up and squeeze in a little lemon juice or add a little vinegar

name: Carrots and Peas
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: salt, pepper and sugar to taste
two tablespoons of fat or butter
one-half cup of milk or soup stock
steps: Wash, scrape and cut one pint of carrots in small cubes
Cook until tender
Drain and reserve one-half cup of carrot water
Mix carrots well with one pint cooked green peas
Sprinkle with two tablespoons of flour, salt, pepper and sugar to taste
Add two tablespoons of fat or butter, one-half cup of milk or soup stock and carrot water
Boil a little longer and serve

name: Cauliflower Au Gratin Without Cheese
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: hot melted butter or salad oil
steps: Arrange your pieces of cauliflower as before explained
Strew over them some fine stale bread-crumbs, with some olives, a few capers, and an anchovy chopped up small
Pour over this a cupful of hot melted butter
Bake for ten minutes
Serve

name: Cayenne Vinegar
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: half an ounce of Cayenne pepper
a pint of white wine vinegar
steps: Put half an ounce of Cayenne pepper into a bottle with a pint of white wine vinegar, cork it tightly, and shake it well for a few days
it will be soon ready for use

name: Cebolas Cozidas (Cooked Onions)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: two to three spoons of fresh butter
steps: Remove the skins from one or two dozen onions and put them in a pan with two or three spoons of fresh butter
Add half a bottle of water, salt and pepper
Let it boil for five minutes over a lively fire, then put the pan over coals until the broth is reduced
Remove the onions, put them on a plate and add to the sauce one spoon of good vinegar and one cup of wine
After boiling a little, pour this sauce over the onions and serve

name: Celery as Entremets
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: trim the heads neatly and cut short, say five or six inches in length
split lengthwise in two or four pieces according to the thickness of the head
plunge the pieces into fast boiling water
as soon as tender, drain, turn out upon a hot silver dish
serve like asparagus with a pat of butter melting over them
send a piping hot Dutch sauce round in a boat

name: Celery Mayonnaise
author: Source author unknown
steps: Chop the celery, or rather cut fine, as indicated in the above recipe
Mix the Mayonnaise with it
Garnish nicely with celery tips and serve

name: Chaghli Turshussu
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: unripe fruit such as peaches, nectarines, almonds, apricots, cherries, apples, plums, pears
steps: Gather any unripe fruit that may have fallen from the trees, such as peaches, nectarines, almonds, apricots, cherries, apples, plums, pears
Mix all together
Place them in bottles or in a stone jar
Cover them with very strong wine vinegar
Tie up the mouths of the bottles with a piece of leather
Let them remain for thirty or forty days before using

name: Chalupas de Morcón (Morcon Chalupas)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Cook the morcones well and fry them
Add plenty of chopped onion and sliced green chiles
Fill the chalupa with this mixture
Add the corresponding salt
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Chatni of Potatoes
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
steps: Mix 1 chhatak of seedless ripe tamarind thoroughly with 1 powa of water and throw away the refuse
Peel and cut some potatoes in round and thin slices
Fry 2 or 3 broken chillies, a pinch of mustards and another of panch-foron in 1 chhatak of mustard oil
Fry 1 powa of the slices of potatoes in it
When the slices are half browned add the tamarind water and a generous pinch of salt
Take down when the soup is thick after mixing with a little sugar

name: Checker-Board Eggs
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Cut the ham and secondary vegetables into threads 1½ inches long. Fry in an oiled pan. Mix well. Add enough primary soup to cover. Cook until done. Salt to suit the taste.
Beat the eggs well with oil and salt. Put them into a hot pan and let them run all over the pan evenly. Turn over.
Put this egg layer on a dish. Cover one-half of the layer with the fried ham, bamboo shoot, celery, and water chestnuts about ¾ inch thick. Then cover this with the other half of the egg layer.
Add Chinese gravy.

name: Cheese Crackers
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cover crackers with cheese seasoned with cayenne pepper.
Heat in oven until cheese melts.

name: Cheese Straws
author: Source author unknown
steps: Mix cheese, butter and flour together, moisten with a little cold water.
Roll thin, cut into strips and bake in medium oven.

name: Chekirdeksiz Uzum Khdshabi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a few drops of the essence of orange-flower or rose
a few small pieces of ice
steps: Get a pound of sultana raisins and take the stalks off
Well wash them and put them in a stewpan with a pint of water
Set it to boil until they are swollen up
Take it off and pass the liquor through a sieve into a saucepan
Add sufficient loaf sugar and boil until it becomes thickish
Remove it and let it cool
Pour it in a glass bowl and moderate the sweetness with cold water
Put the boiled raisins in with a few drops of the essence of orange-flower or rose and a few small pieces of ice
Serve

name: Cherry Salad
author: Source author unknown
steps: Fill maraschino cherries with English walnuts, sprinkle nuts around cherries.
Beat yolks of eggs, butter, mustard, salt, red and black pepper together.
Add vinegar and cook until thick.
When cold add the cream, beating it in well.
Pour dressing over cherries and serve on lettuce leaves.

name: Chestnut Kintons (Cream Candy)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: three quarters pint of mirin sauce
steps: Blanch the chestnuts and place them in lukewarm water.
Boil, changing water several times, until you can pierce the nuts with a needle.
Strain off water, then add one pound of sugar, three quarters of a pint of mirin sauce, and boil slowly.
Have ready sweet potatoes which have been peeled and boiled for twenty minutes.
Add to them the vinegar, and strain and press through sieve.
Gradually mix with the chestnuts, and slowly boil, stirring constantly, until dry; then mold into desired shapes.
Roll in powdered sugar.

name: Chicken a la Villeroy
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Cut up and cook a couple of nice chickens as explained for poulet a la St. Lambert
When the pieces of chicken have been stewed in their own broth, drain them
Make a rich veloute with the latter, thickening it with yolks of egg like custard
Dip the pieces of chicken in the thick sauce, and let them get cold
Bread-crumb them, and fry them a golden yellow in boiling fat
Drain them, and pile them on a napkin, garnished with small potato duchesses, and fried parsley
Send the rest of the sauce round in a boat after adding to it a heaped-up table-spoonful of minced mushrooms

name: Chicken Broth
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Cut the chicken into small pieces and place it in a deep earthen dish
Add one quart of water; cover it and set over a kettle of boiling water, letting it steam until the meat of the chicken has become very tender
Strain off the broth and let it stand over night
In the morning remove the fat and return the liquid to the original earthen dish

name: Chicken Chop Sooy (With Giblets)
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: One pound lean young pig pork, cut into slices one inch long, one-quarter inch wide and one-quarter inch thick
Two chicken livers, gizzards and hearts, sliced thin
One pound cooked white meat of chicken, cut fine
One small can white mushrooms, sliced
steps: Cut one pound lean young pig pork into slices one inch long, one-quarter inch wide and one-quarter inch thick.
Slice thin two chicken livers, gizzards and hearts, and one-half ounce green ginger roots.
Put all in kettle with one tablespoon olive oil previously heated, and brown evenly, stirring frequently till done, using care that it does not scorch.
Add one pound cooked white meat of chicken cut fine.
Pour around sides of kettle one cupful hot chicken stock, add one tablespoon Seasoning Sauce and stir carefully.
Have ready two cups celery cut fine, one small can white mushrooms sliced, a tablespoon shredded onion and put all in kettle, cooking for twelve minutes.
Put in one-half cup bean sprouts, adding a little as directed.
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chicken Chop with Green Ginger
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: one teaspoonful each of olive oil and peanut oil
one-half pound lean young pig pork cut in long thin strips
one pound cooked chicken meat both dark and white
one cupful bamboo shoots cut fine
steps: Have a teasponful each of olive oil and peanut oil hot in the kettle
Put in first a half pound lean young pig pork cut in long thin strips and brown carefully
When done add one pound cooked chicken meat both dark and white
Add one cupful bamboo shoots cut fine, one cup white mushroom tops, one-half ounce green ginger root and pour around dish one cup chicken stock
Cook for ten minutes and add one cup bean sprouts
Cook six minutes longer, no more, or bean sprouts cook too long
Add one teaspoon of each sauce with one teaspoon rice flour for thickening
Add six drops Sesamun oil just before serving
Cut bamboo shoots and mushroom tops very fine
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chicken Curry
author: Source author unknown
steps: Prepare chicken for frying, brown in butter.
Cover with boiling water and simmer till tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add to the curry made from Indian Curry recipe.
Serve with boiled rice.

name: Chicken Entree
author: Source author unknown
steps: Remove meat from bones
Chop fine
Boil the bones in water enough to cover them, for half an hour
Add to the chopped chicken the eggs well beaten and sufficient of the stock to make a smooth paste
Season with salt and pepper, add butter
Boil macaroni until tender, being careful not to break
Line a buttered porcelain bowl with the macaroni and fill with mixture
Set in saucepan of boiling water and cook for half hour, or until chicken is tender
Reverse in circular chop dish, surrounded with mushrooms and serve hot

name: Chicken Fruit Chop Sooy (Sum Soo)
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: One-half pound lean pork from the shoulder
One-half pound white meat of cooked chicken
Six Chinese mushrooms, previously steamed with stems removed
One cupful weak and hot chicken stock
One dessertspoon rice flour, wheat flour, or cornstarch
steps: Cut fine one-half pound of lean pork from the shoulder, one-half pound white meat of cooked chicken, seven Chinese potatoes, six Chinese mushrooms, scant cupful bamboo shoots, and one cupful celery.
Place pork in kettle with one level tablespoon olive oil already heated to prevent meat from sticking, and stir frequently till done.
Add the cooked chicken meat and the vegetables prepared as directed above, adding a little more oil if necessary.
Draw the mixture carefully from the sides of the kettle to the center and pour around the sides of the kettle a cupful of weak and hot chicken stock.
Cover tightly and let cook slowly till the vegetables are done for about fifteen minutes.
Mix one teaspoon of each sauce with one dessertspoon rice flour, wheat flour, or cornstarch, a teaspoon chicken stock, and a pinch sugar to thicken gravy.
Add a little more stock to the kettle if necessary.
Serve with bowl of rice and pot of tea.
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chicken Liver Paste
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Fry chicken livers over slow fire, or boil if preferred.
Drain from water or fat when cooked, and crush through sieve.
Fry a cupful of fresh or dried mushrooms.
Crush these also through sieve, and add it to the livers.
Add the juice of an onion and some lemon juice.
Serve on salted crackers.

name: Chicken Liver Paste, No. 2
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: red radish or sprigs of parsley
steps: Take one-quarter pound chicken livers that have been boiled soft
Drain and rub through grater
Add one-quarter cup of fresh mushrooms that have been fried for three minutes in two tablespoons of chicken fat
Chop these mushrooms
Mix smooth with the liver, moistening with the fat used in frying the mushrooms
Season with salt, pepper, paprika and a little onion and lemon juice
Spread on rye bread slices
Garnish plate with a red radish or sprigs of parsley

name: Chicken Omelet Fo Yun Guy
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Beat the eggs well and put them in a bowl with oil and salt.
Cut the onions, chicken, bamboo shoots, water chestnuts, and mushrooms into threads 1 1/2 inches long.
Mix together all of the ingredients and fry in boiling oil until done.
Put all in a bowl and add Chinese gravy.

name: Chicken Starch
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Pound the chicken, without skin and bone, as fine as possible. It is best when pounded with a hammer on a chopping-board.
Add the soup, cornstarch, and white of egg. Stir well.
Never pour it into the substance without first removing the pan from the fire. Keep stirring. Take off the fire the minute it begins to boil. The taste is bad if it boils too long.

name: Chili Sauce I
author: Source author unknown
steps: Peel and cut up tomatoes
Chop the celery, red peppers and onions fine
Mix all the ingredients together in the fireless cooker kettle and allow it to boil twenty minutes and place in the cooker from eight to twenty four hours
Remove from the cooker, bring again to a brisk boil and seal in glass bottles or earthenware jars with wax or paraffin

name: Chili Sauce III
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil all together until thick
Then add vinegar
Strain and set on the stove
Add salt and spices
Boil all together five minutes and remove

name: Chili Vinegar
author: Source author unknown
steps: Chop, and pound in a mortar four dozen fresh chilies, and put them into a bottle with a pint of strong vinegar
shake the bottle every day, and in three weeks it will be ready for use

name: Chinese Chop Sooy (Ordinary)
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: A dessertspoonful of lard, olive oil, butter or peanut oil
One cupful hot chicken stock or water
Six Chinese mushrooms, soaked or steamed with stems removed
Six Chinese potatoes, peeled and sliced thin
A heaping teaspoon rice flour or cornstarch
steps: Cut one pound of lean pork in small pieces and braise in the kettle with a dessertspoonful of lard, olive oil, butter or peanut oil, the latter being preferred.
Cover tightly, removing the cover and stirring occasionally till cooked through and lightly browned.
Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Add one small cupful sliced onions and continue to cook for three or four minutes.
Pour a cupful of hot chicken stock or water, carefully around the sides of the kettle, taking great care not to pour over the top of the food.
Cut the Chinese mushrooms fine and the Chinese potatoes into thin slices.
Add the mushrooms, potatoes, and celery immediately to the pork and onions.
Put in one tablespoon of the Seasoning Sauce and mix well with the ingredients and cover the kettle tightly.
Let cook for twelve or fifteen minutes slowly, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking to bottom of kettle and burning.
Add water or stock, as necessary, to prevent the mixture from becoming dry.
Mix two tablespoons of the Flavoring Sauce with a heaping teaspoon of rice flour or cornstarch and add to the ingredients in the kettle, allowing the gravy to thicken slowly.
Add four drops of Sesamun Oil, stir carefully and remove from the fire.
Serve with rice in separate bowls and with tea.
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chinese Cured Pork
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: pork, preferably from the shoulder of the pig
steps: Remove the fat from the pork, cut preferably from the shoulder of the pig, and cut into strips.
Rub into the pork the Seasoning Sauce, and a little of the Flavoring Sauce.
Rub over it some good brandy and place in the oven.
Mix a small cup of the two sauces, add a little brandy, and baste frequently till done.
This cured pork is used for a garnish for many of the dishes, and is sliced in thin strips about two inches long.
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chinese Fritters
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
steps: Scald the rice flour and sugar together with hot water
Mix like bread, kneading lightly
Roll into little balls
Cook in deep fat as you would ordinary fritters or doughnuts
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chinese Pickled Yellow Turnips
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one quarter of a clove of garlic
steps: Cut the turnip in thin slices, then cut each slice in narrow strips until it looks like strands.

Place in bowl and over it pour two cupfuls of vinegar, a dash of cayenne, a quarter of a clove of garlic, two teaspoonfuls of salt, and one teaspoonful of ginger, and let stand twenty-four hours before serving.

name: Chinese Red Cheese
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: Bean cake made of Chinese red beans
steps: Wrap up the cakes in a piece of cloth in any desired size
Put pressure on top for 5 days
Take off the weight and then the cloth
Scrape off the mold on top
Place in a jar
Fill the jar 1/2 full of Fun Wine, and add plenty of salt
Cover air-tight, and set away for not less than two weeks; the longer, the better, provided the jar is kept air-tight

name: Chinese Roast Pig
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
steps: The pig is carefully dressed, but is not stuffed.
Rub inside and out with the Seasoning Sauce until the meat is well seasoned.
Rub with the finely ground imported spice.
Hang on a spit over a clear wood fire.
Turn frequently and cook slowly till brown and crisp.
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chinese Scrambled Eggs
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one half teaspoon of sweet lard
dash of cayenne pepper or black pepper
steps: Put half a tablespoonful of lard in frying pan and when it is very hot toss in one onion, chopped fine, and fry to a golden brown.
Break five eggs in a bowl, beat well, and turn into the pan; then keep stirring until it is done.
It should all be a light golden brown.
This is very good with rice.

name: Chinese Sponge Cake
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: A few drops of lemon juice
steps: Beat the eggs in a suitable bowl. Mix well with sugar. Beat for an hour, being careful always to beat in one direction.
Mix with the flour and lemon juice.
Put into a suitable pan and steam for 3/4 hour.

name: Chocolate Caramels
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put all but the chocolate in a kettle and boil fast.
When it will almost thread, add chocolate.
Pour in buttered tins.
Cut when cold.

name: Chocolate Sauce No. 1
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Dissolve one-half pound chocolate in one cup of water
Add sugar to taste
Boil somewhat thick and flavor with vanilla

name: Chocolate Syrup
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Dissolve two cups of sugar in one cup of water and boil five minutes
Mix one cup of cocoa with one cup of water and add to the boiling syrup
Boil slowly for ten minutes
Add salt
Cool and bottle for further use

name: Chop Sooy with Veal
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: one-half pound pork with little fat
one pound lean veal cut in small dice
one cup Chinese potatoes cut fine
one-half cup Chinese mushrooms cut in fine pieces
one tablespoon each kind of sauce
one dessertspoon wheat or rice flour
steps: Cut one-half pound pork with little fat, not too much, fine and brown in kettle with one tablespoon olive oil
Brown for five minutes, then add one pound lean veal cut in small dice and brown all together till veal is done
Cover kettle tightly, taking off cover two or three times to stir meat
When done, have ready one cup Chinese potatoes cut fine, one-half cup bamboo shoots, one-half cup Chinese mushrooms all cut in fine pieces
Pour around one cup weak chicken stock, add the vegetables and cook for twelve minutes
Put in one tablespoon each kind of sauce, and one cupful bean sprouts
Cook for six minutes longer, thicken with one dessertspoon wheat or rice flour and serve with rice
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chow Mein
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
steps: Do not allow the noodles to become too dry after making
If too much time is needed, place noodles in ice box till ready
Put olive oil in pan having the oil about one inch deep when heated
Spread the noodles over bottom of pan and let fry slowly till a golden color
Turn over with wide bladed knife or pancake turner and let fry on the other side till done, perhaps ten to fifteen minutes
Remove noodles and drain carefully to remove oil
Put on platter and serve with any one of the Chop Sooy dishes preferred
The Chop Sooy must be ready and hot, and the noodles served immediately when done
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Chutney, No. 1
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: half a pound or a little more of raisins stoned and cut in halves
about twenty chilies well pounded in a mortar
a quarter of a pound of fine ginger
a quarter of a pound of salt or not quite as much
one pound of brown sugar previously boiled to a syrup, or the same quantity of treacle or golden syrup
steps: Put into a large basin or pan, half a pound, or a little more, of raisins stoned and cut in halves, two onions, one garlic, one eschalot, and about twenty chilies well pounded in a mortar
add half a pound of mustard, a quarter of a pound of fine ginger, and a quarter of a pound of salt, or not quite as much
peel and slice one pound of sour apples, put them in a jar with a pint of vinegar
cover the jar well, and put it into the oven and bake until the apples are rather soft

When they are cold, add them to the other ingredients with one pound of brown sugar previously boiled to a syrup, or the same quantity of treacle or golden syrup, and about three pints of vinegar, including the quantity the apples were baked in
Stir all the ingredients well together, and bottle for use

name: Chutney, No. 2
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a quarter of a pound of pudding raisins
a quarter of a pound of apples
the same quantity of moist sugar
chopped tomatos from which you have taken the seeds
steps: Stone and cut up into rather large pieces, a quarter of a pound of pudding raisins

add to these, a quarter of a pound of apples chopped in small pieces, the same quantity of moist sugar, and chopped tomatos from which you have taken the seeds, two ounces of tamarinds, a tablespoonful of salt, ditto of cayenne, a teaspoonful of ground ginger, two large onions chopped fine, very little chopped lemon peel, a pint of lemon juice, and one quart of vinegar
mix all these ingredients well together
then put them into a jar, well covered
Stir the mixture every day for four or five weeks
if at the end of that time it is too thin, pour enough of the liquid away to make it of a proper thickness, but not dry
bottle the chutney in bottles or jars for use

name: Claret Cup
author: Source author unknown
steps: Dissolve the sugar and lemon juice
Add the Claret, Curacoa, Brandy and sliced orange and lemon juice
Put to cool

name: Climbing Fish with Cabbage
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
ingredientsText: cabbage 1 medium sized or 2 to 2.5 seers chopped
steps: Prepare the climbing fishes, keep entire and fry in oil.
Take out the green peas from its legumes and fry them with pieces of potatoes and cassia leaves in ghee or oil.
Chop the tender white portion of the cabbage and fry it with ghee or oil till light brown.
Then add the potatoes, peas, fishes, all the spices pasted together and salt.
Water will come out of the vegetables when salt is added but a little more water may be necessary to boil them.
Season the curry with ghee boiled with a pinch of panch-foron, cassia leaves and chillies.
Add pasted garam-masalla before taking down.

name: Cochinito (Galantina de) (Suckling Pig Galantine)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: Two pounds of beef liver, chopped
Two pounds of fat ham, chopped
steps: Scald it, singe it at the flame and debone it up to the head, which should not be removed.
Chop separately two pounds of beef liver and two pounds of fat ham, and mix them afterward, adding two eggs, salt and spices.
Extend the flattened suckling pig on a table and cover it with half of the said chopped mixture.
Place on top as much as desired of strips of ham, game and poultry in thin slices, and slices of criadillas de tierra, covering all with the other remaining half of the chopped mixture.
Sew the belly skin and give the suckling pig its natural form.
Wrap it in linen and tie it in such a way that it does not decompose or lose its shape.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Cocoa Nut Biscuits
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: three quarters of a pound grated cocoa nut
three quarters of a pound pounded loaf sugar
steps: Mix three quarters of a pound of grated cocoa nut, the same quantity of pounded loaf sugar, and one teaspoonful of arrow root with one egg
Bake on buttered papers

name: Cocoa Nut Cakes
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: two or three ounces sifted white sugar
steps: Grate a fresh cocoa nut, and leave it to dry
Add to it a few sweet almonds and one bitter almond, also grated, two or three ounces of sifted white sugar, and sufficient well-beaten white of egg to make the whole into a stiff paste
Roll it into round balls
Bake on a greased tin until they are quite dry, and the top of them slightly browned
Put them off on to a cold dish

name: Cocoa Nut Soup
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: three ounces of finely-grated cocoa nut
steps: Put three ounces of finely-grated cocoa nut (omitting the dark rind) to three pints of veal stock
Boil it gently for an hour
Mix with a little cold stock enough corn or rice flour to make the soup sufficiently thick
Season to taste
Add half a pint of cream
Simmer all together for about a quarter of an hour
Nutmeg or mace may be added if liked

name: Cocoanut Pudding
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put tapioca in the milk and cook in a double boiler at least ten minutes.
Beat the yolks of eggs and sugar together; add them to the milk and half of the cocoanut.
Cook five minutes longer; take from the fire, and when cold turn into a shallow glass dish.
Beat the whites of eggs until light; add powdered sugar and beat again; spread this over the top and sprinkle over the remaining cocoanut.
Place a few maraschino cherries over the top.

name: Coffee Cake
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: butter, melted, size of an egg
steps: Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon and bake twenty minutes

name: Coles de Bruselas (Brussels Sprouts)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Remove the yellowed leaves and put them to cook in water and salt
Refresh them, and after draining them well, serve them over a piece of butter with salt and pepper

name: Compota de Manzana a la Portuguesa (Portuguese-Style Apple Compote)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Peel the apples and remove the seeds
Put them in a clay pot on a layer of powdered sugar
Place more powdered sugar in the heart of each apple
Cook in the oven or under a dome oven
Dust with sugar and serve hot

name: Cordeiro ou Cabrito Refogado (Braised Lamb or Kid)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: lamb or kid loin or quarter
steps: Place lamb or kid loin or quarter in a pan with water, salt, pieces of bacon, parsley, onion, and garlic clove
Boil until cooked
Fry two tablespoons wheat flour with two tablespoons butter until dark brass-colored
Add the strained broth, one cup white wine, lemon juice, sugar, raisins, and lemon slices
Add the meat and boil over moderate heat until the broth is reduced to few cups
Serve with this sauce

name: Corn Fritters
author: Source author unknown
steps: Grate the corn.
Beat the egg well, whites and yolks together, and by degrees add the corn, beating in thoroughly and very hard.
Add a tablespoonful of melted butter, and then stir in the milk.
Add a tablespoonful of flour, or just sufficient to thicken and bind, and then fry like fritters in boiling lard, dropping in a deep spoonful at a time.
Serve hot.

name: Couves Flor Fritas (Fried Cauliflower)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Proceed as in the previous article, taking care only that the cauliflower is not entirely cooked
Pass them two or three times through hot butter
Let cool well
Soak in thin batter and then fry, taking care that they achieve a good color
Remove, let drain and serve

name: Crab Omelet Fo Yung High
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Beat the eggs well and put them in a bowl with oil and salt.
Cut the onions, crabs, bamboo shoots, water chestnuts, and mushrooms into threads 1 1/2 inches long.
Mix together all of the ingredients and fry in boiling oil until done.
Put all in a bowl and add Chinese gravy.

name: Cream Cake
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Beat very lightly 2 eggs
Stir them into 1 pint of sour cream
Sift in as much flour as will make a stiff batter
Dissolve 1 teaspoonful of soda in a cup of new milk
Add this and a little salt
Mix them well and pour into rather a shallow pan
Bake quickly a nice brown
Serve hot

name: Cream Puffs
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Put 1 cup of water on the fire
When hot melt in 1 cup of best butter
When it boils beat in 1 cup of sifted flour
If lumpy, stir until perfectly smooth
Place it aside to cool
When cool, stir in 1 at a time 3 eggs without first beating them
Drop the batter on tins in small spoonfuls
Bake 1 hour in quick oven
For the cream put 1 1/2 cups of milk to boil
Beat yolks of 2 eggs very light with 4 tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar
When the milk boils, pour it on the eggs, stirring all the while
Wet 2 tablespoonfuls of cornstarch in fine flour with a little cold milk
Add it to the custard and replace on the fire
Stir until quite thick
Flavor when cold with vanilla
Place the cream in the puff by lifting up the top with a knife and dropping in the cream with a small spoon

name: Creamed Codfish
author: Source author unknown
steps: Pick apart codfish
Wash thoroughly in two waters
Soak over night in cold water
Next morning, drain, cover with boiling water and cook below the boiling point for five minutes
Drain and press
Rub butter and flour together
Add milk
Stir until boiling
Add a dash of pepper and the codfish
Cover and stand over hot water ten minutes
Add the beaten yolk of an egg and salt
Serve with plain boiled potatoes

name: Croquante Cakes (Small Cakes)
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Blanch and cut in halves three-fourths pound of shelled almonds
Slice one-half pound of citron
Mix well together and roll in a little flour
Add to them three-fourths pound of sugar
Add six eggs well beaten
Add the rest of the flour (three-fourths pound)
Butter shallow pans
Put in the mixture about two inches thick
Bake in a quick oven
Slice cake in strips three-fourths of an inch wide and turn each piece
Put back in oven and bake a little longer
When cold put away in tin box

name: Cure's Omelette with Tunny and Herring Roes
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: half a slice of preserved tunny
soft roes of two herrings a la sardine
a few drops of lime juice
steps: Finely mince together half a slice of preserved tunny and the soft roes of two herrings a la sardine with a little shallot and a dessert-spoonful of parsley.
Toss the mixture in butter awhile.
Stir into a basin containing six well mixed eggs.
Cook the mixture as already explained.
Turn it out, when ready, into a hot dish containing a little melted butter, a few drops of lime juice and some minced shallot and parsley.

name: Currie Soup
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a large tablespoonful of currie powder
steps: Mince small three or four onions according to their size
Put them into a saucepan with two ounces of butter
Dredge in some flour and fry them of a light brown, taking care not to burn them
Rub in by degrees a large tablespoonful of currie powder till it is quite a paste
Gradually stir in three tablespoonfuls of gravy soup, mixing it well together
Boil it gently until it is well flavoured with the currie powder
Strain it into another saucepan and add a fowl skinned and cut into small pieces
Stew it slowly for an hour
Take out half a pint of the soup and stew in it a large tablespoonful of tamarinds until you can easily take away the stones
Strain and stir into the soup
Boil all together for a quarter of an hour
Serve rice with it

name: Curried Cod
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take a piece of cod, pull it into large flakes, and fry it till brown
Put this into a stewpan, with half a fried onion
Pour over it sufficient good stock to cover it
Add a teaspoonful of currie powder, and two ounces of butter, with salt to taste; also the juice of half a lemon
Simmer for a quarter of an hour, or until the fish is cooked, thicken the gravy, and serve

name: Curried Sole
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a large lump of butter, about two ounces
steps: Take a filleted sole, a large thick one, cut it into pieces, not too small, lay them in vinegar for an hour
Have ready some gravy, prepared with fried onions and currie powder, as for prawn currie
Add to it the pieces of sole, and a large lump of butter, about two ounces
Simmer gently for half an hour, or rather longer if the sole is thick

name: Curried Sweetbreads
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one tablespoonful of vinegar or lemon juice
steps: Have ready some good veal gravy, add to it a very small quantity of fried onion, a tablespoonful of vinegar or the juice of a lemon, the same quantity of currie powder, and salt to taste
Rub two ounces of butter into enough flour to make this gravy (which ought to be about three-quarters of a pint) a proper thickness
Cut up two or three sweetbreads into pieces about two inches square
Stew them gently in the gravy until sufficiently cooked, and serve

name: Dai-Bara
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
steps: Grind some moistened pulses of kalai to a paste.
Add salt and beat thoroughly.
Prepare cakes of it and fry in ghee or oil till brown.
Boil a little ghee with a few mustard seeds and add some curd.
Stir and take down.
Keep the fried baras immersed in the curd for several hours, and then serve.

name: Dandelion Salad
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut off the roots and green portion of the leaves; wash and steep in salt and water
When they become crisp, drain and press dry
Rub the salad bowl with a clove of garlic and season the dandelions with French dressing
This salad may also be served with two hard-boiled eggs cut in quarters or sliced and laid over; or with two medium-sized beets, sliced, and seasoned

name: Date Sandwiches
author: Source author unknown
steps: Clean dates and cover with cold water for three minutes
Drain and lay on a plate, and put in hot oven for five minutes
Remove stones, cut in slices and place between thin buttered slices of bread

name: Deer
author: Shiu Wong Chan
