Sprinkle with a little melted butter.
Place in the oven or under a domed cover to brown.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Lily-Root Pudding
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Dissolve the lily-root powder in a small quantity of cold water. Mash well.
To this add the 6 cups of water and the sugar. Stir well.
Put into a suitable pan. Steam until done (about 1 hour).

name: Lima and Kidney Beans
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put in boiling water, a little more than enough to cover them
Boil until tender, from half an hour to two hours
Serve with butter

name: Lingoada Assada na Grelha (Grilled Flounder)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Clean the fish and dry to remove moisture
Anoint with butter, salt, pepper and nutmeg
Roast on the grill over moderate fire
Serve with a white sauce made of melted butter, flour, white wine and capers

name: Linguas de Carneiro Douradas e Empasteladas (Gilded and Pastry-Enclosed Lamb Tongues)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one dozen sardines in barrels or fresh
two spoonfuls of wheat flour or fine cornmeal
steps: Boil the tongues until cooked, peel them and split them into four strips lengthwise

Take one dozen sardines which are placed on a plate, covered with brandy, and the plate placed over a vessel containing boiling water to heat it; add brandy and let it burn until it extinguishes on its own
Mix six egg yolks and two egg whites well beaten, one cup of milk, two spoonfuls of wheat flour or fine cornmeal, one spoonful of sugar and a little nutmeg
Put a little butter in the bottom of a casserole and fry it, pouring into it half of the mixture just prepared and let it fry

Place on this fried mixture, after removing the casserole from the fire, the strips of tongues and the sardines broken into pieces with some slices of peeled lemon without seeds, all in alternating order
Pour the rest of the mixture on top, cover the casserole and place it to roast in an oven or over coals, also covering the lid with coals
Serve with some salad

name: Lobster Chop Suey
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: A few pieces of Chinese onion
steps: Boil the lobster in water until it turns red. Take off the shell and cut the meat into fragments not longer than 1½ inches.
Fry the lobster with the Fun Wine, and ginger root juice for 5 minutes over a hot fire.

Cut the bamboo shoots, water chestnuts, celery, and onion into pieces the size of the lobster fragments. Fry these in a hot, oiled pan for 3 minutes. Add water enough to cover and cook for 10 minutes. Then mix with the lobster.

name: Lobster Chow Main
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: First boil the peanut oil and into it throw the noodles, cooking until crisp.
Remove and drain, while preparing following:
Put teaspoon of sweet lard into frying pan, and when hot turn in half the lobster meat, which has previously been cooked.
Cook for a few minutes, then add the onion, mushrooms, and water chestnuts.
The bamboo shoots are added last, and all fried for ten minutes.
Take a hot platter, and place the crisp noodles as a layer at the bottom of the dish, and spread above ingredients on top.
Then take the other half of the lobster meat, and place a layer on top.
Garnish with shredded yolks of hard-boiled eggs.

name: Lobster Cofta Curry
author: Source author unknown
steps: According to their size, take eight or ten lobsters
Clean them thoroughly
Remove the heads and shells
Pull the flesh to pieces and pound to a pulp
Add to it some of the red coral from the head
Mix into it the bread-crumbs, salt, pepper, herbs, and an egg well beaten up, and make into balls
Bruise down the remains of the heads and the contents of the long legs with unroasted coriander-seed

Take all the juice and fry it in mustard oil with the ground condiments omitting the ginger, and cook the balls in the same way as the prawn balls, with the addition of bay-leaves and a few blades of lemon-grass

name: Lobster Currie
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one tablespoonful and a half of currie powder
half a pint of good gravy
tablespoonful of vinegar or lemon juice
steps: Fry two onions in half an ounce of butter, until they are nicely browned
Mix one tablespoonful and a half of currie powder, with half a pint of good gravy, and put this with the fried onions into a stewpan
Take the meat from a large lobster, cut it into rather small pieces, and add it to the gravy and onions with a tablespoonful of vinegar or lemon juice
Simmer slowly for about half an hour, and serve

name: Lobster Omelette
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one tablespoonful of chopped lobster meat
steps: Use small frying pan and put into it a teaspoonful of peanut oil
Heat it
Beat two eggs with a tablespoonful of cold water
Pour half in the pan
Have ready the cooked lobster, broken into small pieces
Quickly pour in the other half of beaten eggs, and cook slowly for five minutes
Slip off pan without breaking, and make two or three more omelettes in exactly the same way, or have several small frying pans and cook all at once
Serve one omelette on top of another in a hot water-heated platter

name: Loin of Mutton en Papillote
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: a tea-spoonful of powdered dried sweet herbs
steps: Trim the loin nicely, and let it lie from morning till roasting time in marinade, composed of a breakfast-cupful of salad oil, two onions, and a carrot, sliced fine as for Julienne, with some whole peppers, salt, chopped parsley, and a tea-spoonful of powdered dried sweet herbs.
Let the joint be turned several times during the day, and baste it often.
When to be dressed, pack it, with its vegetables and all, in a well oiled paper, and roast it carefully, basting it with the oil that composed the marinade.
When nearly done, remove the paper, brush off the vegetables, baste with melted butter, and serve, when nicely browned, with other vegetables independently cooked, and some gravy.

name: Lombo de Pescada Ensopado (Stewed Hake Loin)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Remove the loins from a good fish, sprinkle them on all sides with salt and a little pepper
Pass them in melted butter, and cover with a layer of breadcrumbs
Pass them in beaten eggs and wrap again in another layer of breadcrumbs
Roast them on the grill over a very low fire, and when well browned, put them on a plate
On the other hand, melt two tablespoons of butter, mix with half a cup of white wine and one cup of broth
Boil, pour very hot over the fish, and serve

name: Lombo de Pescada Frito (Fried Hake Loin)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Remove the skin from the fish
Take out the loins
Season with salt, pepper and chopped parsley
Fry in butter
Serve when cooked

name: Lombo de Porco à Moda de Bolonha (Pork Loin Bologna-Style)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take a pork loin with the loin still attached
Cover it with sage leaves and tie both ends with twine to give it a round shape
Place it in a terrine, cover with vinegar, and add some onions and carrots cut into slices, lemon zest, and some cloves
Let it marinate for two to three days
After this time, place the loin in a casserole, adding half of the marinade liquid, two cups of water or meat broth, two onions, two carrots, and a bundle of aromatic herbs, salt and pepper
Cover the casserole, place it over a strong fire which is then reduced, letting it cook for two to three hours
Remove the twine and sage leaves, place it on a plate, and serve with a portion of redcurrant jelly in a separate terrine
Alternatively, the sauce in which the loin was cooked may be poured over it

name: Lord Clive's Currie
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take six sliced onions, one green apple, and a clove of garlic
Stew them to a pulp in a little good stock
Add one teaspoonful of currie powder, a few tablespoonfuls of stock, a salt-spoonful of salt, and the same quantity of Cayenne pepper
Add to this gravy any kind of uncooked meat cut into small pieces
Add a piece of butter

name: Lucauan Eggs
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut eggs in eighths lengthwise.
Add cooked macaroni, cheese, and white sauce seasoned with salt, pepper, onion juice and anchovy essence.
Turn into a buttered baking dish.
Cover with buttered crumbs.
Set in the oven long enough to bake crumbs.

name: Lucauian Eggs
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut eggs in eighths lengthwise.
Add cooked macaroni, cheese, and white sauce seasoned with salt, pepper, onion juice and anchovy essence.
Turn into a buttered baking dish; cover with buttered crumbs and set in the oven long enough to bake crumbs.

name: Lychee Chicken
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Cut into small pieces a fresh young chicken of about two pounds and rub well with salt.
Fry two tablespoonfuls of sweet lard a very light brown.
Add two tablespoonfuls of syou, and cover tight.
Simmer for half an hour.
Have ready a quart of lychee nuts, peeled and stoned.
Add these to the chicken, with the minced onion, and cook slowly for twenty-six minutes.
Serve with rice.

name: Madras Anchovy Toast
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a piece of butter the size of an apple
half a teaspoonful of white wine or a teaspoonful of beer
steps: Put a piece of butter the size of an apple upon a very hot plate
add the well-beaten yolks of two eggs, cayenne pepper to taste, half a teaspoonful of white wine, or a teaspoonful of beer, and a tablespoonful of anchovy paste
Mix well
soak hot toast in it, and serve very hot

name: Maitre d'Hotel Sauce
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: a heaping tablespoon of drippings or goose-fat
a small cup of hot soup or water
steps: Take a heaping tablespoon of drippings or goose-fat, heat it in a spider
Stir two teaspoons of flour into this
Add gradually and carefully a small cup of hot soup or water
Add some chopped parsley, also the juice of a lemon
Add salt and pepper
Stir up well

name: Makarna-Chbrbassi
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Make exactly as Shariys Chbrbassi, only it takes two or three times longer than the vermicelli

name: Malay Currie
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: the rind of half a lemon
steps: Blanch two ounces of almonds
Fry them in a little butter until they are brown, but do not let them burn
Pound them to a cream with an onion and the rind of half a lemon
Mix a dessert-spoonful of currie powder with half a pint of water, and put this with the almonds into a stewpan, with a chicken cut up into joints
Let it simmer gently for nearly an hour
Add a teacup-ful of cream and let it nearly boil
Squeeze into it the juice of a lemon, and serve up

name: Mallard Ducks or Canvasback Ducks Roasted
author: Source author unknown
steps: Clean the ducks as you would a chicken, without scalding, however, rinse out the inside and wipe well inside and out with a wet towel.
Do not wash the duck unless you have broken the gall bladder, as the washing destroys their flavor.
Rub the inside well with salt and pepper, and rub outside as thoroughly.
Place a three-inch lump of butter on the inside.
Truss nicely and place the ducks in a baking pan, and brush the tops with melted butter.

Pour over two tablespoonfuls of water, and set in a very hot oven, and allow them to bake twenty minutes, if they are not very large, and thirty minutes, if larger than the ordinary size of Canvasback ducks.
A wild duck is never cooked dry. It must reach the point where the blood will not run if the flesh is pierced with the fork in carving.
When done, place the ducks in a very hot dish, and serve with their own gravy poured over them.
Garnish nicely with parsley or water cress.
Serve with Currant Jelly.
Always have the plates very hot in which you serve the ducks at table.

name: Mamones de Harina de Trigo (Wheat Flour Mamones)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: One pound of flour in its finest form
steps: Beat twelve egg whites and sixteen egg yolks until the batter is white and thick
Then add one pound of fine flour little by little, so it does not become lumpy or muddled
Make the mamones long like biscotti, or round
To give them a crust, beat eighteen eggs and add them on top
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Mango Butter
author: Source author unknown
steps: Select ripe mangoes and pass through a sieve.
Allow equal weight of sugar and mango, using half white and half native brown sugar.
Boil for three hours.

name: Marbled Cake
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Soak cochineals in a wineglass of water, adding a small pinch of soda
Pour the cake into the pan for baking
At the same time pour with it this water, mixing it well with the cake

name: Marmalade of Ginger
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
ingredientsText: 1 chhatak of pasted leaves of Indian black berry (kala jam)
powders of cardamoms, cinnamon and camphor - 1 pinch each
5 or 6 drops of essence of rose
steps: Peel 1 seer of ginger and perforate them all over with an iron pin.
Keep them immersed in lime water for 3 days and then wash them with plain water.
Boil them with 1 chhatak of pasted leaves of Indian black berry (kala jam) in about 2 seers of water till fully boiled.
Wash them 3 or 4 times with plain water and drop them in a boiling syrup of 1 seer of sugar.
Mix powders of cardamoms, cinnamon and camphor 1 pinch each and 5 or 6 drops of essence of rose with the mass when the syrup is very thick.
Then take down, serve one small piece to each when cold and preserve in bottles.

name: Marreco estufado com ameixas do Canadá (Duck Braised with Canadian Plums)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: Canadian plums, peeled and pitted, or preserved plums mixed with raisins and pieces of peeled quince
half a pound of bacon, cut in pieces
two dozen peeled plums without pits
steps: Take the duck and fill it with peeled and pitted Canadian plums, or in their absence with preserved plums mixed with raisins and pieces of peeled quince
Place the duck in the pan with half a pound of bacon cut in pieces, two glasses of wine, little salt, nutmeg, cardamom, clove of India, two dozen peeled plums without pits
Seal the lid and boil it over regularly hot fire

name: Marrow Balls for Asparagus Soup
author: Source author unknown
steps: Mix together cooked marrow, bread crumbs, parsley, salt and pepper
Add enough raw egg to this mixture to insure the balls not coming to pieces in cooking
Form into balls the size of filberts
Roll in raw egg and fine bread crumbs or flour
Simmer in soup a few minutes before serving

name: Marshmallow Cake
author: Source author unknown
steps: Bake angel cake in two layers
Make boiled icing of one large cup sugar to whites of two small eggs
Cut marshmallows in halves and put on coating of icing, then more icing
Flavor with two-thirds vanilla and one-third almond

name: Marshmallows
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: two thirds of a glass distilled water
steps: Boil sugar and water until it forms a firm ball when dropped in water.
Let the gelatine soak in two thirds of a glass distilled water for about ten minutes.
Add gelatine to boiling sugar as it is taken from the stove.
Add flavoring and beat until spongy and light.
Pour into slightly buttered platter and let stand until next morning.
Cut into cubes and roll in powdered sugar or cornstarch to prevent stickiness.

name: Masa de Empanadas (Meat Pie Dough)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: less than half a cuartilla of flour
sufficient quantity of very hot water
steps: Melt the butter and fat
Skim well before incorporating into the flour
Add the six egg yolks and sufficient quantity of very hot water
Knead for a long time and roll out many times

name: Matzoth Charlotte, No. 2
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Prepare four egg yolks with one cup of sugar and pinch of salt
Soak three matzoth in water and squeeze out
Add one grated apple, one lemon rind and juice
Add one-fourth cup of almonds, and one-fourth cup of raisins
Put the stiffly-beaten whites of eggs in last, before putting into oven
Bake in an even oven about one-half to three-quarters of an hour
To be eaten warm

name: Mayonnaise Especially for Salmon
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Rub the yolks of two hard-boiled eggs to a powder, then add eight tablespoons of cream very gradually to them, also white pepper, a pinch of salt and a mere suspicion of cayenne pepper.
Lastly add two tablespoons of white vinegar.
It is very important that this last ingredient be put in drop by drop, otherwise the mixture will curdle.

name: Meat Chow Main
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one half pound of dried mushrooms
steps: Into a quart of peanut oil put a quarter of a pound of noodles, and cook until crisp; then remove and drain.
Meanwhile take one pound of pork, cut it in small pieces, and fry a golden brown.
Cut up half a pound of veal, and fry with the pork for five minutes.
Add two tablespoonfuls of syou and half a tablespoonful of salt to this, and let it simmer slowly, while preparing the following:

Wash, and soak for ten minutes, half a pound of Chinese dried mushrooms, pulling off the stalks; half a bunch of celery, cut small; also one onion, chopped fine, and half a dozen water chestnuts, sliced fine.
Turn these in with the meat and cook all together for five minutes.
Place the noodles on a hot platter as a bottom layer, then the meat and vegetables.
Garnish the top with threaded ham and the crumbled yolks of two hard-boiled eggs.

name: Medkune
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: two or three pounds of mutton
juice of two or three small lemons
steps: Peel four or five egg-plants, cut them in slices about three-quarters of an inch thick, and partly scald them in salt water
Cut two or three pounds of mutton in pieces the size of walnuts, sprinkle one or two chopped onions over with a little salt, and rub them well together with your hands
Place into a stewpan the pieces of meat and the egg-plants, in layers, cover them with mutton or beef broth, add the juice of two or three small lemons
Put the pan on the fire with the lid on, and let it simmer until it forms a nice gravy at the bottom
Dish it up, sprinkle a little cinnamon over, and serve

name: Menekshe Shurubi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound of fresh gathered violets
two pints and a gill of boiling water
about three pounds of crushed sugar
steps: Procure a pound of fresh gathered violets, cut the stalks off, and put the leaves in a basin
Pour two pints and a gill of boiling water over, immediately cover it, and let it remain for twelve or fifteen hours
Pass the liquor through a clean cloth into a stewpan, add about three pounds of crushed sugar
Stir with a wooden spoon till the sugar is dissolved, and set it on a charcoal fire
Just as it commences to boil up, instantly remove it, and let it remain covered till nearly cold
Then pass it again through a cloth, bottle and cork it up till wanted

name: Meringue Pudding
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
ingredientsText: juice and grated rind of 1 lemon
steps: Stew 6 large, nice apples, and mash through a sieve
Mix in 1 lb. of butter and 1 lb. of sugar
Add 6 eggs beaten very light
Add the juice and grated rind of 1 lemon
Bake the pudding
Save out the whites of 3 eggs, beat them up with 3 tablespoonfuls of sifted sugar to a stiff froth
After the pudding is baked and nearly cold, lay the sugar and egg over the top
Set it in a cool oven for a few minutes, until it is crusted, but not browned

name: Mevlevi Pilawi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound of rice, well washed
half a pound of fresh butter
steps: Put two quarts of water in a saucepan with sufficient salt, put it on the fire.
When boiling, throw into it a pound of rice, well washed, and boil until each grain is soft and separate.
Drain it through a clean cloth or in a colander, put it back in the pan, and set it on a slow fire without the cover until the moisture is dispersed.
Put a saucepan on the fire with half a pound of fresh butter.
When it boils, pour it over the rice and stir it once round with a fork, put the pan on the hob with the cover over, and let it remain for five or ten minutes.
Dish up, and serve hot.

name: Minced Lamb
author: Source author unknown
steps: Rub butter and flour together and the milk and seasoning
Cook until boiling
Add the mint and lamb
Place over hot water while you make the toast
Trim toast, butter and cover each slice with a thick layer of minced lamb, leaving a hole in center
Poach six eggs
Put one in each center

name: Minced Mutton, Fried (Carne de carneiro picada e frita)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: two pounds of mutton, sinews and skin removed
one pound of pork with some fat
one handful of powder of good polvilho biscuits
steps: Mince the mutton with the pork.
Melt a little fat in a pan and when well heated, add the minced meat.
Fry on one side, then turn to fry on the other side.
Serve with a spicy sauce.

name: Mingão da Uberaba (Uberaba Corn Porridge)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Make the same way as Ceará soup, but instead of wheat flour, use milled cornmeal or fine cornmeal

name: Mingão de Paulista (Paulista Corn Porridge)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put a pot with water, salt, and one spoonful of fat on the fire
When boiling, gradually add four spoonfuls of fine cornmeal dissolved in a little cold water and one parsley leaf, stirring constantly
Let cook for a little more time and remove the pot from the fire

name: Mint Chutney
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Scald the mint leaves before pounding them.
Make in the same way as cocoanut chutney, substituting pounded mint for cocoanut.

name: Miolo de Vacca (Beef Brain)
author: Source author unknown
steps: First bring the brain to hot water and after cleaning of blood and the membrane that covers it, place for one or two hours in cold water
Cook in this same water with a small cup of vinegar, salt, pepper, cloves, bay leaves, garlic, parsley, celery root and carrots
Three-quarters of an hour are sufficient for it to be cooked
Serve with any sauce indicated for meats

name: Mo Ku Gai T'ong (Spring Chicken Soup with Mushrooms)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: two and one half pounds of chicken
one quarter pound of lean pork
one quarter pound of dried mushrooms
steps: Clean a fresh young chicken of about two and one half pounds
Cut off all the flesh; put the bones, with liver and gizzard, into three pints of cold water, and boil for two hours, adding water if it boils away
While the stock is boiling, cut up the chicken meat into small pieces
Cut up very fine one quarter pound of lean pork
Wash and soak in lukewarm water one quarter pound of dried mushrooms
Pull off all the stalks
Peel and cut a dozen lotus seeds or water chestnuts
Chop three stalks of celery very fine, and also one onion
Pour off the liquor from the bones, and strain
Cut up liver and gizzard fine and return to stock
Add all the ingredients, with one teaspoonful of salt and one tablespoonful of syou
Boil all together for one hour

name: Modo de Torrar Café à Mineira (Method of Roasting Coffee in the Minas Style)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Place the washed and dry coffee in a small pan proper for roasting coffee; roast over a lively fire, stirring with a bread spoon until it is of suitable color; remove then from the fire and place in a coarse sieve to let the smoke out; put in the same pan one pound of brown sugar or refined sugar for four pounds of coffee; add the roasted coffee, stir well and let cool, then crush or grind the coffee and save it for daily use.

name: Mojarra with Its Roe
author: Source author unknown
steps: Wash them very well, then remove from water, pat dry and remove the roe
In a pan with oil and lard, fry the mojarra carefully so it does not break
In the same lard, fry the roe after slicing it very thinly
Remove it and in the same lard fry bread slices
Remove these and still in the same lard fry minced tomatoes and finely minced onion
Grind half of the fried roe together with the bread and mix with the tomato and onion
Add a pinch of pepper, a little vinegar and a good amount of oil
Let it simmer and when ready, moisten the mojarra with this sauce inside and out
Place on a platter and top with the remaining roe sliced together with sliced fried bread

name: Molasses Cookies
author: Source author unknown
steps: Melt the molasses.
Beat the butter and sugar to a cream, and add, mixing in the soda, dissolved in a tablespoonful of boiling water.
Add the ginger and the ground cloves.
Take off the fire, and beat till cool.
Then add the eggs, beaten well, and flour sufficient to make a nice, soft dough, just stiff enough to roll.
Cut into small cakes, and bake in a quick oven to a delicate brown.

name: Molho de Florença (Florentine Sauce)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one chalice of sweet olive oil
steps: Place a bowl inside a pot filled with boiling water
Put four egg yolks with salt and pepper powder in the bowl
Add little by little one chalice of sweet olive oil, stirring strongly
Remove the bowl and serve with all kinds of fish
Take great care not to apply too much heat, because the egg yolks will curdle and the sauce will be ruined

name: Molho por Excellencia (Sauce Par Excellence)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: some spoons of wheat flour or starch
steps: Wash some sardines and remove the bones; cut them well along with 1 onion
Heat a piece of washed butter in a saucepan
Once melted, add some spoons of wheat flour or starch, a little bell pepper, and nutmeg
Add the chopped sardines, meat broth, juice of 2 lemons, and slices of 1 lemon
Let it boil a little and serve

name: Moong Dal
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: half a pound of raw dal or half a cupful
three-quarters of a chittack of ghee
half a teaspoonful of ground turmeric
half a teaspoonful of ground ginger
a quarter of a teaspoonful of ground garlic
one teaspoonful and a half of salt
steps: Clean, pick, and roast the dal
Mix it up with all the ground condiments and salt
Put into a pot and pour water over the whole, some two inches above the dal
Boil it well until the dal has quite dissolved, allowing it to cake as it were en masse
Churn the dal by twirling it in a wooden instrument called a phootnee
Warm the ghee in a separate pot and fry the onions
Chop the onions and throw into the churned dal
Pour the dal into the pot of melted ghee and keep stirring until the dal and ghee have well mixed
Put the cover on and allow to simmer over a slow fire for about a quarter of an hour

name: Morella Cherries with Fried Bread
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Put a pint of water in a pan and put it on the fire.
When boiling, skim it, then add two pounds of morella cherries with the stalks taken off and the stones taken out.
Stir with a wooden spoon, and boil them until getting tender.
Cut two French penny rolls lengthwise in eight slices.
Put the yolks of two eggs in a basin, with eight tablespoonfuls of milk, and beat it up well.
Dip quickly each slice in it, and fry it a nice colour on both sides in hot fresh butter.
Lay them in a convenient pie-dish, then put the cherries over with the syrup.
If you find the syrup too thick, add a little water.
Set it on a moderate charcoal fire, and let it simmer until the syrup is absorbed, then serve.

name: Mrs. W.'s Currie
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take a piece of butter twice as big as a walnut, fry it with a rather large onion cut into thin slices
Cut up a fowl into joints, and put it into a stewpan with a fried onion
Simmer it for a quarter of an hour
Add two or three chopped apples, and as much water or gravy as will cover it
Let it stew slowly for an hour
Take a tablespoonful of currie powder, and a dessert-spoonful of dry mustard, mix them together with milk into a liquid, and pour it into the stewpan
Add half a tea-cupful of vinegar, the juice of a lemon, and a little salt
Simmer it for half an hour, skim it well, and then serve it up

name: Muffins
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Light the burners of the gas oven before beginning to mix the muffins and work rapidly

Place in a mixing-bowl one well-beaten egg, two tablespoons of butter, one tablespoon of sugar, one-half teaspoon of salt, one scant cup of milk and two teaspoons of baking-powder that have been sifted with sufficient flour to form a batter that will ribbon from the spoon
Beat the batter steadily for five minutes
Stir in one tablespoon of melted butter
Bake in muffin-pans in a quick oven
Bake ten minutes if pans are only half filled

name: Mulligatawny
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: the juice of a lime or small lemon
a piece of butter mixed with a little flour
steps: Cut up the fowl and put it into a pan with two quarts of cold water
Let it simmer until all the juice of the meat is extracted
Strain it, and when cold, put to the liquor two chickens, cut as for a fricassee

Add two tablespoonfuls of currie powder, one sliced onion and a clove of garlic, a little salt, the juice of a lime or small lemon, a piece of butter mixed with a little flour, and a wineglassful of Madeira
When ready to dish up, which will be in about three-quarters of an hour, throw in a little fried onion
Serve rice with it, but in another dish

name: Mulligatawny Soup
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a little lemon or mango juice
steps: Skin and cut up a rabbit or fowl into small joints
Brown them in a frying-pan
Put them into a stewpan with five fried onions, a small piece of garlic, and three pints of stock into which you have previously mixed two tablespoonfuls of currie powder
Simmer gently for two hours
Add one ounce of pounded almonds and mix well
Add a little lemon or mango juice, with a good lump of butter and salt to taste
Serve very hot and send up a large dish of boiled rice with it, or the rice may be put into the soup, if preferred

name: Mushi Kiji (Roast Pheasant)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one pound of small Japanese almonds
one and one half cupfuls of rice paste
one half cupful of cooking sauce
steps: Wash and singe the bird, then rub well with salt.
Place in deep dish and cover with three cupfuls of mirin sauce; more, if that quantity does not cover the bird.
Lay away in a cool place over night, then drain off all liquid.
Have ready the almonds, blanched and chopped very fine.
Add them to the rice paste with the sugar, a little salt, quarter of a cup of cooking sauce, and a pinch of mixed spices.
Stir all together, and stuff the pheasant with this mixture.
Sew up, and truss.
Have ready boiling hot olive oil or goma-seed oil, pour it over the pheasant, and place in a hot oven.
Roast until tender (about one hour), adding little by little the rest of the cooking sauce, and basting frequently.
Cook for a half-hour longer, then place on hot platter and garnish with flower petals and water cress.

name: Mushi Tamana and Buta (Cabbage and Pork)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: First boil the salt pork for one hour, then chop it in small pieces
Select a good hard cabbage without blemishes and wash it thoroughly in cold water
Soak it in water with a handful of salt to kill all possible vermin
Remove from salted water, and rinse in fresh water, removing all salt
Carefully cut out the heart and center leaves, making a good-sized pocket, and fill this space with the chopped pork and one onion chopped very fine, salt, pepper, and a teaspoonful of goma seeds
Press the cabbage leaves back into place, and tie tight in cheesecloth
Have ready a deep pot of boiling salted water, and in this place the cabbage in the bag
Cover, and boil slowly for two hours
Remove to a platter, and pour over it the syou sauce, which has first been boiled
Serve with rice

name: Mutton Cutlets with Mixed Vegetables
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: eight cutlets from a neck of mutton
steps: Take the eight cutlets and trim them neatly
Grill them over a brisk, clear fire
When done, arrange them round a circle of nicely mashed potato
Place a sauce an macedoine de legumes in the centre
The sauce should contain French beans, a carrot, a turnip, and a piece of cucumber, previously boiled and cut into small dice
Heat the vegetables up in well made sauce blonde
Add a few green peas and some pieces of boiled celery if available

name: Muéganos Poblanos (Pueblan Honey Fritters)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: anise powder, the amount that fits between three fingers
half a small cup of settled tequesquite water
one and a half pounds of sugar for syrup
steps: Put one pound of flour in a pan with thirty egg yolks
Add the amount of anise powder that fits between three fingers
Add half a small cup of settled tequesquite water and three tablespoons of brandy
Knead and if it remains loose, add flour until it does not stick to the hand
Beat a lot on a metate
Make long thin sticks that are wound in the hand
Fry in lard, making the sticks on a table
Make a syrup with three pounds of sugar and one and a half pounds of sugar

name: Mólho Pardo (Brown Sauce)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a quantity of grated bread crusts
a few cups of beef broth or beef substance for sauces
steps: Fry in a little fat pieces of roasted beef and a quantity of grated bread crusts
After half an hour, add onion leaves, parsley, salt, one pimiento, and a few cups of beef broth or beef substance
Allow to boil for another half hour
Strain and, if desired, add a little vinegar or lemon juice before serving

name: Nasubi Yaki (Fried Eggplant)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Peel the eggplant and cut it in slices.
Cover with ice water and a handful of salt.
Put on a heavy weight, iron or stone, to press out the juice, and leave for about half an hour.
Strain off all water, which will be a dark brown, and rinse with fresh cold water, wiping dry each slice.
Dip each piece in beaten eggs, and fry in goma-seed oil; drain off all oil.
Place on a platter, covering well with one cupful of cooking sauce, boiled.
Sprinkle with goma seeds, and serve with rice.

name: Ndr Khdshabi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: water equal to the quantity of juice
steps: Cut open three or four pomegranates and take the grains out
Pick up the large ones and put the small ones in a cloth
Squeeze all the juice from them into a saucepan
Add four ounces of loaf sugar with the same quantity of water as the juice
Stir on a slow fire until it becomes thickish
Remove it and let it cool
Proceed as above by pouring into a glass bowl and serving with ice and essence

name: Nectar
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: 6 Ounces of Fine White Pulverized Sugar
1 Ounce of the Fresh Zest of Lemon
½ Drachm of Tincture of Vanilla
steps: Pound to a powder all the ingredients which require it, mix with the honey, benzoin, etc., pour over the alcohol, and steep for fifteen days.
Distill the liquor till it is reduced to four quarts, using a water bath, or bain-marie, for the distillation.
Make a syrup of six pounds of fine white sugar, add the Vanilla, color a deep red with Cochineal, and add to the liquor.
Blend and shake well, bottle and keep in a cool place.

name: Nevi Archer
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound or so of flour
half or three-quarters of a pound of scalded fresh butter
three or four tablespoonfuls of cream
two or three tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar
steps: Work lightly in a basin a pound or so of flour, with half or three-quarters of a pound of scalded fresh butter
Add two or three eggs, three or four tablespoonfuls of cream, a little salt, two or three tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar
Work all together well to form a nice stiff paste
Make it into cakes, or in any shape you please
Arrange them in a buttered baking-tin
Egg over, and bake a nice brown in the oven
Sprinkle some powdered sugar over, and serve

name: Nevi Digher
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: one or two tablespoonfuls of tomato sauce
half a teacup of wine vinegar
half a teacup of olive oil
steps: Get any fish you fancy and clean it well
Cut three or four onions in thin slices and mix them with a plate of picked parsley
Lay half on the bottom of a stewpan
Place the fish over and the other half of the onions and parsley on the top
Add sufficient salt and pepper, one or two tablespoonfuls of tomato sauce, half a teacup of wine vinegar, the same quantity of olive oil, and one of water
Set the pan on a charcoal fire and let it simmer gently until the fish is cooked
Dish it up and serve

name: Nevi Diglier
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound and six ounces of the best fresh butter
a quarter of a pound of flour
a quarter of a pound of rice-flour
a quarter of a pound of wheat-starch
two pints and a half of boiling syrup
a pint and a half of boiling milk
steps: Set on a charcoal fire a stewpan with a pound and six ounces of the best fresh butter
When melted, add gradually a quarter of a pound of flour, ditto of rice-flour, and the same of wheat-starch, and keep stirring until the flour becomes a gold colour
Add six ounces of skinned almonds, and stir for a few minutes longer
Pour two pints and a half of boiling syrup over, as above, with a pint and a half of boiling milk
Instantly put the cover over the pan, and let it remain for fifteen minutes
Stir it well, dish up, sprinkle some rose-water over, with a little powdered cinnamon, and serve

name: Nevi Higher
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: one or two pounds of lamb
six or seven dozens of young okras
juice of one or two lemons
three cups of mutton or beef broth
steps: Cut one or two pounds of lamb in pieces about the size of walnuts
Place them in a stewpan with an ounce of fresh butter, a small teaspoonful of salt, and half a teacup of water
Put on the fire
When boiling, stir round with a wooden spoon for about twelve minutes, or until it forms a whitish thick gravy at the bottom
Lay the pieces of meat on the bottom of a rather deep and circular baking-pan
Over which lay regularly six or seven dozens of young okras, together with three or four finely-sliced onions, fried partly brown in fresh butter
Add the gravy, with the juice of one or two lemons, three cups of either mutton or beef broth, and a little salt
Bake it in a very hot oven until the okras are quite soft and nicely brown
Turn it gently on to a dish, without spoiling the shape, sprinkle a little cinnamon over, and serve

name: Noodle Soup with Chicken and Mushrooms
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Put the noodles into boiling water, and boil until they float on the surface.
Quickly place in cold water and stir.
Put again into boiling water for 1 minute.
Put into a clean bowl containing the oil, sesamum-seed oil, Chinese sauce, and a little pepper.
Cut the chicken, mushrooms, and water chestnuts into pieces 1½ inches long. Cook until done. Mix together and add Chinese gravy.
Divide the noodles into individual portions, and into each bowl pour enough boiling primary soup to cover.
Add the chicken gravy and serve.

name: Noodles
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: small spoonful of clear soup stock
steps: Beat one or more eggs and add a pinch of salt
Add as much flour as the egg will absorb
Add a small spoonful of clear soup stock and mix with the fingers into a soft, smooth dough, adding more flour as needed
Roll out as thin as possible and let stand for a few minutes
Roll over and over carefully into a long thin roll
Cut thin slices from the end of the roll
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Nut Cake
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: 1 teaspoon soda dissolved in 3 tablespoons hot water
steps: Cream butter and sugar
Add eggs
Add flour
Add dates and walnuts
Dissolve soda in hot water and add
Bake

name: Nut Cookies
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cream butter and sugar; add eggs, flour, baking powder, salt, milk and nuts; flavor with vanilla.
Drop a teaspoonful on buttered pans about two inches apart; if too thick, add a little more milk.

name: Oat Flakes
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: sugar and cream, or simply cream or milk
steps: Put the quart of water into a porcelain-lined saucepan, and let it come to a boil
Add the salt, and when it is boiling stir in gradually the oat flakes
Keep stirring to prevent burning
Let the preparation boil for about fifteen or twenty minutes
Serve with sugar and cream, or simply cream or milk

name: Omelette Soufflee
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
ingredientsText: five yolks and two whites of eggs
steps: Fry the eggs as directed for sweet omelet, using about five yolks and two whites, all of which require being finely beaten and strained
Soften a little preserve by holding it over the fire, or mixing a little warm water with it
Spread it slightly over the omelette
Whisk the remainder of the whites to a froth with white sugar
Lay the whisked whites on the preserve
Slide the omelette onto a hot dish
Double it and serve directly

name: Onigara Yaki (Broiled Lobster)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Wash the lobster carefully in cold water.
Place in boiling, salted water, and boil very slowly for one hour.
Remove from the saucepan, and immediately throw into cold water.
Cut in two pieces lengthwise, and dip each half in syou sauce.
Place upon gridiron, and toast well both back and front, taking minute care not to blacken skin and fins.
Once again cover with syou sauce, sprinkle with sanshi spice and pepper, and serve.

name: Orange Biscuits
author: Source author unknown
steps: Beat the eggs and sugar to a cream.
Add the flour gradually, and the juice and zest of the orange.
Beat well.
Bake on paper sheets, in the form of small wafers, very thinly spread, in a moderate oven, to a light color.

name: Orange Cream
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Take the juice of 4 oranges, and the rinds of 2, grated, the yolks of 8 eggs
Mix it well together and stir it over a chafing dish of coals
Add 1/2 a pint of cream, and stir it all one way

name: Orange Jelly
author: Source author unknown
steps: Proceed in exactly the same manner as for Lemon Jelly.

name: Orange Marmalade No. 1
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: small yellow oranges, size of limes
steps: Take small yellow oranges the size of limes. Peel and cover with water, letting them stand all night.
In the morning pour off the water.
Take out every seed if you desire sweet marmalade; if you like it bitter, leave some seeds. Be careful to save all the juice.
To every cup of the fruit add three cups of water.
Then to every cup of this mixture add one cup of sugar and boil until it jellies.
Put a little in a saucer on ice and don't boil beyond the jelly point, if you want it clear.

name: Orangeade
author: Source author unknown
steps: Squeeze out the juice of an orange
Pour boiling water on a little of the peel and cover it close
Boil water and sugar to a thin syrup and skim it
When cold, mix all together with as much water as will make a rich drink
Strain through a jelly-bag and ice

name: Otra Masa para Pasteles (Another Dough for Pastries)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: 1 and a half pounds of flour
juice of half a lemon (for icing)
steps: To 1 and a half pounds of flour add 2 ounces of ground sugar, 1 egg yolk, 1 ounce of good oil, 1 ounce of lard, and saffron for coloring
Add necessary water and make the dough
Make pastries as described in previous recipes
For icing, if desired: make an icing with 1 pound of sifted sugar, 3 well-beaten egg whites, and the juice of half a lemon
Mix all ingredients together and brush onto pastries with feathers before putting in the oven
After baking, if desired, sprinkle with small candies and return to the oven for a short time

name: Our Currie
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one tablespoonful and a half of currie powder
one lemon or one tablespoonful of vinegar
a quarter of a pound of butter
steps: Skin a moderate sized fowl, and cut it up

Put it into a stewpan with one sliced onion, and another previously fried brown, one clove of garlic, one teaspoonful of salt, one tablespoonful and a half of currie powder, and the juice of one lemon, or one tablespoonful of vinegar
Add a small piece of mint
Cover the meat with water or gravy, and let it stew very slowly for an hour and a half
Add a quarter of a pound of butter, and let it stew an hour and a half more

name: Owa Okashi
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Roast sweet rice over an open fire, same as popcorn.
Mix with goma seeds, and hold together in pressed bars with barley sugar.

name: Oyster Soup
author: Source author unknown
steps: In purchasing the oysters, be careful to make the vendor add the oyster juice when intended for soup
Drain the oysters through a colander and set them over the ice box to keep fresh and cold
Strain the liquor and put it into a soup kettle, adding the chopped parsley and pepper-corns
Let it come to a boil
Boil the milk separately in a saucepan, as boiling the milk and oyster juice together is likely to curdle the milk
When the milk comes to a boil, add to the oyster juice and put in the tablespoonful of butter
Stir the soup constantly, throwing in the oysters and continuing to stir until it comes to a boil again
Under no circumstances allow the oysters to boil, as that destroys their flavor and makes them tough
Watch for the ruffling of the edges, which indicates the right condition
At this point the soup must be served immediately
Serve with sliced lemon and oyster or wafer crackers

name: Oysters Stewed With Champagne
author: Lafcadio Hearn
ingredientsText: a quarter of a pound of butter
grated bread which has been toasted, beaten and sifted
steps: Put into a silver chafing dish a quarter of a pound of butter
Lay in a quart of oysters
Strew over them grated bread which has been toasted, beaten and sifted
Some cut parsley and a little pepper and salt
Cover the top with bits of butter cut thin
Pour on a pint of champagne
Cover and cook
This may be done in a pan or oven

name: Pan Bread
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: Flour Sufficient to Make a Smooth Dough
⅛ Ounces of Sugar, If Desired
steps: Make the same dough as for Bakers' Bread, only work the loaves twice over.
Then put them in the oven and dredge lightly with flour.
As they begin to rise make a light paste of flour and water or egg and water and spread very lightly over them.
This is brushed lightly with lard, to keep from getting too crusty.
Bake in a rather hotter oven than the other bread.

name: Partridge Hash
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Cut the partridges, water chestnuts, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots into very small pieces. Cut the lettuce into threads.
Fry the chopped partridges in a hot, oiled pan.
Add the ginger juice and Fun Wine.
Add the vegetables and mix well.
Add enough primary soup to cover and cook until done.
Add Chinese gravy and remove from the stove at once. Salt to suit the taste.
Serve on top of the lettuce. Use the Chinese ham dice and fried noodles as a garnish.

name: Partridge, Quail, or Lark Braised (Perdiz, codorniz, cotovia refogadas)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one chalice of juice from land orange
steps: Take the bird, rub it with salt and pepper, and wrap it in strips of bacon
place it in a pan with one pound of fat beef, salt, pepper, parsley, cilantro, onion leaves, one cup water, and one chalice of juice from land orange
cover the pan and let it boil for one hour over moderate heat
then braise one tablespoon of wheat flour in two tablespoons of butter
fry the bird in this mixture and immediately add the broth in which the bird was cooked
let it cook for another half hour and serve

name: Partridges with Soubise Sauce
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Prepare partridges as for roasting
Fill each partridge with a chopped Bombay onion previously boiled in milk seasoned with spiced pepper, salt, and rolled in a slice of boiled bacon
Make a broth with the giblets of the birds, any scraps you may have, a slice of lean bacon, an onion cut into quarters, a few pepper corns, and a seasoning of salt and pepper
Simmer the partridges in the broth until perfectly tender, about three-quarters of an hour
Take them out and drain them, replacing them in the hot pan in which they were done, with the cover on
Strain the liquor in which the birds have been cooked
Simmer four large Bombay onions in milk till tender, drain them, chop them up very fine, and pass them through the sieve
Make a rich puree with melted butter and the stock aforesaid
When boiling hot, dish the birds and pour the onion puree over them
Serve garnished with curls of crisply fried bacon, with a spoonful of cream added if possible

name: Pasteis de Nata (Cream Pastries)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Beat four cups of milk cream with ten egg yolks, one spoonful of sugar, and lemon zest
Bring to a boil, stir and fill the crusts with this mixture
Place in the oven, and when baked, serve covered with sugar and powdered cinnamon

name: Pastel de Queso (Cheese Pie)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Make the pastry with real dough (without sugar)
When moistened with eggs, mix in grated cheese or cheese cut into pieces
Proceed as for other pastries
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Pato Ensopado com Nabos (Duck Stewed with Turnips)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Wrap the duck in wheat flour and fry it in fat

name: Pdlude
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Dissolve two pounds of white sugar in a stewpan with two quarts of water
Add about five ounces of wheat starch
Stir it well
When as smooth as milk, put it on a moderate charcoal fire
Continually stir it for about three hours, or until it forms a smooth substance, but not too thick
Add a few drops of the essence of rose or orange-flower
Stir it for a few minutes longer
Pour it into a mould previously oiled with almond-oil
Put it on ice, or in a cool place, till firm
When ready, dip the mould in warm water and turn it out
Serve (You can ornament the top with some skinned pistachios or almonds)

name: Peach Pickles
author: Lafcadio Hearn
steps: Remove the down with a brush like a clothes brush from ripe, sound, cling-stone peaches
Make a gallon of good vinegar hot
Add to it four pounds of brown sugar
Boil and skim it clear
Stick five or six cloves into each of the peaches, then pour the hot vinegar over them
Cover the vessel and set it in a cold place for eight or ten days
Drain off the vinegar, make it hot, skim it, and again turn it over the peaches
Let them become cold, then put them into glass jars and secure as directed for preserves

name: Peach Preserve
author: Source author unknown
steps: Clean the peaches, slit them with a silver or plated knife, and remove the stones
Have a very strong syrup ready, and while it is boiling hot throw in the peaches, and let them stand over a slow fire for six to eight hours
Remove them from the fire, and twelve hours after drain off the syrup and reboil it
Return the fruit into the syrup, and if it shows any disposition to ferment, boil it again
When satisfied it will not ferment any more, add a little brandy, say a wineglassful to every fifty peaches, and boil the whole over a slow fire for two hours
Bottle when quite cold
The kernels from the stones may be put in if desired

name: Peaches and Apricots in Brandy
author: Lafcadio Hearn
ingredientsText: Nice smooth peaches not too ripe
Sugar in weight equal to the fruit
Half a pint of water to each pound of sugar
Equal quantities of syrup and French brandy
steps: Put peaches in a vessel and cover them with weak lye
Take them out in two hours, and wipe carefully to get off the down and outside skin, and lay them in cold water
Weigh the fruit, add their weight in sugar, and half a pint of water to each pound of sugar
Boil and skim this syrup, put in the peaches
When the syrup is clear of scum, let them boil for twenty minutes or half an hour
Take them out and lay them on dishes to cool
Boil the syrup for an hour longer, or until reduced one-half and quite thick
When cold, put the peaches or apricots in jars, and cover them with equal quantities of the syrup and French brandy

name: Peppermints
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil sugar, water and cream of tartar three minutes, or until it begins to thread.
Remove from fire.
Add peppermint to taste.
Beat it until it begins to thicken.
Drop on waxed paper.

name: Perdices Asadas a la Parrilla (Grilled Partridges)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: After cleaning, place the raw partridges on the grill, rolling them with oil.
Roll them in breadcrumbs and return to the grill so they brown.
Serve with lettuce salad, unpicked.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Perdizes, Codornizes, etc. Ensopadas com Guandús (Partridges, Quail, etc. Stewed with Pigeon Peas)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Brown one spoon of cornmeal flour with two spoons of fat
Add the bird cut into pieces and turn on all sides
Add a portion of pigeon peas cooked in water and salt
Stir and boil for another half hour
Add a glass of vinegar at the end and serve

name: Perfection Salad
author: Source author unknown
steps: Soak the gelatine in cold water five minutes.
Add vinegar, lemon juice, boiling water, sugar and salt.
Strain and when beginning to set add remaining ingredients.
Put on ice for twenty-four hours, and serve with mayonnaise dressing.

name: Peru Assado com Molho de Leite (Turkey Roasted with Milk Sauce)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take the turkey and fill the breast with its liver and a piece of calf liver passed through a sieve and mixed with a handful of bread crumbs moistened with red wine
Add two tablespoons of sugar, grated nutmeg, cardamom, and a little salt
Spit the turkey and roast

name: Perú Assado com Pinhões (Roast Turkey with Pine Nuts)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Soak the turkey, brushed with salt, garlic, onion and lemon juice, for four hours.
Then fill it with cooked and peeled pine nuts, cut cooked eggs, half a dozen sliced bananas and peeled lemon slices without seeds.
Place it in a pan lined with bacon and roast it.
When cooked, serve it with its own sauce after removing the fat.

name: Pescoço de Carneiro Assado na Grelha (Grilled Lamb Neck)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut the neck meat into slices
Place over fire with cold water, salt, parsley, and onion leaves
Boil for half an hour
Remove and wrap with bread crumbs
Cover with a little melted butter
Roast on the grill
Serve with spicy sauce

name: Petits Pois au Beurre
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Serve boiled or jugged peas with a pat of fresh butter melted in a small sauce-pan and mixed with them at the last moment

name: Piccalili
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
steps: Pickle gherkins, French beans, and cauliflower, separately, as already directed
Cut the other vegetables (carrots, onions, capsicums, white cabbage, celery) in small pieces, and soak in brine; boil the carrots in it to make them tender
Into half a gallon of vinegar put two ounces of ginger, one of whole black pepper, one of whole allspice, and one of bruised chillies, three ounces of shalots, and one ounce of garlic
Boil together nearly twenty minutes
Mix a little of it in a basin, with two ounces of flour of mustard and one ounce of turmeric
Stir it in gradually with the rest
Pour the liquor over the vegetables

name: Pickled Beef Tongue
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Soak in cold water one-half hour.
Crush a piece of saltpetre, size of walnut, one teacup of salt, one teaspoon of pepper, three small cloves of garlic cut fine; mix seasoning.
Drain water off tongue.
With a pointed knife prick tongue; rub in seasoning.
Put tongue in crock; add the balance of salt, etc.; cover with plate and weight.
Allow to stand from four to five days.
Without washing off the seasoning, boil in fresh water until tender.

name: Pickled Cantaloupe or Muskmelons
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: 3 pounds and a half white sugar per dozen small cantaloupes
steps: Take fine, ripe melons, pare, take out the seeds and wash
Cut into slices about three inches long and two inches wide
Lay them in a stone jar and cover with vinegar for twenty-four hours or longer
Lay the fruit on a clean board to drip
Throw away one quart of the vinegar to each quart remaining
Boil the spices, vinegar and sugar, adding a pint of fresh vinegar to the old
When well skimmed put in the melons, boil fifteen minutes, twenty is still better
Take out the fruit, put it in jars and boil the syrup awhile longer
Skim it again and pour boiling hot upon the fruit
Seal when cold

name: Pickled Cucumbers
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Make a brine of salt and water strong enough to bear an egg
Pour it over the cucumbers and cover them with cabbage leaves
Let them stand for a week until they are quite yellow
Pour off the water
Take a porcelain kettle and cover the bottom with fresh leaves
Put in the cucumbers with a piece of alum
Cover them closely with vine leaves and then with a dish or cloth to keep in the steam
Fill up kettle with clear water and hang it over the fire, but not in a blaze
Keep the fire under the kettle moderate and keep them over the fire in a slow heat for several hours
If they are not then a pretty green, repeat the process
When they are well greened, take them out of the kettle and drain them on a sieve
Put them into a clean stone jar
Spice the vinegar with cloves, mace, mustard seed and sugar
Boil well for 5 or 6 minutes

name: Pies de Cerdo en Escabeche (Pork Feet in Pickle Sauce)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Wash the feet and cut them in half.
Cook them well and remove the bones, taking care not to remove any meat.
Roll them in flour, dip in beaten egg, and fry.
For the sauce: brown some garlic in lard, then add water and a little good vinegar.
Grind a little clove, pepper, and saffron.
Thicken with a little toasted bread ground in lard.
Add the spices, cooked sweet lime slices, orange leaves, and a small piece of panela, so that the vinegar stands out.
Once seasoned, place the fried feet in this sauce.
Serve sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds on top.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Pigeon Chop Suey
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Take the bones out of the pigeons and cut the meat into thin pieces. Put into a hot, oiled pan and fry for 5 minutes.
Cut the secondary vegetables into thin pieces. Put into a hot pan and fry for 2 minutes. Add water and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the secondary vegetables to the pigeon fragments. Mix well.
Add primary soup and cook for 5 minutes.
Add Chinese gravy.

name: Pigeon Hash
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Cut into very small pieces the pigeons, water chestnuts, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots. Cut the lettuce into threads.
Fry the chopped pigeon in a hot, oiled pan.
Add the ginger juice and Fun Wine.
Add the vegetables and mix well.
Add enough primary soup to cover and cook until done.
Add Chinese gravy and remove from the stove at once. Salt to suit the taste.
Serve on top of the lettuce. Use the Chinese ham dice and fried noodles as a garnish.

name: Pillau
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a pound and a half of bacon
steps: Wash two pounds of rice, boil it in a little water with half a pound of butter, some salt, peppercorns, cloves, and mace
Keep the saucepan closely covered until the rice is sufficiently cooked
Have ready a pound and a half of bacon, and two fowls nicely boiled
Place the bacon in the middle of a dish, and the fowls on each side
Cover over with the boiled rice, and garnish with hard boiled eggs and fried whole onions

name: Pineapple Chicken
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Cut the chicken, pineapple, peppers, celery, and ginger into pieces 1 1/2 inches long.
Break the eggs into the chicken and mix well together with a little cornstarch and salt. Then put into boiling oil and fry until all becomes yellow.

Put the pineapple, pepper, celery, and ginger into a hot, oiled pan and fry for 2 minutes. Add the fried chicken. Mix well and add the Fun Wine. Cook over a hot fire for 5 minutes; then add enough primary soup to cover and cook until about one cup of liquid is left.
Add the vinegar and a little sugar.
Pour Chinese gravy over the chicken.

name: Pineapple Duck
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Cut into small oblong pieces the duck, pineapple, peppers, celery, and ginger.
Break the eggs into the duck and mix well together with a little cornstarch and salt.
Put the pineapple, pepper, celery, and ginger into a hot, oiled pan and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the fried duck. Mix well and add the Fun Wine. Have a hot fire. After 5 minutes add enough primary soup to cover the substances and cook until about one cup of liquid is left.
Add the vinegar and sugar and mix with Chinese gravy.

name: Pineapple Ice Cream— No. 2
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: ½ cup to pint of fruit
steps: Pare a fresh, ripe pineapple, remove the eyes and core, then chop fine and sprinkle with half a cup of sugar to a pint of fruit
Let it stand for half an hour, then press through a strainer
Add lemon juice and more sugar if needed
Mix with half frozen ice cream (plain) and finish freezing

name: Pirinj Chorbassi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: three or four ounces of the best rice
yolk of one or two eggs
steps: Wash three or four ounces of the best rice
Put it into a stewpan, with a little salt, and three or four pints of broth
Set the pan on the fire, and let it boil gently till the rice is soft
Add the yolk of one or two eggs prepared as in Terbiyeli Jigher Chorbassi
Pour the soup into a tureen, sprinkle a little cinnamon over, and serve

name: Pirmj-Unu Helivassi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a pound of the best fresh butter
a pound and a half of rice-flour
a quarter of a pound of skinned almonds
a pint and a half of boiling syrup
a pint and a half of boiling milk
steps: Put in a stewpan a pound of the best fresh butter, and scald it
Then remove it from the fire: when a little cold, add by degrees a pound and a half of rice-flour
Set it again on the fire, and keep stirring for twenty-five minutes, or until the butter appears on the surface of the flour, and the flour swells up like grains of gunpowder
Then add a quarter of a pound of skinned almonds, and stir it for a few minutes longer
Then immediately add a pint and a half of boiling syrup, previously prepared of white sugar and water, as in No. 159, and the same quantity of boiling milk
Instantly put the cover over, and let it remain for about five minutes
Then stir it well with a wooden fork, dish it up in spoonfuls, and let it bear the impression of the spoon
Sprinkle a little powdered sugar over, and serve

name: Pish Pash
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a blade or two of mace
steps: Put half a fowl into a saucepan with about a quart of water, let it boil to rags, then strain off the meat
To the liquor add the other half fowl cut up into joints, half a teacupful of rice, a blade or two of mace, and pepper and salt to taste
Let this stew until the fowl is very tender and nearly all the gravy is absorbed, then send to table

name: Plum Pudding No. 2
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: a half box of raisins and currants
one and one-half cups of sugar
steps: Chop a half box of raisins and currants, one-quarter pound of citron, and one-quarter pound of suet very fine
Mix with two eggs, one and one-half cups of sugar, a wineglass of brandy, two cups of cider, one teaspoon of cinnamon and ground cloves
When all these are well mixed add enough flour with a teaspoon of baking-powder in it to thicken well
Cook in a greased mold and allow to steam for three hours

name: Pocket Books For Tea
author: Lafcadio Hearn
ingredientsText: a cup of light and warm yeast
a cup of warm, sweet milk
a spoonful of grated orange peel and nutmeg
a lump of butter as big as an egg
steps: Take a cup of light and warm yeast, a cup of warm, sweet milk, two eggs beaten, a cup of sugar, a spoonful of grated orange peel and nutmeg
add to this, flour enough to make a thin batter
set it in a warm place to rise
pour this batter into sifted flour, enough to form into a rather stiff dough
add salt and a lump of butter as big as an egg
Work it thoroughly
set it in a tureen to rise again
When it is risen, flour the board and roll out the dough half an inch thick
smear the surface with butter
cut into strips about six inches long, and two inches wide
fold them over and over
lay them within an inch of each other on a warm and greased baking tin, or pan
swab the tops over with warmed butter and a beaten egg
set them to rise, which will require an hour
Just before you put them in the oven, sift some sugar over them

name: Pollos en Salsa de Betabel y Manzana (Chicken in Beet and Apple Sauce)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Fry strips of ham and sliced chorizo in lard and remove them
In the same fat, fry chopped garlic, cooked and ground beet and apple with appropriate salt
Season with ground cloves, pepper, and cinnamon
Add capers and cooked small onions
Place the chicken with its broth, the fried ham and chorizo, and a bit of wine
When well simmered and seasoned, add cured tornachilesand olives before serving
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Pombos Assados na Grelha (Grilled Squabs)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Clean the squabs and cut them in half along the spine
Flatten them by beating with a piece of wood
Roast them in hot butter
Cover both sides with a good layer of breadcrumbs, seasoning with salt and pepper
Grill on both sides
Serve with the following sauce: boil one half cup meat broth with three tablespoons vinegar, two pinches chopped onion and the same amount of parsley, salt, pepper and one teaspoon mustard powder
For this preparation, the youngest squabs should be sought

name: Pop Corn
author: Source author unknown
steps: Into a large deep frying pan put a tablespoon of lard or butter and half a teaspoon salt.
Heat pan and when very hot throw in a handful of pop corn and cover.
Shake pan gently while corn is popping.
When corn is all popped the fat will be gone.

name: Porco do Matto com Ameixas (Wild Boar with Prunes)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cook the meat and scald in salted water
Fry afterwards in butter with a little wheat flour
Add a little rapadura, two dozen prunes, cinnamon, lemon peel, wine, and a little meat broth
Let boil and strain through a sieve
Place the meat in this sauce
Give it one more boil and serve

name: Pork Salad
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: 3 3/8 pounds string beans cut 2 inches long
steps: Boil the pork until done and place in cold water. Punch several small holes with a large needle. Gently squeeze the oil out of it. Change water until no oil is on the top.
Cut the pork into thin pieces 1/32 inch by 3/8 inch by 1 3/8 inches. Mix with salt to suit the taste, and with the mustard and vinegar.
Boil the string beans for 10 minutes. Put into a bowl, and add salt and enough vinegar.

name: Pork Soup
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: 2 cups lean pork cut into fragments
3 cups star melon cut into small pieces after the rind is removed
steps: Mix the pork, cornstarch, Chinese sauce, and salt
Bring the primary soup to a boil
Then add the pork mixture and the mushrooms, and cook for 1/2 hour
Ten minutes before taking soup off stove, add the melon

name: Portakal Elmassiyyessi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: five or six ounces of powdered sugar
a few drops of prepared cochineal
steps: Get six nice oranges, take off the rind of one of them, and remove the pith, place them in a basin, and squeeze the juice of the oranges in it
Put five or six ounces of powdered sugar in a saucepan with half a pint of water, and boil it until it becomes a syrup
Take it off, and add the juice and the rind of the oranges; put the saucepan again on the fire with the cover over
As soon as it begins to boil, skim it well, and add gradually a small teacup of water; let it boil one or two minutes longer
Add an ounce of isinglass, dissolved as directed; stir well, and pass it through a jelly-bag till clear
Add a few drops of prepared cochineal, and pour it in a mould; place it on ice until firm
Turn it out as before, and serve

name: Postre de Camote Blanco y Natillas (White Sweet Potato and Custard Dessert)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: Half pound of ground white sweet potato
steps: Make clarified syrup with six pounds of sugar
Add half pound of ground white sweet potato and half pound of ground almonds
When the paste begins to set, add a quarter of custard
Let it acquire the proper consistency
Put the paste on a platter with crumbled camote and ground cinnamon on top
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Postre de Queso (Cheese Dessert)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Put fresh cheese to soak, then grind it very finely, put it on a table, add three egg yolks and a handful of flour
Stir, knead and make some curious little figures or small rings that are fried in lard, then sprinkled with honey and arranged on a platter, decorating with sugar beads and cinnamon
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Postre de Yemas de Huevo, Bizcocho y Mantequilla (Dessert of Egg Yolks, Sponge Cake and Butter)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Cook milk with sugar
Beat egg yolks and mix with the cooked milk
Take a cold slab of the best sponge cake and cut it into slices
In a dish, lay down a layer of slices and on top of each slice place layers of butter, adding cinnamon and toasted sesame seeds to each one, until filling the platter
Once well layered high, pour the milk with egg yolks over it until well soaked
Place fire above and below, both not too intense, and leave until it sets like a cake
Decorate with toasted sesame seeds and ground cinnamon on top
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Pot-au-Feu
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: 4 pounds soup-meat (3 pounds flesh to 1 pound bone)
A couple of large white onions
Two large or three small carrots
steps: Put a piece of soup-meat of four pounds weight, in the proportion of three pounds of flesh to one of bone, tightly bound with a string, with two ounces of salt and the bones separately broken up, into a stock pot filled with water, so as to completely cover the meat.
Put the pot by the side of the fire and let it become gradually heated.
As this takes place, a scum will form upon the surface which must be carefully removed as it rises.
When nearly boiling, a coffee cupful of cold water should be thrown into the pot to accelerate the rising of the scum.
Keep the water from boiling point until all the scum is removed.

Put into the saucepan the following vegetables which should have been previously carefully cleaned and cut up: a couple of large white onions, a clove of garlic, two large or three small carrots, two or three turnips, six leeks, one head of celery, a bunch of curly parsley, and two cloves in the onion.
Put in, tied up in a piece of muslin, some thyme, marjoram, and a handful of whole pepper (a tea-spoonful each of dried thyme and marjoram will be quite enough).
Watch the vegetables carefully, and remove them when they are done.
Remove the muslin bag also.
Put in a dessert-spoonful of sugar, a table-spoonful of Harvey sauce, and two of mushroom ketchup.
Let it simmer slowly from three to four hours.
Strain the soup into a basin.

name: Potage A La Nivernaise
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Set your soup meat for stock as usual for a clear soup
Take four good-sized carrots, wash them well
Cut out of them a number of thickish pieces the size and shape of a pigeon's egg, or a little smaller
When you have cut a couple of dozen such pieces, throw all the scraps and trimmings of the carrots into the stock pot to flavour the soup well
Shortly before serving time, melt a table-spoonful of butter in a frying-pan
Put into it the carrot pieces, which should have been all but boiled till soft in the soup
Toss them about over the fire adding a salt-spoonful of powdered sugar with a dusting of pepper and of salt
Moisten the pan with a spoonful of stock as the butter is absorbed
When done, the pieces of carrot will be almost glazed
Put the glazed carrots into the tureen and pour the soup over them

name: Potage a la Puree de Becassines
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: a dessert-spoonful of red currant jelly
a couple of ounces of butter
a tea-spoonful of red currant jelly
steps: Make a good strong stock for six basins (at least a quart and a half) with a shin of beef, and one good-sized chicken cut up into fragments; flavour it highly with sweet herbs, and mixed vegetables.
Take six snipes, and lightly roast them: pick the whole of the meat from their breasts, and save it; mash the bones that remain, and put them in a bowl with the trails.

When the stock is quite ready, strain it, return it to the pot, and throw into it the bowlful of mashed snipe bones, two glasses of port wine, a dessert-spoonful of red currant jelly, and a dessert-spoonful of crystal-vinegar.
Let the contents of the pot simmer slowly for an hour and half, skimming off any scum that may rise.
Strain the liquor from the bones, and set it in a bowl to cool.
Pass the snipe meat that you saved through the mincing machine, and pound it thoroughly to a paste, using a little of the soup to help that operation.
Skim any fat that may have risen on the surface of your soup.
Take a roomy sauce-pan, place it on the fire, put a couple of ounces of butter into it, stir into the butter a tablespoonful of flour, work it to a smooth paste.
Add, by degrees both soup and snipe paste, keeping the spoon at work the whole time.
When all is expended, let the puree reach the boil in order to thicken properly.
Add a glass of port, a tea-spoonful of red currant jelly, and the juice of a good lime.
Break a raw egg into a cup, saving the yolk carefully; mix a little of the soup with the yolk.

name: Potato Pudding
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: four tablespoons of blanched and pounded almonds
half a pound of grated potatoes which have been cooked the day previous
steps: Stir the yolks of eight eggs with a cup of sugar
Add four tablespoons of blanched and pounded almonds, and grate in the peel of a lemon
Add also its juice
Have ready half a pound of grated potatoes which have been cooked the day previous
Last add the stiffly-beaten whites
Add one teaspoon of salt
Grease your pudding form well, pour in the mixture and bake
Set in a pan of boiling water in the oven
The water in the pan must not reach higher than half way up the pudding form
Bake for half an hour
When done turn out on a platter
Serve with a wine or chocolate sauce

name: Potato Puff
author: Source author unknown
steps: Put cold mashed potatoes in a saucepan; add milk; stir and beat until the potatoes are hot and smooth.
Take from fire; fold in the well-beaten whites of two eggs.
Heap in a baking dish and brown quickly in a hot oven.
Serve with roast or broiled beef.

name: Potato Salad, No. 2
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
ingredientsText: one quart of small Bermuda potatoes
steps: Wash and scrub the potatoes thoroughly in cold water
Put them in a kettle with enough cold water, slightly salted, just to cover them
Stand them over a brisk fire with the kettle covered until the water begins to boil
Turn down the heat, lift the cover of the kettle slightly, and let the potatoes cook slowly till done
Drain off the water and stand the potatoes where they will get cold, but do not put them in a refrigerator
When quite cold, peel the potatoes and slice them very thin in a salad bowl
To every two layers of potato slices sprinkle over a very light layer of white onions sliced very thin
Pour over the salad a French dressing made of equal parts of oil and vinegar with tarragon vinegar, salt and pepper
When ready to serve, cover the surface of the salad with a stiff mayonnaise in which a suggestion of cream has been mixed
Ornament with quarters of hard-boiled eggs, boiled beets cut in fancy slices and a fringe of parsley around the edge of the bowl

name: Potato Yeast
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Peel and boil soft a large Irish potato
Rub it through a sieve
Add an equal quantity of flour
Make it liquid with hop tea
When a little warmer than new milk, add a gill of good yeast
Stir it well
Keep it closely covered in a small pitcher

name: Potatoes Au Gratin
author: Source author unknown
steps: Chop cold boiled potatoes rather fine; season with salt and pepper.
Put them in a baking dish; pour over sufficient cream sauce to just cover.
Dust the top with grated plain or Parmesan cheese, and put in a hot oven until nicely browned.

name: Potatoes Sautees
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Boil your potatoes
Slice them moderately thickly
Toss them in plenty of butter in your frying-pan till they colour nicely
Pour the brown butter over them
Give them a dust of salt

name: Potted Prawns
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: a few drops of anchovy sauce
steps: Select some nice sized prawns
Boil them
Pick out very carefully all the grit and that black line which runs straight down the back and underneath every prawn
Wash them afterwards in cold water
Pour a lot of water over them as they lie on the top of your sieve
Dry them
Toss them in a little melted butter in a frying-pan until they have absorbed the butter
Pass through the mincing machine
Pound them thoroughly in the mortar
Press them through the wire sieve
Season the paste with salt, white and red pepper, a few drops of anchovy sauce, and a little pounded mace
Work the whole together with some nice freshly made butter till thoroughly incorporated
Set it in an earthenware jar
Pour a spoonful of melted butter over the surface

name: Prawn Currie
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: half a pint of good stock or gravy soup
steps: Mix one tablespoonful of currie powder and one teaspoonful of flour, with a little water, into a smooth paste
Stir it into half a pint of good stock or gravy soup
Add a large onion, sliced and fried, and simmer it in a stewpan until it thickens
Have ready two dozen large prawns, taken whole from their shells, and put them into the stewpan
Simmer for a quarter of an hour, stirring occasionally, care being taken not to break the prawns
Then add two ounces of butter, and a tablespoonful of vinegar, and simmer for a quarter of an hour longer

name: Preserved Cherries
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Lay them with the sugar the night before
Drain off the syrup to boil the sugar with before you put in the cherries
Keep them as whole as you can
Put them in pots
Cover with the syrup
Cover down the same as the others
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Preserved Cucumbers or Melons
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: half an ounce of powdered ginger
the juice and rind of a lemon
steps: Take large cucumbers or melons, such as are green, put them into a jar of strong salt and water, with vine leaves on the top
Set them by the fireside until they turn yellow, then wash them
Put them on a slow fire in alum and water, covered with vine leaves
Let them boil till they become green, take them off and leave them in the liquor until they are cold
Quarter them and take out the soft part and seeds, if there are any
