Put them in cold spring water, changing it twice a day for three days
Have ready a syrup made as follows: To one pound of loaf sugar add half an ounce of powdered ginger, and as much water as will moisten it
Boil it and skim it well
When it is quite free from scum and boiling fast, add the juice and rind of a lemon
When this syrup is quite cold pour it over the cucumber or melon
Should the syrup be too thin after standing two or three days, boil it again with a little more sugar
A spoonful of rum gives it the West Indian flavour

name: Preserved Peaches
author: Source author unknown
steps: Make a strong syrup, which boil and skim well
Have ready some fine peaches, gathered before they are over ripe
Rub the lint off them carefully with a cloth
Take a needle and run it down the seam of each peach to the depth of the skin, and place them in a jar, covering them with good brandy, and let them remain two hours
Take them out and put them into a preserving pan, so that each may lie singly
Pour the syrup over them, and boil them until they look clear, but be careful not to break them
Remove the peaches with a spoon into glasses, and when the syrup is cold, mix it with the brandy and pour it on the peaches
The glasses must be well tied down with a bladder, and the air carefully excluded

name: Preserved Pine
author: Source author unknown
steps: Make a syrup with one pound of white sugar to a quarter of a pint of water
Boil it until it becomes clear, skimming it carefully
Have ready a pine apple peeled and cut into slices
When the syrup is ready and boiling, put in the slices of pine, and simmer for about three quarters of an hour
Put into glasses or jars, and when cold tie down

name: Presunto à Ingleza (English-Style Ham)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: half pound of ground Indian pepper
four ounces of Indian pepper in grain
four ounces of juniper berries in grain
four pounds of molasses or muscovado sugar
steps: After cutting two hams, round them and cut the trimmings around them
Prick the skin with the tip of a knife so that the seasoning can penetrate them
Place ten pounds of salt, half pound of ground Indian pepper, and four ounces of saltpeter on a table
After rubbing them with this mixture, place them in a small tub, putting the rest of the salt on top, and leave them there for seven days

After this time, remove them, bring the brine to a boil, composed of water and the blood that came from the ham, skim well, and add serpol, bay leaf, two ounces of ginger, four ounces of Indian pepper in grain, the same amount of juniper berries in grain, marjoram, sage, oregano, and four pounds of molasses or muscovado sugar
Place the hams back in the tub, and when the brine is cold, pour it over them, and if it is not sufficient to cover the hams, add water and salt
Place a board with any weight on top to keep them in this brine for three weeks
After this time, remove them and place them in a press for twelve hours, and after draining, hang them in smoke
When they have taken on a beautiful color, rub them with wine mixed with vinegar to protect them from flies, then dry them for preservation

name: Princess Royal Custard
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: quarter of a pound Jordan almonds
essence of almonds or orange-flower water
steps: Beat up in a large deep bowl the yolks of eight fresh eggs
Dredge into it while beating up a dessertspoonful of corn-flour
Sweeten to taste with the best pounded loaf sugar
Add to it a quarter of a pound of Jordan almonds well bruised in a marble mortar
Pour the mixture into a clean newly-tinned copper pan
Stir into it a seer of good cold milk
Put the pan on the fire
Never cease stirring it, keeping the spoon as much as possible in the centre of the pan
Reduce the flame after it has boiled for fifteen minutes, and continue to boil for a few minutes longer, until the custard is of the consistency required
Fill the custard cups or glasses, leaving about half an inch space to fill up with the whites of the eggs, beaten up to a very light froth
Flavour it with a little essence of almonds, or orange-flower water

name: Prune Salad
author: Source author unknown
steps: Stew prunes until they are soft, without any sugar.
Cut carefully on the side and remove the pit.
Place a piece of English walnut inside and serve with mayonnaise dressing.

name: Prunes a la Chasseur
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: glass jar of best French plums (prunes)
steps: Buy a glass jar of the best French plums (prunes) and a bottle of good cherry brandy
Take out a few plums
Pour as much cherry brandy into the jar as the plums will admit
The next day you can add more, for the plums will absorb the brandy
Continue for a day or two
Finally cork it down for a fortnight or so
Serve at dessert
Never let the jar be empty, but re-fill it as the plums are eaten

name: Pudim de Fubá Mimoso (Fine Cornmeal Pudding)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Mix one quarter of butter with one pound of fine cornmeal, one spoon of polvilho, four eggs, one quarter of sugar
Add a portion of scalded raisins, lemon zest, salt and nutmeg
Add hot milk to form a thick mixture
Tie in a napkin
Place in a pot with boiling water
Boil until cooked
Serve with an appropriate sauce

name: Pudim de Rim de Vitela (Veal Kidney Pudding)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: half a pound of ground crackers
steps: Roast two veal kidneys
When cold, chop them very finely
Mix with half a pound of ground crackers, one quarter of sugar, six beaten eggs, a little salt and one cup of milk
Boil everything well in a saucepan
Place in a buttered mold
Bake in the oven and serve hot

name: Pudín de Almendra (Almond Pudding)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: one pound of peeled and ground almonds
steps: Make a syrup with six pounds of sugar, clarified with a straw, the juice of one lemon and one egg white
When at medium point, lower sixty-four egg yolks as for real eggs, and stir with four cuartillos of milk, then add to the syrup
Alternatively, put the sugar in the milk and let it boil on the fire; once cooled, add the yolks and mix one pound of peeled and ground almonds with two pounds of butter
Place a layer of sliced mamón in the dish, another of milk and another of almond mixture with butter, sprinkled well with ground cinnamon
Once the dish is filled in this manner, cover with beaten egg yolks and cook at two gentle fires, testing with a straw if the pudding is well cooked
To prevent sticking, brush constantly with butter using a feather
If desired, stud with peeled almonds dried in the sun
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Puli Cakes of Moog
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
steps: Keep some husked pulses of moog under water for two hours
Fry them, if desired, with a little ghee for a few minutes
Make a paste of them
Add salt and a little flour, if necessary, to make the paste stiff
Prepare Puli cakes as before stuffing them with kheer or the preparation of cocoa-nut
Fry till reddish brown with ghee

name: Pumpkin and Yellow Seeds
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Remove large seeds and spread them on paper.
Sprinkle with salt, and bake them until dry.

name: Punch a la Romain
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: two pounds of the best loaf sugar
two seers of cutcha, or raw ice
steps: Squeeze the juice out of eight juicy limes and four lemons or oranges
strain it through muslin
well mix with it two pounds of the best loaf sugar
beat to a light froth the whites of ten fresh eggs
add gradually to the sugared juice
pour the whole into a pewter vessel
place it in a tub containing two seers of cutcha, or raw ice, stirring it frequently to make it congeal
Ice two quarts of champagne
when required add it to the contents of the pewter vessel
mix all well together
serve in green or amber-coloured hock glasses

name: Puree de Tomates
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: six or eight good sized tomatoes
steps: Soup meat as usual for two
Make your stock from the soup meat
Choose an enamel-lined sauce-pan and throw in the tomatoes cut into quarters, dried basil, shredded onion, salt, garlic cloves, and a table-spoonful of butter
Cook the pieces of tomato until quite soft, stirring to prevent catching
Turn them out upon a sieve, pick out the garlic, and work the tomatoes through the sieve, saving the pulp in a bowl
When dinner time is at hand, melt an ounce of butter at the bottom of a sauce-pan
Work a dessert-spoonful of flour into it till smooth
Add a little stock and a little puree by degrees till exhausted
Let the soup come to the boil to thicken properly
Serve with croutons of fried bread

name: Quail Hash
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Cut the quail, water chestnuts, mushrooms, and bamboo shoots into very small pieces. Cut the lettuce into threads.
Fry the chopped quails in a hot, oiled pan.
Add the secondary vegetables and mix well.
Add enough primary soup to cover and cook until done.
Add Chinese gravy and remove from the stove at once. Salt to suit the taste.
Serve on top of the lettuce. Use the Chinese ham dice and fried noodles as a garnish.

name: Quick Coffee Cake
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Cream one-half cup of butter with one cup of sugar
Add three eggs, one and one-half cups of flour, two teaspoons of baking-powder, mixed with the flour, and one-half cup of milk
Mix well together
Bake in a long bread or cake pan, and have on top chopped almonds, sugar and cinnamon

name: Rabbit Pie
author: Lafcadio Hearn
ingredientsText: a half cup of brown gravy from veal or chicken
the juice of half a lemon
a piece of butter, as large as a hen's egg
steps: Season mushrooms, parsley, and shallots with pepper, salt, and thyme or sweet herbs
Cook them a light brown
Throw in a glass of white wine, a half cup of brown gravy from veal or chicken, and the juice of half a lemon
If you have no gravy on hand, add to the rabbits a cup of sweet milk, and a piece of butter, as large as a hen's egg
Toss all up on the fire fifteen or twenty minutes
Make a nice paste, line the sides of the pan
Pour in the stewed rabbit, and cover with paste
Bake until a light brown
Eat cold or hot

name: Rasa Puli
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
steps: Make a stiff dough of powdered rice with boiling water, adding the necessary amount of water at a time
Make medium balls
Stuff them with kheer or the preparation of cocoa-nut
Give them the shape of an almond
Fry in ghee
Immerse in a syrup of sugar till they are saturated

name: Ratafia Pudding
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Soak the cakes in 1/2 pint of almond milk
Beat in 6 eggs, leave out 3 whites
Grease and sugar your mould
Lay over it some orange marmalade
Turn in the mixture
Boil for an hour the same as the other puddings
Serve a sauce round
You can sometimes ornament these puddings with cut almonds
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Repolho Roxo Refogado (Braised Red Cabbage)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Chop a red cabbage finely
Blanch it and let it cool
Place two finely diced onions, parsley, two spoons of butter, salt, pepper and a spoon of sugar in a casserole
Let it boil and serve, placing on top a cup of red wine

name: Rice and Nut Candies
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: These are made chiefly of boiled rice pressed into balls with chopped nuts, tossed into boiling sirup, and then allowed to cool and harden.

name: Rice Cake with Butter
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Melt the butter in your pan, only warm, not to oil.
Add the sugar, stir it well till it is like a cream.
Break the eggs three at the time, and stir the paste all the time.
When all the eggs are worked in, add the ground rice and flour.
Bake it in a round tin buttered.
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Rice Caudle
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
steps: Boil half a pint of milk
Add a spoonful of ground rice mixed with a little milk till quite smooth
Stir it into the boiling milk
Let it simmer till it thickens
Carefully strain it and sweeten with white sugar

name: Ringo-Kan (Apple Jelly, Japanese Style)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Wash half a pound of seaweed jelly and soak it in water for about three hours, then squeeze it dry and break in small pieces into a pan with one and a half quarts of water.
Boil over medium heat.
Add three quarters of a pound of sugar, stirring the while, and a pinch of salt.
Prepare two big, tart apples by peeling and removing the cores, then rub them on a nutmeg grater until they are reduced to powder.
Transfer jelly to another saucepan, strain it, and mix with powdered apple.

name: Rins de Carneiro Assados (Roasted Lamb Kidneys)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Remove fat from kidneys and scald in hot water
Split in two halves
Dust with salt and pepper
Place on grill and roast, dripping a little butter on them
Turn to roast the other side
Serve with salad

name: Risen Waffles
author: Source author unknown
steps: Scald the milk, add the butter, and let it grow tepid.
Sift the flour and salt together, and add the milk and butter, and finally the yeast.
Beat all continuously for five or ten minutes, and then cover well and set in a warm place for about two hours.
Beat the whites and the yolks of the eggs separately, and add first the yolks to the batter, after it has risen well, and then add the whites.
Beat in thoroughly, and set to rise again for about a quarter of an hour.
Then beat lightly and pour into a pitcher.
Prepare the waffle irons as indicated above, and proceed to bake in the same manner.

name: Roast Chicken (Japanese Style)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Clean and singe the chicken.
Put the feet to boil until the scabs scale off, then place with the giblets to boil slowly.
Make a stuffing of rice boiled dry in chicken gravy, add chopped onion and a pinch of mixed spices, salt, pepper, and a dash of cayenne.
Put this in body of chicken and sew up.
Roast for an hour, or longer, according to age of chicken.
Make a gravy from the stock of the giblets.
Chop the giblets up fine and add to the gravy.
Serve with roasted sweet potatoes.

name: Roast Goose
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Put the goose in hot, not boiling, water for 2 minutes and then add the spicery powder, sauce, oil, and the salt. Leave the goose in for 20 minutes. Be sure every bit of goose is dipped into it.

Place the goose as shown in cut on page 50. Start the fire before this, so that the wall is hot. Let the goose roast for 1 hour. A hot fire is necessary before the goose is put in. Afterward have a low fire. There must be no smoke.

name: Roast Goose with Brussels Sprouts
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Pick, draw, singe, truss, and stuff the goose
Roast it before a clear fire
When done, cut a slice into the breast and let the gravy run out for a moment
Add to the gravy a tea-spoonful of salt, a salt-spoonful of Nepaul pepper, a tea-spoonful of mixed mustard, and a glass of portwine
Stir these ingredients into the gravy
Baste the bird well with it and continue with the carving
Serve with either apple or tomato sauce in a boat
Serve with potatoes and Brussels-sprouts if in season

name: Round Plum Pickle
author: Source author unknown
steps: Get the perfectly ripe fruit
Put them into a damp cloth, and roll them about to free them of dust
Sprinkle them well with salt
Stand them in the sun for three or four days
Drain away all the water
Bottle the plums alternately with cloves of garlic, green or fresh red chilies, sliced ginger, peppercorns, and ground mustard-seed
Add a little salt
Fill up the bottles with vinegar, and cork
Expose them to the sun for fifteen to twenty days

name: Sakura (Cherry Custard)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Beat up lightly and frothily six fresh eggs
Add one cupful of milk, sugar, and three tablespoonfuls of cherry sirup
Throw a handful of ripe, plump red cherries into the baking pan, and over this pour the above mixture
Bake for about half an hour in a medium oven
Remove, and at intervals over top of dish set more cherries

name: Salada de Batatas (Potato Salad)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cook a portion of small potatoes, peel them and cut them into thin slices
Mix with two onions cut into slices, salt, ground pepper, sweet oil and vinegar
Mix everything well
Serve with roasts

name: Salmon Loaf
author: Source author unknown
steps: Drain off the liquor for the sauce, pick out the bones, mash salmon fine with a spoon, add the eggs well beaten, melted butter, grated bread crumbs, and salt and mix well.
Steam three-quarters of an hour either in a mould or a bag.
Add to the liquor from salmon milk, flour, egg, a little salt, and boil until it thickens.
Slice the loaf, pour the sauce over slices, and garnish with bits of parsley and slices of lemon.

name: Salsa Española (Spanish Sauce)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: Substance of small game and fowl
Two or three tablespoons of oil
steps: Boil and skim the foam from a quantity of broth
Add the substance of small game and fowl and broth
Remove the grease and pass through a sieve

Alternatively, use equal parts substance and broth, one glass of white wine, a bunch of parsley, one small onion, one bay leaf, one head of garlic, two cloves, two or three tablespoons of oil, a bunch of cilantro, and one onion sliced into rings
Boil everything together for two hours
Remove the grease
Add salt and pepper

name: Salsify Oysters
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Scrape and boil the salsify
Beat fine in a mortar
Season with salt and red pepper
Mix them in a batter of eggs and a very little flour
Drop the size of an oyster and fry a light brown

name: Santol Jelly
author: Source author unknown
steps: Wash the fruit thoroughly. Cut up without paring into eighths, taking out the seeds.
Barely cover the fruit with water and boil until the fruit is soft.
Squeeze the fruit through a cloth.
Take equal parts of juice and sugar. When measured, put the juice on the stove to come to a boil and put the sugar in the oven to heat through, being careful not to scorch it.
When both are hot, put in the sugar.
Barely cover the seeds and boil, but be careful as the pulp burns to the bottom readily.
Squeeze through a cloth and treat the seed juice in the same way as the fruit juice.
Do not cook after it jellies.

name: Sardela Salatassi
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Put as many sardines as are wanted in a basin, with some vinegar, and let them remain in it for half an hour
Scrape off the scales gently and wash them in fresh vinegar
Arrange them round the edge of a dish
Put in the centre two or three handfuls of chopped parsley, two or three tablespoonfuls of chopped onions, and one or two dozens of olives, all mixed together
Put half a teaspoonful of salt in a basin, with two or three tablespoonfuls of the best wine vinegar, or the juice of two lemons, and about half a teacup of the best olive oil
Beat up well with a wooden fork or spoon until it becomes like cream
Pour it over the sardines and the parsley, and serve

name: Sardela Salatası
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Put as many sardines as are wanted in a basin with some vinegar and let them remain in it for half an hour
Scrape off the scales gently and wash them in fresh vinegar
Arrange them round the edge of a dish
Put in the centre two or three handfuls of chopped parsley, two or three tablespoonfuls of chopped onions, and one or two dozens of olives, all mixed together
Put half a teaspoonful of salt in a basin with two or three tablespoonfuls of the best wine vinegar or the juice of two lemons and about half a teacup of the best olive oil
Beat up well with a wooden fork or spoon until it becomes like cream
Pour it over the sardines and the parsley and serve

name: Satsuma Soup
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one quarter pound of dried mushrooms
one quarter pound of aburage (oil-fried Tofu)
one quarter pound of miso paste (soy bean and rice cheese)
one half teaspoonful of mixed red-pepper spices
steps: To prepare the chicken, separate the meat from the bones; then put bones in cold water and boil slowly for about two hours.
Strain, and add the well-chopped vegetables. (The mushrooms should have been washed, and soaked in lukewarm water for ten minutes previously.)
Boil for one more hour, then add the chicken meat, cut in very small pieces, salt, spices, and half a teaspoonful of sugar.
Cook all slowly for one hour.

name: Satsuma Tamana (Cabbage, Satsuma Style)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Wash and shred fine a hard, crisp cabbage.
In deep pan put goma-seed or olive oil.
Add the cabbage, with half a dozen stoned prunes and the juice of a lemon, pepper, and salt.
Let this slowly stew in its own juices for an hour or so.

name: Sauce for Alderman's Mock Turtle Pie
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: the pulp of sixteen or twenty prunes
steps: Mix with some of the stock the contents of a canister of oysters well bruised, the pulp of sixteen or twenty prunes, a blade of mace, some nutmeg and cloves, a wineglassful of port wine, and a tablespoonful of Worcestershire sauce.
Allow to simmer for ten minutes, and add it to the ready-baked pie before it is put on the table.

name: Sauce for Victoria Pudding
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Mix flour with half an ounce of butter
Add a cupful of boiling water
Stir in jam, lime juice, and brandy
Simmer for five minutes
Mix with a little pat of butter
Strain and pour over and round the pudding

name: Sauer Kraut
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
ingredientsText: seven or eight pounds of beef, either brisket or a fillet off the shoulder
steps: Boil about seven or eight pounds of beef either brisket or a fillet off the shoulder in enough water to cover it
When it has boiled for one hour, add as much sauer kraut as may be approved
Let it stew gently for four hours
Serve in a deep dish
Remove the fat for a more delicate dish

name: Scalloped Onions
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take onions, slice and boil until tender.
Cover bottom of buttered baking dish with onions.
Add layer of bread crumbs with bits of butter, pepper and salt.
Add more onions and more bread crumbs until dish is almost full.
Add milk and cream until full.
Bake twenty minutes or half an hour.

name: Scalloped Potatoes, No. 2
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Cut cold potatoes into cubes
Mix well with cream sauce, adding more seasoning if necessary
Pour into a baking dish
Cover with bread crumbs
Dot with small pieces of butter
Bake for about half an hour

name: Scorched Fish
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
steps: Remove the scales from fishes, wash and scorch them equally on both sides till they are soft.
Remove the black crusts and the bones.
Mix them with chopped onions, green chillies, mustard oil and salt.
Serve.

name: Sdghtin-Bureghi
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Put in a saucepan five or six chopped onions, a little salt, and some water, set it on the fire, and boil it for a few minutes
Drain the onions, and put them in a fryingpan with some fresh butter
Set the pan on the fire, and stew the onions until the moisture is dispersed
Beat up three or four eggs, and add it by degrees to the onions
Put it on the fire again, and stir it for three minutes or so with a wooden spoon
Take it off, and lay it between pieces of paste as No. 86, and bake it a nice colour
Dish up and serve

name: Seaweed Soup
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one and one half teaspoonfuls of Quong Sang Chong (water chestnut flour)
steps: Boil one can of seaweed until it is like thin jelly
Have ready three chicken giblets, chopped very fine, having first boiled them one hour in a quart of water
Add the seaweed, and boil all together for half an hour
Strain, then crumble in the yolks of two hard-boiled eggs
Stir in two tablespoonfuls of syou, and salt to taste
Rub smooth one and a half teaspoonfuls of Quong Sang Chong in a little cold water, then add to the soup and stir until it thickens slightly
Serve with a small piece of seaweed on top that has been soaking in spiced vinegar

name: Seer With Mushrooms
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: a good deep cut of seer fish
a pint of thin brown gravy
a tablespoonful of chablis or sauterne
a teaspoonful of red currant jelly
steps: Choose a good deep cut of seer fish
Take about a pint of thin brown gravy, a little onion, a carrot cut up, a bit of celery, and some parsley
Flavour it with a tablespoonful of chablis or sauterne, and one of mushroom ketchup, a teaspoonful of red currant jelly, and a little lime juice
Stew the fish in this liquor very gently
When done, strain it, thicken the gravy with butter and flour, adding a dozen black Leicestershire mushrooms
Heat up without boiling, and serve

name: Shariys Chorbassi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: three or four pints of broth
hearts and livers of several chickens, half cooked
five or six ounces of mixed vermicelli
steps: Put three or four pints of broth in a stewpan with the hearts and the livers of several chickens, half cooked and cut into small dice, and a little salt
Put it on the fire
When boiling, add five or six ounces of mixed vermicelli, and let it boil till tender
Remove the pan, and pour the contents in a tureen
Sprinkle a little white pepper and cinnamon over, and serve

name: Shark Fins
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: a few pieces of dry garlic
steps: Buy 2 pounds of dry shark fins from a Chinese grocery store. Soak in cold water for 3 hours.
Boil the fins with a few pieces of dry garlic and 2 pieces of ginger root. Change the water several times when boiling.
Put into a suitable pan. Add 2 tablespoonfuls of lard, and twice more than enough primary soup to cover. Boil slowly for 3/4 hour. Drain off the liquid and throw it away.
Put into another pan, containing 6 pints of primary soup, and boil.

Change again into a third pan of primary soup. Add gravy which consists of 1 cup of chicken starch, the whites of 3 eggs, Chinese ham dice and a little cornstarch and salt. Use 1 tablespoonful red vinegar to improve the taste. Garnish with parsley and serve hot.

name: Shavings (Kraus-Gebackenes)
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Sift about one pint of flour in a bowl
Make a depression in the centre
Break in five eggs, a pinch of salt, one teaspoon of ground cinnamon and one tablespoon of pulverized sugar
Mix this as you would a noodle dough, though not quite as stiff
Roll out very thin
Cut into long strips with a jagging iron
Fry a light yellow
Roll on a round stick as soon as taken up from the fat or butter
Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon or grated peel of a lemon
Mix both thoroughly

name: Shika Shiro (Pot-roasted Venison)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one quarter pound of fresh pork (fat)
one quarter pound of miso paste
steps: Place the meat in an earthenware bowl and cover with one cup of vinegar, two tablespoonfuls of sugar and the same amount of salt, one tablespoonful of mixed spices, and one onion, sliced.
Cover, and put away to pickle for two or three days in a cool place.
When ready to cook, remove meat from the juices, cut up the pork in small strips, and fry a light brown in deep iron pan.
Add the venison meat, and fry well on both sides until brown, taking care not to burn it.
Add the syou sauce, cover tight, and let simmer for one hour, or two, if necessary.
Mix the miso paste with a little cold water, and stir it until it thickens.
Remove the platter, and garnish with slices of lemon sprinkled with chopped parsley.

name: Shin of Beef Soup
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a tablespoonful of Lea & Perrin's Worcestershire sauce
steps: Take a shin of beef, cut it up small, wash it thoroughly, and boil with pepper and salt in sufficient water to well cover the meat
Let it boil over a brisk fire, taking away the black scum
Add a little cold water, and skim off the white scum
Reduce the fire, and allow the soup to simmer until it somewhat thickens
Strain the soup, cut away all the fat, season with soup herbs, and add more pepper and salt if necessary
Give it a good boil up, and then clear it with the white of an egg well beaten up
After which add a tablespoonful of Lea & Perrin's Worcestershire sauce, and half a wineglassful of sherry

name: Shrimp Chop Suey
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: 9 pounds shrimp with the shells off
1 piece of onion cut into threads
steps: Fry mushrooms, bean sprouts, and onion in an oily pan for 10 minutes. Add enough water to cover. Boil for 15 minutes.
Fry the shrimp in a hot, oiled pan and add the Fun Wine. Keep frying until the shrimp turns red.
Mix the shrimp with the mushrooms, bean sprouts, and onion, and add 2 cups of primary soup. When it boils, add Chinese gravy.

name: Shrimp Sauce
author: Source author unknown
steps: Pick some shrimps nicely from the shell
Put them into melted butter, and add a tablespoonful of lemon pickle and vinegar
Heat it

name: Shrimps with Gourd Leaves
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
ingredientsText: chopped and thoroughly washed tender gourd leaves
steps: Prepare some lobsters, cut in pieces and fry.
Fishes are always to be smeared with powdered turmeric and salt before frying.
Then brown some potatoes and onions peeled and cut in pieces.
Add water, salt, powdered turmeric, cumin, pepper, chillies, coriander and some chopped and thoroughly washed tender gourd leaves.
When fully boiled season the curry with ghee or oil boiled with a few cassia leaves and panch-foron.
Garam-masalla may be added.
Leave little soup.

name: Soft Immortal Food
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Cut each piece of bean cake into 4 pieces.
Soak the mushrooms, vermicelli, and bean sticks in water for 1½ hour. Cut the vermicelli into pieces 3 inches long.
Put all of the ingredients in cold water and cook for 1 hour. Put in plenty of oil and red cheese.
Add Chinese gravy.

name: Sopa a la Habanera (Havana-style Soup)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Prepare the bread by first making it into long, thin strips
After toasting them, place them in a cooking pot, arranging them in layers, mixing between them chopped garlic, parsley, and grated cheese
Crush some toasted almonds or hazelnuts and add broth from the pot
Bring to a boil and add some cloves, or if preferred, cinnamon
Once cooked, place half in the soup

name: Sopa de Leite (Milk Soup)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil milk with a little salt and sugar
When serving, add four beaten egg yolks and keep on the fire, stirring constantly until nearly boiling
Pour the soup into a tureen over bread slices and serve

name: Sopa de Peixe à Caiapó (Fish Soup Caiapó-style)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil beef with plenty of roots, parsley, carrots, celery, small potatoes and some apples cut in pieces
When almost cooked, add fish portions and let them cook more
Strain through a sieve and thicken the broth with wheat flour boiled in vinegar

name: Sopa de Tomates (Tomato Soup)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil tomatoes in water and salt until they fall apart
Pour this broth into a pan in which an onion has been fried
Chop some hardtack or biscuits and add to the pan

name: Sopa Dourada da Boa-Vista (Golden Boa-Vista Soup)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cut bread into slices
Soak them in milk for five to ten minutes
Remove and pass each slice through a mixture of four beaten eggs and four spoonfuls of sugar
Fry the coated slices on both sides in butter
Serve covered with sugar and ground cinnamon

name: Sopa Polaca (Polish Soup)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one hen, one duck or one mallard
half a pound of chopped lard, already fried
steps: Cut the hen, duck or mallard into small pieces and sauté in half a pound of chopped lard already fried
Add a little water, salt and necessary seasonings, and continue sautéing for more time
When cooked, let cool to remove the bones
Chop the meat into even finer pieces and add four hard-boiled eggs, making a kind of filling
On the other hand, make a dough of wheat flour and eggs, which should be stretched until very thin

Cut it into strips, and placing at intervals small pieces of chopped meat, cover them with the other strips of dough, pressing down the places where there is no meat, thus forming small pastries that are separated so they can retain the meat they contain
Boil them one after another in pure beef broth
Serve mixed with the broth

name: Sorubim Frito (Fried Sorubim)
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: postas of sorubim the thickness of a finger
steps: Take some steaks of sorubim the thickness of a finger
Sprinkle on both sides with salt, pepper and mustard
Fry in fat, and once fried, place on a plate, pouring over each steak a slice of peeled lemon, and squeezing a little lemon juice
Put a little hot fat and serve

name: Souffle of Raspberries
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Rub through a sieve a pint of raspberries
Grate the rind of a lemon and the juice of 1/2 a lemon
Add 1 lb. of powdered sugar
Let it simmer till it thickens a little
Turn it out to get cold
Beat up the yolks of 8 eggs
Grate 3 stale sponge cakes
Beat the eggs and cakes together
Add the snow of 3 eggs slowly
Mix in 2 oz. of melted veal fat
Grease a mould and sift sugar over
Bake in a slow oven
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Spiced Cucumbers
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Take nice firm cucumbers, slice thin and salt overnight
In the morning take vinegar sufficient for covering the quantity prepared, mixed spices and sugar according to taste
Put on to cook and when boiling put in the cucumbers and cook for thirty minutes
Put in airtight jars

name: Spiced Molasses Cake
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: 1/4 Teaspoonful Each of Cloves, Allspice and Cinnamon (ground)
steps: Warm the molasses and dilute with the vinegar.
Beat the butter and the sugar to a cream, and then add the eggs, whites and yolks, well-beaten together.
Then add gradually one-half of the flour and the molasses.
Add the grated spices and salt.
Beat well.
Add the soda, dissolved in two tablespoonfuls of boiling water, and beat well.
Bake in a moderate oven from thirty to forty-five minutes.

name: Sponge Cake
author: Source author unknown
steps: Beat eggs very light, add sugar and beat.
Add water, and flour with baking powder sifted into it.

name: Steak Stewed with Tomatoes
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Cut 3 or 4 good sized tomatoes and put them in a stewpan with an onion
Add salt and pepper
Put in the steak
As soon as it is tender take out the steak
Rub the tomatoes and onion through a sieve
Put back the steak in the saucepan and throw over the sauce
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Steamed Chestnut Pork
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: 3 3/8 pounds pork cut into pieces 1 inch by 3/8 inch by 1 3/8 inches
steps: Dip the pork into sweet sauce and fry in boiling oil until red.
Take out the pork and place in cold water. Change water until no oil is on top of the water.
Dry fried pork and place in a bowl.
Add the chestnuts and the Fun Wine. Steam for 1 3/8 hours.

name: Steamed Duck
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Soak the chestnuts and barley in cold water for 1 hour.
Open the back of the duck with one cut about 4 inches long. Take out the bones without tearing the meat.
When the duck has been cleaned wash it inside and out with Chinese sauce. Salt thoroughly and put into a hot, oiled pan and fry for 10 minutes.
Add the Fun Wine. Turn the duck frequently.
Now put the duck, with the open side upward, in a bowl a little larger than the duck. Fill with the chestnuts, barley, and white nuts and any juice left in the frying-pan.
Steam for 2½ hours.
Pour off the gravy into another bowl. Skim off the oil.
Transfer the duck carefully into a larger bowl by holding the bowls mouth to mouth.
Pour the gravy over the duck and serve.

name: Steamed Lamb
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: 2 pounds of lamb cut into pieces 3/8 inch by 1 3/8 inches by 3/8 inch
salt and sweet sauce (Chinese name Chew Tout)
steps: Use water to boil the lamb for 10 minutes.
Take out the lamb and dip into a bowl of salt and sweet sauce (Chinese name Chew Tout).
Put all into a suitable bowl. Add enough primary soup to cover and add the chestnuts, red dates, and Fun Wine. Steam until tender.
Remove any oil from the liquid, and serve.

name: Steamed Pike
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Clean the fish but do not cut it. Rub with salt. Add 1 teaspoonful oil.
Cut the onion, mushrooms, ginger root, and pork into threads, 1½ inches long. Spread this on top of the fish and steam for 1¼ hour. Garnish with parsley.

name: Steamed Turtle
author: Shiu Wong Chan
steps: Put the live turtles into a cooking-pan of cold water. Bring to a boil slowly.
Remove the shell and interior. Wash. Cut the meat into pieces 1 inch by 1 inch by 1½ inches.
Have a hot fire. Put 2 tablespoonfuls of oil into a frying-pan. When the oil is very hot put in the meat, Fun Wine, and ginger root juice. Fry for 10 minutes. Turn constantly.
Cut the bamboo shoots into pieces ¾ inch by 1½ inches by 1/16 inch. Cut the pork into pieces ¾ inch by 1¼ inches by ¾ inch.
Add to the meat in the frying-pan, the mushrooms, chestnuts, bamboo shoots, pork and enough primary soup to cover. Bring to a boil.
Put all into a suitable bowl and steam for 1½ hours.
Skim off any oil which may be on the top. Salt to taste.

name: Stewed Fish
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one cup of good, boiling vinegar
pint or glass of Port Wine
steps: Clean the fish well and slice and pour over one cup of good, boiling vinegar.
Make a roux by putting one tablespoonful of lard into the stewpan, and when hot add gradually two tablespoonfuls of flour rubbed smoothly.
When quite brown, take the fish, which has been previously rubbed with salt and pepper, and place in the pot.
Let it simmer gently a few minutes, and then add a large chopped onion, parsley, one clove of garlic, one sprig of thyme, a bay leaf, two blades of mace and eight or ten allspice.
Let these brown and cover with water sufficient to prevent burning.
Put the fish on a slow fire to stew, and when half done, add a little Cayenne, and, if possible, add a pint or glass of Port Wine.
When done, place the fish in a dish, pour the gravy over it, and garnish with crotons, with alternate slices of lemon and prepared horseradish.

name: Stewed Onions
author: Source author unknown
steps: Cook as boiled onions; drain.
Add milk, butter, pepper and salt, flour stirred to a cream.
Let all boil up at once.
Serve.

name: Stewed Oysters On Toast
author: Lafcadio Hearn
ingredientsText: a piece of butter as large as a hen’s egg for two dozen oysters
steps: Take the oysters from their liquor, let it settle
Then strain and add some whole pepper, two blades of mace, and three cloves
Put over a moderate fire in a block-tin covered sauce-pan
Mix a little flour with a piece of butter, as large as a hen’s egg for two dozen oysters
And stir in the boiling liquor
Remove any scum which may rise
Then put in the oysters and let them cook for five minutes
Line a hot oyster dish with toasted, well-buttered bread
And pour over it the boiling oysters
Only rich juicy oysters will stew to advantage
Milk is always an improvement, but in this recipe it can be dispensed with
If, however, it is convenient pour in a half a pint just as the oysters are put in to boil
As earlier it might curdle

name: Stewed Squash
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Peel squash and cut in quarters
put on to boil in cold water and cook until tender
Drain and mash fine and smooth
add one-half cup of milk or cream, one tablespoon of butter, pinch of salt and pepper
put back on stove to keep hot
Beat well with a spoon to make light and smooth

name: Strawberries A La Bridge
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Into a champagne-glass put large strawberries, halved and sugared, and an equal amount of marshmallows halved.
Place on top a mass of whipped cream, already sweetened and flavored.
Top with a single strawberry, sprinkle with shelled pecans.

name: Stuffed Bananas
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Bake long, plump bananas for ten minutes in medium oven.
Remove and split skin down one side.
Remove the inside, and whip it up with shredded coconut, a little cream and sugar, and a little lemon juice.
Return to shell, and bake for another ten minutes.

name: Stuffed Chicken (Turkish Style)
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Steam chicken and when it is almost tender stuff it with the following: Take one-fourth pound of almonds, chopped; season with parsley, pepper and salt to taste, add one tablespoon of bread crumbs and bind this with one well-beaten egg.
Put chicken in roasting-pan and roast until done.

name: Stuffed Pig's Feet a la Perigueux
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil the Pig's Feet, and then split them in two.
Take out the bones, lay the flesh on a dry, clean cloth and wipe well.
Make a forcemeat of boned turkey.
Add the truffles, which have been finely minced, and a half glass of Madeira or Sherry wine.
Mix this well together.
Take six pieces of crepinette, cut them the size of a man's hand and lay on a clean biscuit board.
Place on each piece of skin a portion of the forcemeat about the size of a hen's egg and flatten out well.
Place one-half of a pig's foot on top of this farcie, and cover with another layer of the stuffing.
On either side lay three thin slices of truffles.
Wrap the crepinettes up in some fanciful shape, such as an envelope or card case.
Dip them separately in a well-beaten egg, and then in grated bread-crumbs.
Put two tablespoonfuls of butter in a saucepan or deep frying pan, cover closely.
Let the feet cook on a slow fire for twenty-five minutes, allowing twelve minutes and a half to each side.
Serve with a pint of hot Perigueux sauce.
Place the sauce in a dish, lay the feet neatly over it and send to the table hot.

name: Suet Pudding
author: Source author unknown
steps: Mix ingredients
Steam three hours

name: Sukta
author: E.P. Veerasawmy
ingredientsText: Varieties of vegetables, as jhinga, potato, patol, brinjal, radish, beans, figs, green bananas, bori (dried cakes of pasted pulse)
Kernel of a ripe cocoa-nut scratched out
Tender jute leaves and neem leaves, uch-chhe, karala, palta
steps: Brown the boris in oil first and keep them aside
Fry the bitter vegetables in sufficient oil and add the other pieces of peeled vegetables
When everything is properly browned by constant stirring, add water with very little powdered turmeric and pasted ginger, and sufficient quantities of salt, powdered mustard, pepper and cumin
Add the browned boris when the mass is boiled
Season it with some ghee heated with a few mustard seeds
Add a little milk or sugar if desired
Take down with a quantity of soup
Add a little thin solution of flour if the soup is too thin

name: Suspiros de Yemas de Huevos (Sighs of Egg Yolks)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Mix egg yolks with ground and sifted sugar, stirring so that small figures or cakes can be made by hand
Let rest six to eight hours
After this time put in a moderate oven where they will cook and burst very quickly
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Sussiiz Pilaw
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: two pounds of mutton or lamb
two pounds and a half of rice
half a pound of hot fresh butter
half a dozen pieces of gum-mastic
two or three pieces of cinnamon
steps: Cut two pounds of mutton or lamb into pieces the size of walnuts, wash them, sprinkle them with sufficient salt and pepper, and lay them on the bottom of a stewpan with a tight-fitting cover.
Well wash two pounds and a half of rice, and place it over the meat.

Pour half a pound of hot fresh butter over, add half a dozen pieces of gum-mastic, two or three pieces of cinnamon, put the cover over the pan contrariwise, wrap a wet cloth round it, and fill the cover with water.
Set the pan on a slow charcoal fire, and let it simmer for about four hours.
Take off the cover, and turn the contents carefully on to a hot dish, and serve.

name: Sussuz Kyufte
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: a quarter of a pound of fresh butter
steps: Mince very fine as much as is required of the best part of raw mutton
Sprinkle a little salt, pepper, and cinnamon over
Knead well with a little onion juice, and make it into balls the size of walnuts
Put in a bowl or basin a teacup of water, and a quarter of a pound of fresh butter
Arrange the balls of meat in the bowl, and place it into an iron pot
Put the cover over and paste it round, or wrap a wet cloth round it, so as to prevent the steam from escaping
Set it on a moderate fire, and let it simmer for about two hours
Dish it up tastefully, and serve hot

name: Sweet and Pungent Chicken
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: Three and one half pound chicken
steps: Take a young chicken of about three and one half pounds.
Clean and singe it, and remove all the bones.
Lay in a stone dish and over it pour (enough to cover well) a mixture of two cupfuls of boiling vinegar, a dessert-spoonful of salt, and two tablespoonfuls of sugar.
Cover, and put away in a cool place for twenty-four hours.
Prepare a brown gravy by chopping half an onion and frying it a light brown in sweet lard or chicken fat.
Cut the chicken into quarters, and put in a pan with two tablespoonfuls of syou.
Simmer for half an hour very gently.
Serve with rice.

name: Tajadas de Carnero a la Inglesa (Slices of Mutton English Style)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Cut all the meat as described
Dust with flour
Moisten with broth and heat without boiling
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Tamago Tofu
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Break any required number of eggs and beat with chopsticks
Mix with twice the amount of cooking juice and one third of syou sauce
Pour the mixture into a thin china bowl or a tin mold, and steam over boiling water for thirty or forty minutes
Transfer a soupladleful to each individual bowl, and over each pour a small quantity of cooking juice and a few drops of syou sauce
Sprinkle with ground horseradish, and serve very hot

name: Tapioca Custard
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil tapioca twenty minutes with two cups of water
Beat the eggs with the milk which has been dissolved in half cup of water, and add to the boiling tapioca
Cook together a few minutes until thick and smooth
Add flavoring when done

name: Tea
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: Rinse the pot with boiling water before putting in the tea
The water should just come to a boil—no more
Pour on the tea leaves
Let it stand for two or three minutes, but on no account must it be allowed to boil
Strain tea from leaves, and serve pure, if Chinese tea is used

name: Tea Rolls
author: Source author unknown
steps: Sift the flour and salt together.
Scald the milk, and when tepid add the yeast, dissolved in a little warm water, to one-half of the milk.
Add one-half of the flour, and make a thin batter, stirring very smooth.

Set it to rise in a warm place, and at the end of three hours make it into a dough with the remainder of the milk and flour, and knead well till the dough no longer adheres to the board or to your hands.
Then shape it with your hands into small balls, set to rise for a half hour longer, or an hour, and bake in a moderate oven for a half hour.

name: Tekir-Betlighi Pulalcissi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: juice of one or two lemons
yolks of two or three eggs
a quarter of a pint of olive oil
steps: Take out the gills and the insides of seven or eight red mullets, and wash them
Peel two or three onions, and well pound them in a mortar
Add a little mixed spice, salt, and pepper, the juice of one or two lemons, the yolks of two or three eggs, and a little water, and beat them up well together with a wooden spoon
Pour it over the mullets, and let them remain for about two hours
Put a quarter of a pint of olive oil in a flat stewpan, with a plate of chopped parsley
Put it on the fire, and just scald it
Add half a pint of water, half a teaspoonful of salt
When it boils, lay the mullets in with the ingredients, and let it simmer for fifteen or twenty minutes
Dish up tastefully, and serve hot

name: Tembani of Mackerel (Fish Delicacy)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one half cupful of cooking juice
steps: Clean the fish, and remove all bones.
Cut into half-inch dice, sprinkle with salt, and let stand for about half an hour.
Wash the radish and cut into thin pieces, then throw it into the salted, boiling water.
Boil for about five minutes, then strain off all water and add half a cupful of syou sauce and the same amount of cooking juice.
Let all boil up, then add the fish and let it simmer for about twenty-five minutes.
Remove from the fire, and before serving add a tablespoonful of vinegar.
Place on a hot platter, and sprinkle with grated lemon or orange peel.
Serve with boiled rice.

name: Ten Sune Gune (Sweet and Sour Fish)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one and one half cupfuls of water
one tablespoonful of Quong Sang Chong (water-chestnut flour)
two and one half tablespoonfuls of vinegar
one and one half tablespoonfuls of sugar
steps: Clean a sea bass of about two pounds and take out all the insides, taking care to keep the fish whole
Put it into a medium deep dish large enough to fit the fish
Pour over it water almost boiling, cover fish well over, put a lid on dish, and leave on range for one hour
Do not boil, but keep it hot
Rub smooth one tablespoonful of Quong Sang Chong
To a cup and a half of water add one tablespoonful of salt, one and one half tablespoonfuls of sugar, and two and one half tablespoonfuls of vinegar
Mix well and boil until it thickens, stirring constantly to prevent burning
Dish up the fish, place on another hot, dry dish, then pour over it the sauce, and serve with rice

name: Tendons of Veal
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
steps: Cut from the bones of a breast of veal the tendons which are round the front
Trim and blanch them
Put them with slices of smoked beef into a stewpan with some shavings of veal, a few herbs, a little sliced lemon, two or three onions, and a little broth
They must simmer for seven or eight hours
When done, thicken the gravy

name: Tenjere Kyulbassussi
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Cut as much as is wanted of rump steak or veal in slices the size of a hand, and about half an inch thick
Sprinkle a little salt and pepper over, place them on a gridiron, set it on a moderate charcoal fire, and frequently turn them
When nicely browned, place them in a stewpan with a few cloves of garlic peeled, and a half or a tea-cup of wine vinegar, a little cinnamon and cummin
Cover them with broth, put the pan with the cover over on a moderate charcoal fire, and let it simmer till tender
Serve hot

name: Terbiyeli Jigher Chbrbassi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: yolks of two or three eggs
juice of one or two lemons or wine vinegar
steps: Get a lamb's or sheep's lights and cut it into small dice
Put them in a stewpan with a little salt, and a small quantity of water
Put it on the fire until the lights are nearly cooked
Add three or four pints of broth, and let it simmer till the pieces of lights are quite done
Beat up the yolks of two or three eggs in a small saucepan, with the juice of one or two lemons, or with a little wine vinegar, and stir it on a slow fire with a wooden spoon till a little thick
Take it off and pour it gradually into the soup, stirring it quickly at the same time, to prevent the eggs from curdling
Pour the soup into a tureen, sprinkle a little cinnamon over, and serve

name: The Epicure's Sauce
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: the same quantity of white pepper
steps: Chop fine, one capsicum, two eschalots, and one or two bird's-eye chilies
add two tablespoonfuls of port wine, six tablespoonfuls of mushroom catsup, two of soy, and two of walnut catsup, half a teaspoonful of cayenne, and the same quantity of white pepper
put all into a bottle, which place in a warm place for two or three weeks
then strain, and add half a pint of vinegar

name: The Famous Bakewell Pudding
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
ingredientsText: An inch of nice preserve or jam
J lb. of well boiled potatoes
J ounce each of sweet and bitter almonds
steps: Lay a nice puff paste on plate, then an inch of nice preserve or jam
Mix, like pound cake, J lb. of butter, beaten to cream, J lb. of well boiled potatoes pressed through a sieve, J lb. of sugar, J ounce each of sweet and bitter almonds, both blanched and pounded
When beaten well together, add 5 eggs well frothed, 1 tablespoon of brandy
Pour over the layer of preserves and bake

name: The Pearl
author: Source author unknown
steps: Let the sugar boil a little longer

If you find that on drawing it out to a thread it snaps quickly, and also that while boiling the sugar presents the form of large pearls or globules on its surface, it will then have reached the small pearl degree
When the pearls become closely connected on the surface of the sugar, it will have reached the large pearl degree

name: Tippoo's Sauce
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a few pieces of lemon peel
half a teaspoonful of Cayenne pepper
steps: Put into a saucepan the juice of four lemons, a few pieces of lemon peel, a small quantity of salt, a little tamarind juice, and half a teaspoonful of Cayenne pepper
simmer this for a few minutes, and turn it into a basin
Strain through a fine strainer when cold, and then bottle it into small bottles, which should be well corked, and kept in a place free from

name: To Batter Oysters
author: Christian Woman's Exchange
steps: Make a light batter of 8 eggs, a dessertspoonful of butter, a little wheat flour, pepper and salt to the taste
Drain the oysters from the liquor
Stir them into the batter
Drop the mixture from a ladle into boiling lard
Let the fritters cook until they are of a rich brown

name: To Boil Rice
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one and one quarter cupfuls of cold water
steps: Wash the rice thoroughly in many waters, until the water is as clear as for drinking
To one cupful of rice add one and one quarter cupfuls of cold water
Cover tight, and boil slowly half an hour—no more
On no account stir
Set on back of range, covered with a clean cloth or napkin, until ready to serve
Rice should be served in individual bowls, replenished as soon as empty throughout the meal
Salt is not added until it is served

name: To Boil Rice for Currie
author: Source author unknown
steps: Wash the rice in several waters, then leave it in a basin of cold water to soak for two or three hours
Have ready a saucepan full of water, with a little salt in it
When the water boils, drain the rice and put it into the saucepan
Let it boil very quickly for about seven minutes, then pour it into a colander, and place the colander on the top of the saucepan, that the water may quite drain off
The rice ought to be stirred with a fork that the grains may be separated
It ought to be boiled in a large quantity of water, and it will be sufficiently cooked when the grains become a little soft, and over done if they at all stick together
Rice should always be served in a separate dish from the currie

name: To Roast a Turkey
author: Estella Atrutel
steps: Put it in water and salt it
Let all the water drain out of the inside
Dry the outside well with a clean cloth
Prepare the stuffing and put it in at the breast
Plump it nicely and sew the skin with a needle and thread
Do not fill it too much or the skin might burst
Rub it well outside with mixed pepper and salt
Flour it lightly
Lay it in a dry dish and leave it for one hour before roasting
Put a sheet of white paper well greased over the breast to prevent it being scorched
Remove it an hour before sending it up
Dredge it lightly with flour
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: To Stew Cold Poultry with Vegetables
author: Estella Atrutel
ingredientsText: Remnants of cold fowl or duck
a good size cup of gravy
a couple of spoonfuls of sugar
turnips, Jerusalem artichokes, or small new potatoes
steps: Fry an onion sliced in a little dripping, pour in a good size cup of gravy, made from odd pieces.
Wash and drain well 1/2 peck of peas, put them with a couple of spoonfuls of sugar, pepper, salt.
When nearly done lay in the pieces of fowl or duck.
When done dish up, poultry in the centre of the dish, and vegetables round.
They are very nice done with turnips, Jerusalem artichokes, or small new potatoes, for all these vegetables colour with saffron, and dish up very hot.
sourceTitle: An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery

name: Tomato and Cheese Salad
author: Source author unknown
steps: Peel the tomatoes after scalding them and slice thickly.
Wipe each slice dry and cover with a layer of cream cheese mixed with chopped red pepper and garnished with small rounds of the pepper.
Serve with French dressing.

name: Tomato Chutney
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: a quarter their bulk of white onion
steps: Remove the seeds and watery juice from two or three ripe tomatoes, chop them up with a quarter their bulk of white onion, and season the mince with a little salt.
Add a pinch of salt, two green chillies chopped small, and a little bit of celery also chopped.
Give the whole a dust of black pepper, and moisten it with a tea-spoonful of vinegar.

name: Tomato Omelet
author: Source author unknown
steps: Beat eggs without separating until well mixed.
Add tomato, salt and cayenne.
Put butter into omelet pan; when hot add egg mixture; shake until set; fold and turn the omelet out on a platter.

name: Tomatoes - French Fashion
author: Source author unknown
steps: Scald and peel small solid tomatoes.
To each six, allow cream sauce made by rubbing together butter and flour.
Add milk, stir until boiling, season with salt and pepper.
Put a tablespoon of sauce in the bottom of a custard cup; put in a tomato and cover with another tablespoon sauce; dust top with bread crumbs.
Stand the cups in a pan of boiling water and bake in moderate oven for half an hour.
Serve in the cups.

name: Top-Marul Salatassi
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Procure two or three cabbage-lettuces
Remove the outer leaves and throw them away
Pull the others one by one
Wash and well drain them in a cloth
Put them in the bowl, with a few slices of beet-root, one or two hard-boiled eggs cut in quarters
Add two teaspoonfuls of chopped chervil, one of tarragon, and one of chives or young onions
Sprinkle over with your fingers half a teaspoonful of salt, one or two pinches of pepper
Add two or three tablespoonfuls of the best olive oil, and one and-a-half of wine vinegar, or the juice of a lemon
Turn the salad in the bowl with a spoon and fork until well mixed, and serve

name: Tori Shiru (Chicken Soup)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one half pound of egg noodles
one quarter pound of white mushrooms
steps: Thoroughly clean and singe the chicken, and scald feet to peel off scabs or skin.
Cut giblets in small pieces and the chicken in about six pieces, and cover with three quarts of cold water.
Boil all for about three hours, according to the age of the chicken.
While it is boiling wash and cut up the vegetables.
Now make the egg noodles of flour and eggs and roll as thin as paper on a floured board, then cut in shapes of flowers (chrysanthemums, the Japanese prefer), and leave spread out on the board to dry.
Drain all soup from the bones and bring to a boil.
Add vegetables, salt, pepper, and one teaspoonful of sugar; also the syou sauce.
Boil all for half an hour, then throw in the noodles and cook for ten minutes.
Serve each bowl of soup with one large noodle flower on top.

name: Torta de Almendra Sobre Masa de Hojuelas (Almond Cake on Puff Pastry)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Weigh one pound of almonds and grind them so they remain grainy
Soak in orange blossom water
Mix with eleven well-beaten egg whites
Add one pound of ground sugar and mix well
Prepare and beat a small amount of puff pastry dough
Place one sheet of this dough in a casserole greased with butter
Pour the almond paste on top
Cover with another thin sheet of dough
Sprinkle with butter
Place the cake to cook between two fires
While cooking, add raisins, almonds, ground cinnamon, dragée, pine nuts, walnuts, and hazelnuts
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Torta de Arroz con Picadillo (Rice Cake with Minced Meat)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Wash and soak the rice in two or three waters
After drying, moisten with water and cook, either steamed wrapped in a napkin or in a little water, seasoned with corresponding salt
Once cooked, set aside, and the next day drain well and mix with a little salt, or without it if desired
Moisten with broth or mix with a small amount of saffron, cloves, and ground pepper dissolved in water
Beat egg whites well, and when they have thickened add the yolks
Add the rice moistened with broth or with the spices already mentioned
Grease a mold with lard and put in a layer of rice and another of minced meat, alternating layers until the mold is full, finishing by pouring the beaten egg mixture on top
When it has set on the bottom, place a comal with little heat on top so the cake sets on both sides
Once set, it can be dusted with a little sugar
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Torta de Pies de Puerco (Pork Feet Cake)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: molleja or liver, or small fish pieces
steps: When the pork feet are half-cooked, add a hen so that everything finishes cooking together.
Skim the broth and add salt, all spices, ground garlic, and chorizos.
Do this the day before the cake is to be eaten.
On the day it is to be served, make a picadillo with all its requisites, adding four to six beaten eggs stirred so they are set, and a little saffron.
To the broth in which the hen cooked, well seasoned with all spices, add a little vinegar.
Beat ten to twelve eggs separately, beating first the whites and then adding the yolks.
Put the picadillo in a pan over the fire, gradually adding sliced tongue, pieces of pork feet without bones, hen, chorizo, sliced hard-boiled eggs, raisins, almonds, olives, and capers.
Pour this over half the beaten egg in a pan with very hot lard so it sets, doing so carefully so the pieces of picadillo do not mix with the egg.
After adding the picadillo, cover it completely with the other half of the beaten egg.
When recognized with a knife that the cake is set, lower it to the ground by placing a comal on top so it cooks without lard.
When well browned, if the pan is not full, add more well-puffed beaten eggs and put the comal on top again.
If there is suspicion that the cake is not well cooked, put it back on gentle fire until it is.

For the sauce, fry from morning twelve ground tomatoes with garlic, chiles, and parsley, then adding a little broth, eight egg yolks, and the juice of two lemons, stirring quickly so the yolks break down.
Let it simmer for a while and add all spices and more well-washed capers, or in their place molleja or small liver pieces, or small fish pieces, mint, parsley, and saffron.
When bringing to the table, add olives and any other garnishes desired.
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Tortitas o Frutas de Sartén (Pan Fritters or Fruits of the Skillet)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
ingredientsText: Salt, the amount that fits in three fingers
Sufficient flour to make a dough like biscuit dough
steps: Mix one cup of water, one pound of sugar, one pound of lard, three egg yolks, salt, and sufficient flour to make a dough like biscuit dough
Form small round tortillas with it, place them on papers, and put them to cook in a very mild oven
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Tostadas en Canapé (Canapé Toasted Slices)
author: Mariano Galván Rivera
steps: Make a mixture of sweetbread or calf's thymus gland, rooster crests and artichoke bottoms, cut into dice shapes
Cut mushrooms in the same form, fry them and moisten with substance
Add the mixture and cook everything with beef marrow
Season, and then bind with egg yolks and a little sauce
Let cool
Coat with beaten eggs and fry
Serve with the same beef or veal marrow
sourceTitle: Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano

name: Tripas de Vacca à Mineira (Beef Tripe Miner Style)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Wash the tripe well in many waters
Place in a vessel with salt and orange juice and let sit until the next day
Remove and after washing once more in cold water, scald with hot water, leaving in this water until cooled
Place on the fire with cold water, salt, Indian pepper, parsley, and onion leaves
Let boil four to five hours
Add two or three eggs beaten in cold water
Let boil for another half hour
After adding slices of lemon, serve

name: Turkey Boned and Forced
author: Judith Cohen Montefiore (attr.)
steps: Have the turkey boned by the poulterer
Fill it with a fine forcemeat, which may be varied in several ways
The basis should be according to the receipt given for veal stuffings, forcemeats, sausage meat, tongue, and mushrooms added as approved
If boiled, serve with any fine white sauce, French cooks use the veloute or bechamel
If roasted, use a cradle spit if available, or carefully tie the turkey to the spit

name: Turtle Soup for a Large Company, No. 1
author: Lafcadio Hearn
ingredientsText: eight pounds of beef or veal
one pound of ham or bacon
pepper, salt, and sweet herbs to taste
the liquor of a boiled turtle
the flesh of the turtle, prepared as in recipe No. 1
a quarter of a pound of good sweet butter
steps: Cut the head off the turtle the day before you dress it, and drain the blood thoroughly from the body
Then cut it up in the following manner: Divide the back, belly, head and fins from the intestines and lean parts
Be careful not to cut the gall bag
Scald in boiling water to remove the skin and shell
Cut up in neat pieces and throw into cold water
Boil the back and belly in a little water long enough to extract the bones easily
If for a large company a leg of veal will also be required, and a slice of ham, which must be stewed with the lean parts till well browned
Then add boiling water, and the liquor and bones of the boiled turtle
Season with sliced lemon, whole pepper, a bunch of parsley, two leeks sliced, and salt to taste
Let this all boil slowly for four hours then strain
Add the pieces of back, belly, head and fins (take the bones from the fins)
Pour in half a pint of Madeira wine and a quarter of a pound of good sweet butter, with a tablespoonful of flour worked in it
Also, a lemon sliced thin
Let it boil gently for two hours, then serve

name: Tutti-Frutti Cake
author: Source author unknown
steps: Take one teacupful of sugar and one of butter and beat to a cream
Add a teacupful of milk and two and a half teaspoonfuls of flour sifted, with two heaping teaspoonfuls of baking powder
Add one pound of raisins, well-seeded, and one pound each of shredded figs and pounded almonds
After mixing all these well, add the whites of seven eggs, beaten to a stiff froth
Bake in a slow oven
When done, make a light syrup and spread over the top, and garnish with pieces of finely-cut preserved citron, oranges, preserved, currants and other candies

name: Tyre or Dhye
author: Source author unknown
steps: Warm some milk without boiling it
stir into it a little stale butter about the size of a large pea
put the vessel in a warm place well covered over, and in the course of eight or ten hours the tyre will be ready

name: Unboiled Icing
author: Florence Kreisler Greenbaum
steps: Take the white of one egg and add to it the same quantity of water
Stir into this as much confectioner's sugar to make it of the right consistency to spread upon the cake
Flavor with any flavoring desired
Color as desired by adding fruit coloring

name: Unohana Yaki (Flower Custard)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
steps: To make the pink custards, whip the whites of five eggs into the dissolved two ounces of gelatine.
Add, while stirring over a slow fire, three tablespoonfuls of cherry sirup.
Let it come to a boil, then pour quickly into flower-shaped molds, and let it set.
Yellow custards can be made by using the yolks instead of the whites of eggs, and half a pint of coconut milk.
When the custards are solid, turn them from the molds on to large leaves on a plate, or decorate the flowered custard with leaves suitable to the flower represented.
If the flower has a dark center, use goma seeds, and if variegated colors are liked, pour half the yellow and half the cherry custards into the molds.
The pouring should be done very quickly and lightly, and the molds, of course, should be of flower designs.

name: Usagi Amai-Sui (Hare, Sweet and Sour)
author: Sara Bosse & Onoto Watanna
ingredientsText: one half cupful of mirin sauce
one half pound of fat fresh pork
steps: Take a small hare or large rabbit that has been hanging for at least two days, and after it has been skinned, and the insides removed, wash well in cold water.
Cut in quarters and put in a deep dish, covering it well with the vinegar, sugar, salt, and so on, mixed with water.
Add the spices also, and a quarter of a cupful of mirin sauce.
Cover up well, and let it pickle in a cool place for two or three days.
Remove it from the liquid and cut in small pieces.
Have ready the fat pork cut in small pieces, and fry.
Toss in the hare, and brown.
Have ready a covered China cook dish or casserole, and place in it the hare and pork, adding the syou sauce, a pinch of salt, pinch of the spices, and the quarter cupful of mirin sauce.
Cover up tightly, and cook in a slow oven for one hour.
Then prepare a dozen large red plums, removing the stones, and add them.
Dissolve one teaspoonful of Kanton and mix with the gravy, taking care not to break the plums.
Cook for another five minutes, then place on a hot platter, decorated with slices of lemon or limes, with a plum placed on top of each slice.
This is good served either with white-bean cakes or rice.

name: Usscumru Balighindan Papas Yahnissi
author: Turabi Efendi
ingredientsText: half a teacup of wine vinegar
two or three teacups of water
a tablespoonful of preserved tomato sauce
steps: Take out the inside of half a dozen mackerel and wash them
Boil them in water for one or two minutes
When cold, remove the bones
Cut three or four onions in slices and fry them partly brown in olive oil
Lay the half on the bottom of a stewpan with a handful of picked parsley mixed with a little fennel
Pour in what oil is left in the frying-pan
Place the pieces of mackerel over
Put the other half of the onions with the same quantity of parsley and fennel on the top
Add half a teacup of wine vinegar and two or three teacups of the water in which the fish is boiled
Add sufficient salt and pepper
Put the pan on a moderate charcoal fire with the lid on and let it simmer gently for about fifteen or twenty minutes until the fish is nicely done
Dish it up, sprinkle a little cinnamon over, and serve

name: Usskumru Balighi Kebabi
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Cut off the point of the head of the mackerel
If large, divide each one in three pieces; if small, in two pieces
Wash and dry them in a cloth
Sprinkle them with sufficient salt and pepper, and a handful or two of chopped parsley mixed with fennel
Let them remain for an hour
Put them on skewers, with a bay-leaf between each piece
Cook them as above

name: Vegetable Consommé for Mulligatunny
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
steps: Throw carrots and onions into a stew-pan with butter, parsley, and celery
Fry until the vegetables begin to take colour
Moisten with two quarts of hot water
Boil and skim
Put into the pan half an ounce of salt, a quarter ounce of black peppercorns, and a pint measure of shelled green peas
Simmer for three hours
Skim off any oil that may rise from the butter
Strain the broth into a basin through a tamis

name: Vegetable Currie
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: one tablespoonful and a half of currie powder
a quarter of a pound of butter
steps: Peel and cut up in square pieces, four large potatoes, and fry them in butter until they are a light brown colour

Put them into a stewpan with a pint of brown gravy, one raw onion, and one previously fried, half a small vegetable marrow cut into pieces, a handful of green peas, the same of French beans, and a few slices of cucumber
Add one tablespoonful and a half of currie powder, a tablespoonful of vinegar, and salt to taste
Simmer very slowly, stirring carefully from time to time until the vegetables are nearly cooked
Then add a quarter of a pound of butter mixed with a teaspoonful of flour to thicken the gravy, and simmer again until the vegetables are sufficiently cooked but not broken
A small piece of mint is by some considered an improvement

name: Vegetable Mulligatawny
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: a quarter of a pound of butter
two or three small vegetable marrows
a tablespoonful and a half or two tablespoonfuls of currie powder
steps: Put a quarter of a pound of butter into a frying pan and slightly brown it
Pour it into a large saucepan

Add two or three small vegetable marrows cut up and freed from seeds, two large onions, three or four acid apples peeled and cored, two or three tomatos if in season, and a cucumber cut up, taking care not to put any of the seeds in
Stew these gently until tender
Add a tablespoonful and a half or two tablespoonfuls of currie powder, and salt to taste
Let this simmer about a quarter of an hour longer, adding sufficient good stock to cover it
Reduce it all to a pulp and press it through a sieve
Put the liquid into a fresh saucepan with as much fresh stock as will make it the required thinness
Add a squeeze of lemon juice if liked
Serve the soup as hot as possible

name: Vegetable Soup
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: Any kind of vegetables washed thoroughly and cut into pieces one inch long
steps: Heat the cooking pan for 1/2 minute
Then spread one teaspoonful of oil all over the surface of the pan and let it heat for from 1 to 2 minutes
Add the salt, then the vegetables and ginger
Turn over frequently until the volume of the vegetables is reduced to 1/2
Add the primary soup, and let it cook until it boils
Keep the soup boiling slowly until done; the length of time depends upon the kind of vegetables
It is best to keep the pan uncovered

name: Venison Steaks à la Poivrade
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: 6 Filets or as Many Filets as Desired
steps: Take the filets or Venison steaks from any part of the Venison. The best are from the haunch or leg, and cut three-quarters of an inch in thickness.
Rub them well with salt and pepper.
Fry in butter, allowing about five minutes to the steak.
Place in a heated dish, and garnish with melted butter and chopped parsley.
Serve with a Sauce Poivrade for Venison, pouring the sauce over the steaks.

name: Victoria Pudding
author: Wyvern (A.R. Kenney-Herbert)
ingredientsText: a quarter of a pound of bread-crumbs
a quarter of a pound of jam
steps: Mix bread-crumbs, shredded suet, jam, lime juice, grated lime peel, sifted sugar, eggs and salt thoroughly
Place it in a buttered mould, and boil for three hours
For the sauce, mix two tea-spoonfuls of flour with half an ounce of butter, and add a cupful of boiling water
Stir in a table-spoonful of the jam you use for your pudding, the juice of a lime and a spoonful of brandy
Simmer for a few minutes

name: Vishna Shier Ubi
author: Turabi Efendi
steps: Squeeze as many pounds of morella cherries as are wanted, and pass the juice through a cloth into a basin, and leave it for twenty-four hours
Strain it gently into another basin, and throw the residue away
Put the juice in a very clean stewpan, with double the quantity of sifted sugar
Stir till the sugar is dissolved, and set it to boil
As soon as it bubbles up take it off, and pass it through a sieve or cloth
When cold, bottle and cork it up until wanted

name: Vitella Assada de Creme (Roasted Veal with Cream)
author: Source author unknown
steps: Boil three garafas of milk with half pound of butter, salt, pepper, parsley, nutmeg, and a halved onion
Once it has boiled a little, add the moderately larded veal quarter
Bring to a boil again and let cool
Remove the quarter and place on a spit, cover with lemon slices and onions, and finally with buttered paper
Roast and serve with toasted potatoes, vegetables, and also with salad

name: Waffles
author: Source author unknown
ingredientsText: ¾ cup butter and lard mixed
steps: Beat egg whites and yolks separately
Melt butter and lard
Take milk, beaten egg yolks, melted butter and lard mixed, baking powder, and flour enough to make a batter as stiff as pancake batter
Add baking powder and the whites of eggs the last thing before cooking

name: Walnut Chicken
author: Shiu Wong Chan
ingredientsText: 2 cups water chestnuts cut into dice
steps: Remove the skins from the walnuts by placing them in boiling water. Then fry them in boiling oil until they turn yellow.

Put the secondary vegetables in a hot cooking-pan containing oil and fry for 2 or 3 minutes. Keep them moving so that each particle receives the same amount of heat. Add enough primary soup to cover and boil for 15 minutes.
Put the chicken in a hot, oiled pan and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the vegetables.
Add Chinese gravy and remove from the stove.
Place on a dish and garnish with the fried walnuts.

name: War Mein
author: Jessie Louise Nolton
ingredientsText: two pounds of any kind of meat
one pound peeled and sliced Chinese potatoes
steps: Cut meat into small square pieces
Soak Chinese mushrooms for two hours, remove the stems and cut in fine pieces
Cut Spanish onions fine
Put all in pan with enough Seasoning Sauce to cover bottom of pan about one inch deep
When boiling, cover tightly and set on back of stove to cook slowly about two hours
When nearly done, put in one pound peeled and sliced Chinese potatoes and let cook till done, about ten minutes
Add a little boiling water if needed, but not too much
Cook noodles in boiling water and drain in colander
Put meat mixture in large oval dish and cover over top with two cupfuls cooked noodles
Beat one egg very light, cook in flat pan spreading very thin, and let cool
Slice egg in thin, fine strips
Slice green onion tops and a piece of cooked ham about three inches long
Put egg strips over center of noodles with ham each side and green onion at ends of dish
sourceTitle: Chinese Cookery in the Home Kitchen

name: Watermelon Sherbet
author: Source author unknown
steps: Split a ripe watermelon in half.
Scoop out the center, rejecting the seeds.
Put the scooped fruit in a bowl.
Take a silver fork and pick it in small pieces.
Mix with a half pound of pulverized sugar.
Turn the mixture into a freezer and turn slowly for fifteen minutes.
Serve in glasses, adding a teaspoonful of Sherry to each glass.

name: Welsh Rarebit
author: Source author unknown
steps: Mix cheese with the yolks of eggs
add the grated bread and butter and seasoning
Toast slices of bread cut thin into shapes
spread the paste thick upon them and put in oven
Let them become hot and slightly browned
Serve hot

name: Wine Vapor Duck
author: Shiu Wong Chan
